sanskrit: प्रविश्य तु महारण्यं दण्डकारण्यमात्मवान्। ददर्श रामो दुर्धर्षस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्।।3.1.1।।
transliteration: praviśya tu mahāraṇyṃ daṇḍakāraṇyamātmavān| dadarśa rāmo durdharṣastāpasāśramamaṇḍalam||3.1.1||
meaning: The invincible and selfpossessed Rama entered the great forest of Dandaka and saw there a multitude of hermitages of the ascetics.

sanskrit: वाक्यमेतत्तु वैदेह्या व्याहृतं भर्तृभक्तया। श्रुत्वा धर्मे स्थितो रामः प्रत्युवाचाथ मैथिलीम्।।3.10.1।।
transliteration: vākyametattu vaidehyā vyāhṛtṃ bhartṛbhaktayā| śrutvā dharme sthito rāmḥ pratyuvācātha maithilīm||3.10.1||
meaning: Having heard these words spoken by Sita who was devoted to her husband, replied Rama who was firm in righteousness.

sanskrit: अग्रतः प्रययौ रामस्सीता मध्ये सुमध्यमा। पृष्ठतस्तु धनुष्पाणिर्लक्ष्मणोऽनुजगाम ह।।3.11.1।।
transliteration: agratḥ prayayau rāmassītā madhye sumadhyamā| pṛṣṭhatastu dhanuṣpāṇirlakṣmaṇo'nujagāma ha||3.11.1||
meaning: Rama walked in front, Sita with a beautiful waist, in the middle and Lakshmana holding the bow, behind them৷৷

sanskrit: सप्रविश्याऽश्रमपदं लक्ष्मणो राघवानुजः। अगस्त्यशिष्यमासाद्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।।3.12.1।।
transliteration: sapraviśyā'śramapadṃ lakṣmaṇo rāghavānujḥ| agastyaśiṣyamāsādya vākyametaduvāca ha||3.12.1||
meaning: Lakshmana, the younger brother of Rama, entered the hermitage of Agastya and met one of his disciples and said to him these words :

sanskrit: राम प्रीतोऽस्मि भद्रं ते परितुष्टोऽस्मि लक्ष्मण। अभिवादयितुं यन्मां प्राप्तौ स्थ स्सह सीतया।।3.13.1।।
transliteration: rāma prīto'smi bhadrṃ te parituṣṭo'smi lakṣmaṇa| abhivādayituṃ yanmāṃ prāptau stha ssaha sītayā||3.13.1||
meaning: O Rama ,I am pleased. I wish you well. I am glad that both of you have come here with Sita to pay respect to me.

sanskrit: अथ पञ्चवटीं गच्छन्नन्तरा रघुनन्दनः। आससाद महाकायं गृध्रं भीमपराक्रमम्।।3.14.1।।
transliteration: atha pañcavaṭīṃ gacchannantarā raghunandanḥ| āsasāda mahākāyṃ gṛdhrṃ bhīmaparākramam||3.14.1||
meaning: On the way to Panchavati, Rama, the delight of the Raghu race, met a vulture with a huge body and fearful strength.

sanskrit: ततः पञ्चवटीं गत्वा नानाव्यालमृगायुताम्। उवाच भ्रातरं रामस्सौमित्रिं दीप्ततेजसम्।।3.15.1।।
transliteration: tatḥ pañcavaṭīṃ gatvā nānāvyālamṛgāyutām| uvāca bhrātarṃ rāmassaumitriṃ dīptatejasam||3.15.1||
meaning: On reaching Panchavati, which was full of various vicious animals, Rama said to Lakshmana, his brother who was glowing like fire:

sanskrit: वसतस्तस्य तु सुखं राघवस्य महात्मनः। शरद्व्यपाये हेमन्तऋतुरिष्टः प्रवर्तत।।3.16.1।।
transliteration: vasatastasya tu sukhṃ rāghavasya mahātmanḥ| śaradvyapāye hemantaṛturiṣṭḥ pravartata||3.16.1||
meaning: While the great self Rama lived happily there, autumn passed and dear winter set in.

sanskrit: कृताभिषेको रामस्तु सीता सौमित्रिरेव च। तस्माद्गोदावरीतीरात्ततो जग्मुस्वमाश्रमम्।।3.17.1।।
transliteration: kṛtābhiṣeko rāmastu sītā saumitrireva ca| tasmādgodāvarītīrāttato jagmusvamāśramam||3.17.1||
meaning: Ablution over, Rama, accompanied by Sita and Lakshmana, went back from the bank of the river Godabari to their hermitage.

sanskrit: ततश्शूर्पणखां रामः कामपाशावपाशिताम्। स्वच्छया श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्मितपूर्वमथाब्रवीत्।।3.18.1।।
transliteration: tataśśūrpaṇakhāṃ rāmḥ kāmapāśāvapāśitām| svacchayā ślakṣṇayā vācā smitapūrvamathābravīt||3.18.1||
meaning: To Surpanakha bound by the noose of passion Rama with a smile replied in a clear, lucid manner:

sanskrit: तां तथा पतितां दृष्ट्वा विरूपां शोणितोक्षिताम्। भगिनीं क्रोधसन्तप्तः खरः पप्रच्छ राक्षसः।।3.19.1।।
transliteration: tāṃ tathā patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā virūpāṃ śoṇitokṣitām| bhaginīṃ krodhasantaptḥ kharḥ papraccha rākṣasḥ||3.19.1||
meaning: Burning with anger to see his sister fallen down disfigured and drenched in blood, Khara enquired:

sanskrit: कृतातिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति। आम्नत्ऱ्य स मुनीन्सर्वान्वनमेवान्वगाहत।।3.2.1।।
transliteration: kṛtātithyo'tha rāmastu sūryasyodayanṃ prati| āmnatऱya sa munīnsarvānvanamevānvagāhata||3.2.1||
meaning: After receiving hospitality from the sages, Rama took of all of them at sunrise and entered deep into the forest.

sanskrit: ततश्शूर्पणखा घोरा राघवाश्रममागता। राक्षसानाचचक्षे तौ भ्रातरौ सह सीतया।।3.20.1।।
transliteration: tataśśūrpaṇakhā ghorā rāghavāśramamāgatā| rākṣasānācacakṣe tau bhrātarau saha sītayā||3.20.1||
meaning: The frightful Surpanakha came to the hermitage of Rama and showed both the brothers and Sita to the demons.

sanskrit: स पुनः पतितां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधाच्छूर्पणखां खरः। उवाच व्यक्तया वाचा तामनर्थार्थमागताम्।।3.21.1।।
transliteration: sa punḥ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhācchūrpaṇakhāṃ kharḥ| uvāca vyaktayā vācā tāmanarthārthamāgatām||3.21.1||
meaning: Seeing Surpanakha collapse, Khara said in clear terms about the unfortunate situation she had created:

sanskrit: एवमाधर्षितश्शूरश्शूर्पणख्या खरस्ततः। उवाच रक्षसां मध्ये खरः खरतरं वचः।।3.22.1।।
transliteration: evamādharṣitaśśūraśśūrpaṇakhyā kharastatḥ| uvāca rakṣasāṃ madhye kharḥ kharatarṃ vacḥ||3.22.1||
meaning: Ashamed and accused thus in the presence of the demons, the valiant Khara spoke to Surpanakha in harsh words:

sanskrit: तस्मिन्याते बले घोरमशिवं शोणितोदकम्। अभ्यवर्षन्महामेघस्तुमुलो गर्दभारुणः।।3.23.1।।
transliteration: tasminyāte bale ghoramaśivṃ śoṇitodakam| abhyavarṣanmahāmeghastumulo gardabhāruṇḥ||3.23.1||
meaning: As the army marched from there (Janasthana) a huge dark cloud of the colour of an ass rained dreadful inauspicious water, red as blood.

sanskrit: आश्रमं प्रति याते तु खरे खरपराक्रमे। तानेवौत्पातिकान्रामस्सह भ्रात्रा ददर्श ह।।3.24.1।।
transliteration: āśramṃ prati yāte tu khare kharaparākrame| tānevautpātikānrāmassaha bhrātrā dadarśa ha||3.24.1||
meaning: When Khara endowed with malicious might was marching towards the hermitage, Rama and his brother saw the same omens of impending calamity the demon had seen.

sanskrit: अवष्टब्धधनुं रामं क्रुद्धं च रिपुघातिनम्। ददर्शाऽश्रममागम्य खरस्सह पुरस्सरैः।।3.25.1।।
transliteration: avaṣṭabdhadhanuṃ rāmṃ kruddhṃ ca ripughātinam| dadarśā'śramamāgamya kharassaha purassaraiḥ||3.25.1||
meaning: Khara accompanied by his pilot party arrived at the hermitage of Rama, the destroyer of enemies and saw him in fury, standing ready with his bow.

sanskrit: दूषणस्तु स्वकं सैन्यं हन्यमानं निरीक्ष्य सः। सन्दिदेश महाबाहुर्भीमवेगान्दुरासदान्।।3.26.1।। राक्षसान्पञ्चसहस्रान्समरेष्व
transliteration: dūṣaṇastu svakṃ sainyṃ hanyamānṃ nirīkṣya sḥ| sandideśa mahābāhurbhīmavegāndurāsadān||3.26.1|| rākṣasānpañcasahasrānsama
meaning: Mightyarmed Dusana saw the army getting killed in war. He led the forces of five thousand demons, dreadfuly quick at fighting, dangeous to face and who will not beat a retreat.

sanskrit: खरं तु रामाभिमुखं प्रयान्तं वाहिनीपतिः। राक्षसस्त्रिशिरा नाम सन्निपत्येदमब्रवीत्।।3.27.1।।
transliteration: kharṃ tu rāmābhimukhṃ prayāntṃ vāhinīpatiḥ| rākṣasastriśirā nāma sannipatyedamabravīt||3.27.1||
meaning: As Khara advanced towards Rama, Trisira the chief of the army approached him and said these words:

sanskrit: निहतं दूषणं दृष्ट्वा रणे त्रिशिरसा सह। खरस्याप्यभवत्त्रासो दृष्ट्वा रामस्य विक्रमम्।।3.28.1।।
transliteration: nihatṃ dūṣaṇṃ dṛṣṭvā raṇe triśirasā saha| kharasyāpyabhavattrāso dṛṣṭvā rāmasya vikramam||3.28.1||
meaning: Khara was overtaken by fear at the prowess of Rama, when he saw Dusana and Trisira killed.

sanskrit: खरं तु विरथं रामो गदापाणिमवस्थितम्। मृदुपूर्वं महातेजाः परुषं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।3.29.1।।
transliteration: kharṃ tu virathṃ rāmo gadāpāṇimavasthitam| mṛdupūrvṃ mahātejāḥ paruṣṃ vākyamabravīt||3.29.1||
meaning: Effulgent Rama looked at Khara who stood with a mace in hand minus his chariot and said to him first in a gentle voice and then harshly :

sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा लक्ष्मणश्श्रीमान्विराधे प्रहसन्निव। कोभवान्वनमभ्येत्य चरिष्यसि यथासुखम्।।3.3.1।।
transliteration: ityuktvā lakṣmaṇaśśrīmānvirādhe prahasanniva| kobhavānvanamabhyetya cariṣyasi yathāsukham||3.3.1||
meaning: Graceful Lakshmana asked Viradha with a smile, Who are you wandering in the forest at will ?.

sanskrit: भित्त्वा तु तां गदां बाणै राघवो धर्मवत्सलः। स्मयमानः खरं वाक्यं संरब्धमिदमब्रवीत्।।3.30.1।।
transliteration: bhittvā tu tāṃ gadāṃ bāṇai rāghavo dharmavatsalḥ| smayamānḥ kharṃ vākyṃ sṃrabdhamidamabravīt||3.30.1||
meaning: Rama, fond of dharma, broke into pieces Khara's mace with his arrows, and smiling at bewildered Khara, said:

sanskrit: त्वरमाणस्ततो गत्वा जनस्थानादकम्पनः। प्रविश्य लङ्कां वेगेन रावणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।3.31.1।।
transliteration: tvaramāṇastato gatvā janasthānādakampanḥ| praviśya laṅkāṃ vegena rāvaṇṃ vākyamabravīt||3.31.1||
meaning: Quickly did Akampana leave Janasthana, and quickly he entered Lanka. He said to Ravana:

sanskrit: ततश्शूर्पणखा दृष्ट्वा सहस्राणि चतुर्दश। हतान्येकेन रामेण रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम्।।3.32.1।। दूषणं च खरं चैव हतं त्रिशिरसा सह।
transliteration: tataśśūrpaṇakhā dṛṣṭvā sahasrāṇi caturdaśa| hatānyekena rāmeṇa rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām||3.32.1|| dūṣaṇṃ ca kharṃ caiva ha
meaning: Seeing Dusana, Khara and also Trisira along with the fourteen thousand demon warriors of terrific performance killed by Rama, singlehanded, Surpanakha roared like a cloud.

sanskrit: ततः शूर्पणखा दीना रावणं लोकरावणम्। अमात्यमध्ये सङ्क्रुद्धा परुषं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।3.33.1।।
transliteration: tatḥ śūrpaṇakhā dīnā rāvaṇṃ lokarāvaṇam| amātyamadhye saṅkruddhā paruṣṃ vākyamabravīt||3.33.1||
meaning: When the distressed, anguished Surpanakha met Ravana who makes the world weep, he was seated in the midst of his ministers. She addressed him these harsh words:

sanskrit: ततश्शूर्पणखां दृष्ट्वा ब्रुवन्तीं परुषं वचः। अमात्यमध्ये सङ्क्रुद्धः परिपप्रच्छ रावणः।।3.34.1।।
transliteration: tataśśūrpaṇakhāṃ dṛṣṭvā bruvantīṃ paruṣṃ vacḥ| amātyamadhye saṅkruddhḥ paripapraccha rāvaṇḥ||3.34.1||
meaning: Incensed at the harsh words Surpanakha used in the midst of ministers, Ravana said:

sanskrit: ततश्शूर्पणखावाक्यं तच्छ्रुत्वा रोमहर्षणम्। सचिवानभ्यनुज्ञाय कार्यं बुद्ध्वा जगाम ह।।3.35.1।।
transliteration: tataśśūrpaṇakhāvākyṃ tacchrutvā romaharṣaṇam| sacivānabhyanujñāya kāryṃ buddhvā jagāma ha||3.35.1||
meaning: Then hearing the horripilating words of Surpanakha, Ravana took leave of the ministers and went thinking about the task ahead of him.

sanskrit: मारीच श्रूयातां तात वचनं मम भाषतः। आर्तोऽस्मि मम चार्तस्य भवान्हि परमा गतिः।।3.36.1।।
transliteration: mārīca śrūyātāṃ tāta vacanṃ mama bhāṣatḥ| ārto'smi mama cārtasya bhavānhi paramā gatiḥ||3.36.1||
meaning: O dear Maricha hear my words. I am distressed and you are my ultimate refuge.

sanskrit: तच्छृत्वा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः। प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो मारीचो राक्षसेश्वरम्।।3.37.1।।
transliteration: tacchṛtvā rākṣasendrasya vākyṃ vākyaviśāradḥ| pratyuvāca mahāprājño mārīco rākṣaseśvaram||3.37.1||
meaning: Having heard the words of Ravana, lord of the demons, wise Maricha who was also an eloquent speaker replied:

sanskrit: कदाचिदप्यहं वीर्यात्पर्यटन्पृथिवीमिमाम्। बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयन्पर्वतोपमः।।3.38.1।। नीलजीमूतसङ्काशस्तप्तकाञ्चनकुण्डलः। भय
transliteration: kadācidapyahṃ vīryātparyaṭanpṛthivīmimām| balṃ nāgasahasrasya dhārayanparvatopamḥ||3.38.1|| nīlajīmūtasaṅkāśastaptakāñca
meaning: Once I was roaming the earth, like a mountain possessing the strength of a thousand elephants, like a dark cloud, wearing bright gold earrings and crown,holding a spear in hand, terrorising the people. I was wandering in

sanskrit: एवमस्मि तदा मुक्तः कथञ्चित्तेन संयुगे। इदानीमपि यद्वृत्तं तच्छृणुष्व निरुत्तरम्।।3.39.1।।
transliteration: evamasmi tadā muktḥ kathañcittena sṃyuge| idānīmapi yadvṛttṃ tacchṛṇuṣva niruttaram||3.39.1||
meaning: I was somehow saved by him this way in the combat.Listen without any reply to what has taken place recently.

sanskrit: ह्रियमाणौ तु तौ दृष्ट्वा वैदेही रामलक्ष्मणौ। उच्चैस्स्वरेण चुक्रोश प्रगृह्य सुमहाजाभुजौ।।3.4.1।।
transliteration: hriyamāṇau tu tau dṛṣṭvā vaidehī rāmalakṣmaṇau| uccaissvareṇa cukrośa pragṛhya sumahājābhujau||3.4.1||
meaning: Seeing those two mightyarmed Rama and Lakshmana being carried away by Viradha, Sita started crying loudly:

sanskrit: मारीचेन तु तद्वाक्यं क्षमं युक्तं च निशाचरः। उक्तो न प्रतिजग्राह मर्तुकाम इवौषधम्।।3.40.1।।
transliteration: mārīcena tu tadvākyṃ kṣamṃ yuktṃ ca niśācarḥ| ukto na pratijagrāha martukāma ivauṣadham||3.40.1||
meaning: The demon Ravana did not heed the appropriate advice of the competent Maricha just like a man wishing to die refuses medicine.

sanskrit: आज्ञप्तो राजवद्वाक्यं प्रतिकूलं निशाचरः। अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं मारीचो राक्षसाधिपम्।।3.41.1।।
transliteration: ājñapto rājavadvākyṃ pratikūlṃ niśācarḥ| abravītparuṣṃ vākyṃ mārīco rākṣasādhipam||3.41.1||
meaning: At this royal command which was against his interest Maracha used harsh words to the demonking:

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु वचनं मारीचो रावणं ततः। गच्छावेत्यब्रवीद्दीनो भयाद्रात्रिंचरप्रभोः।।3.42.1।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tu vacanṃ mārīco rāvaṇṃ tatḥ| gacchāvetyabravīddīno bhayādrātriṃcaraprabhoḥ||3.42.1||
meaning: Having thus spoken to the demonking, the distressed Maricha said out of fear, Let both of us go.

sanskrit: सा तं सम्प्रेक्ष्य सुश्रोणी कुसुमान्यपचिन्वती। हेमराजतवर्णाभ्यां पार्श्वाभ्यामुपशोभितम्।।3.43.1।। प्रहृष्टा चानवद्याङ्गी
transliteration: sā tṃ samprekṣya suśroṇī kusumānyapacinvatī| hemarājatavarṇābhyāṃ pārśvābhyāmupaśobhitam||3.43.1|| prahṛṣṭā cānavadyāṅgī
meaning: Sita while plucking flowers Sita who had fine hips, flawless beautiful limbs and pure golden complexion felt delighted to see the deer with gold and silver colours on both sides of his body. She called out to Rama and La

sanskrit: तथा तु तं समादिश्य भ्रातरं रघुनन्दनः। बबन्धासिं महातेजा जाम्बूनदमयत्सरुम्।।3.44.1।।
transliteration: tathā tu tṃ samādiśya bhrātarṃ raghunandanḥ| babandhāsiṃ mahātejā jāmbūnadamayatsarum||3.44.1||
meaning: The brilliant Rama, delight of the Raghu dynasty, thus instructed his brother and fastened a sword with a golden handle to his waist.

sanskrit: आर्तस्वरं तु तं भर्तुर्विज्ञाय सदृशं वने। उवाच लक्ष्मणं सीता गच्छ जीनीहि राघवम्।।3.45.1।।
transliteration: ārtasvarṃ tu tṃ bharturvijñāya sadṛśṃ vane| uvāca lakṣmaṇṃ sītā gaccha jīnīhi rāghavam||3.45.1||
meaning: On hearing the voice in distress and recognising that it was similar to her husband's voice, Sita said to Lakshmana, 'Go and find out Rama's whereabouts'.

sanskrit: तया परुषमुक्तस्तु कुपितो राघवानुजः। स विकाङ्क्षन्भृशं रामं प्रतस्थे नचिरादिव।।3.46.1।।
transliteration: tayā paruṣamuktastu kupito rāghavānujḥ| sa vikāṅkṣanbhṛśṃ rāmṃ pratasthe nacirādiva||3.46.1||
meaning: Lakshmana, brother of Rama, hurt by the harsh words of Sita, hastened with Rama's wellbeing in mind.

sanskrit: रावणेन तु वैदेही तदा पृष्टा जिहीर्षता। परिव्राजकरूपेण शशंसात्मानमात्मना।।3.47.1।।
transliteration: rāvaṇena tu vaidehī tadā pṛṣṭā jihīrṣatā| parivrājakarūpeṇa śaśṃsātmānamātmanā||3.47.1||
meaning: Then Ravana in the guise of a mendicant with crooked intention to abduct her, asked Vaidehi to tell him about herself.

sanskrit: एवं बृवन्त्यां सीतायां संरब्दः परुषं वचः। ललाटे भृकुटीं कृत्वा रावणः प्रत्युवाच ह।।3.48.1।।
transliteration: evṃ bṛvantyāṃ sītāyāṃ sṃrabdḥ paruṣṃ vacḥ| lalāṭe bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇḥ pratyuvāca ha||3.48.1||
meaning: Addressed thus by Sita, Ravana, his anger roused, knitted his eyebrows with a frown on his forehead and replied to her harshly:

sanskrit: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवाम्। हस्ते हस्तं समाहत्य चकार सुमहद्वपुः।।3.49.1।।
transliteration: sītāyā vacanṃ śrutvā daśagrīvḥ pratāpavām| haste hastṃ samāhatya cakāra sumahadvapuḥ||3.49.1||
meaning: On hearing the Sita's words, the powerful Ravana struck his palms one over the other and assumed a huge form (original figure).

sanskrit: हत्वा तु तं भीमबलं विराधं राक्षसं वने। ततस्सीतां परिष्वज्य समाश्वास्य च वीर्यवान्।।3.5.1।। अब्रवील्लक्ष्मणं रामो भ्रातरं
transliteration: hatvā tu tṃ bhīmabalṃ virādhṃ rākṣasṃ vane| tatassītāṃ pariṣvajya samāśvāsya ca vīryavān||3.5.1|| abravīllakṣmaṇṃ rāmo b
meaning: On killing Viradha, the demon of terrific strength, heroic Rama embraced Sita, consoled her and said to his brother Lakshmana, glowing like fire:

sanskrit: तं शब्दमवसुप्तस्तु जटायुरथ शुश्रुवे। निरीक्ष्य रावणं क्षिप्रं वैदेहीं च ददर्श सः।।3.50.1।।
transliteration: tṃ śabdamavasuptastu jaṭāyuratha śuśruve| nirīkṣya rāvaṇṃ kṣiprṃ vaidehīṃ ca dadarśa sḥ||3.50.1||
meaning: While reposing, Jatayu heard the cry and at once looked up and saw Ravana and Vaidehi.

sanskrit: इत्युक्तस्य यथान्यायं रावणस्य जटायुषा। क्रुद्धस्याग्निनिभास्सर्वा रेजुर्विंशतिदृष्टयः।।3.51.1।।
transliteration: ityuktasya yathānyāyṃ rāvaṇasya jaṭāyuṣā| kruddhasyāgninibhāssarvā rejurviṃśatidṛṣṭayḥ||3.51.1||
meaning: Ravana's twenty eyes glowed like fire in anger after Jatayu thus rightly said.

sanskrit: सा तु ताराधिपमुखी रावणेन समीक्ष्य तम्। गृध्रराजं विनिहतं विललाप सुदुःखिता।।3.52.1।।
transliteration: sā tu tārādhipamukhī rāvaṇena samīkṣya tam| gṛdhrarājṃ vinihatṃ vilalāpa suduḥkhitā||3.52.1||
meaning: Sita,whose face was like the lord of the stars (Moon), saw Jatayu, king of birds, struck down by Ravana, and lamented in extreme grif :

sanskrit: खमुत्पतन्तं तं दृष्ट्वा मैथिली जनकात्मजा। दुःखिता परमोद्विग्ना भये महति वर्तिनी।।3.53.1।।
transliteration: khamutpatantṃ tṃ dṛṣṭvā maithilī janakātmajā| duḥkhitā paramodvignā bhaye mahati vartinī||3.53.1||
meaning: Sita, daughter of Janaka, princess of Mithila felt miserable, looking at Ravana taking off and got very much agitated out of fear.

sanskrit: ह्रियमाणा तु वैदेही कञ्चिन्नाथमपश्यती। ददर्श गिरिशृङ्गस्थान्पञ्च वानरपुङ्गवान्।।3.54.1।।
transliteration: hriyamāṇā tu vaidehī kañcinnāthamapaśyatī| dadarśa giriśṛṅgasthānpañca vānarapuṅgavān||3.54.1||
meaning: While Sita was being kidnapped, she saw no one to protect her. Only five great monkeys stood on the top of a mountain.

sanskrit: सन्दिश्य राक्षसान्घोरान् रावणोऽष्टौ महाबलान्। आत्मानं बुद्धिवैक्लब्यात्कृतकृत्यममन्यत।।3.55.1।।
transliteration: sandiśya rākṣasānghorān rāvaṇo'ṣṭau mahābalān| ātmānṃ buddhivaiklabyātkṛtakṛtyamamanyata||3.55.1||
meaning: After ordering the eight most fierce and powerful demons, Ravana had a sense of accomplishment within himself because of his perverse intellect.

sanskrit: सा तथोक्ता तु वैदेही निर्भया शोककर्शिता। तृणमन्तरतः कृत्वा रावणं प्रत्यभाषत।।3.56.1।।
transliteration: sā tathoktā tu vaidehī nirbhayā śokakarśitā| tṛṇamantaratḥ kṛtvā rāvaṇṃ pratyabhāṣata||3.56.1||
meaning: Thus addressed by Ravana, Sita, immersed in deep sorrow and unafraid of him, placed a blade of grass between her and him (intending not to speak to him straight) and replied:

sanskrit: राक्षसं मृगरूपेण चरन्तं कामरूपिणम्। निहत्य रामो मारीचं तूर्णं पथि न्यवर्तत।।3.57.1।।
transliteration: rākṣasṃ mṛgarūpeṇa carantṃ kāmarūpiṇam| nihatya rāmo mārīcṃ tūrṇṃ pathi nyavartata||3.57.1||
meaning: Rama killed Maricha, the demon assuming the form of the deer as per his will and swiftly took the return path.

sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं दीनं शून्ये दशरथात्मजः। पर्यपृच्छत धर्मात्मा वैदेहीमागतं विना।।3.58.1।।
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇṃ dīnṃ śūnye daśarathātmajḥ| paryapṛcchata dharmātmā vaidehīmāgatṃ vinā||3.58.1||
meaning: Rama, son of Dasaratha, the righteous self, saw Lakshmana downcast and dejected. Seeing him without Sita, Rama enquired:

sanskrit: अथाश्रमादुपावृत्तमन्तरा रघुनन्दनः। परिपप्रच्छ सौमित्रिं रामो दुःखार्दितं पुनः।।3.59.1।।
transliteration: athāśramādupāvṛttamantarā raghunandanḥ| paripapraccha saumitriṃ rāmo duḥkhārditṃ punḥ||3.59.1||
meaning: Rama, the delight of the Raghus, once again questioned Lakshmana who had come out of the hermitage, deeply hurt:

sanskrit: शरभङ्गे दिवं प्राप्ते मुनिसङ्घास्समागताः। अभ्यगच्छन्त काकुत्स्थं रामं ज्वलिततेजसम्।।3.6.1।।
transliteration: śarabhaṅge divṃ prāpte munisaṅghāssamāgatāḥ| abhyagacchanta kākutsthṃ rāmṃ jvalitatejasam||3.6.1||
meaning: When Sarabhanga attained the heaven, all the sages collected together and came to Rama whose radiance was like fire.

sanskrit: भृशमाव्रजमानस्य तस्याधो वामलोचनम्। प्रास्फुरच्चास्खलद्रामो वेपथुश्चाप्य जायत।।3.60.1।।
transliteration: bhṛśamāvrajamānasya tasyādho vāmalocanam| prāsphuraccāskhaladrāmo vepathuścāpya jāyata||3.60.1||
meaning: As Rama was returning( to the hermitage), his left eye throbbed repeatedly and he stumbled and his body trembled.

sanskrit: दृष्ट्वाश्रमपदं शून्यं रामो दशरथात्मजः। रहितां पर्णशालां च विध्वस्तान्यासनानि च।।3.61.1।। अदृष्ट्वा तत्र वैदेहीं सन्निरी
transliteration: dṛṣṭvāśramapadṃ śūnyṃ rāmo daśarathātmajḥ| rahitāṃ parṇaśālāṃ ca vidhvastānyāsanāni ca||3.61.1|| adṛṣṭvā tatra vaidehīṃ
meaning: Rama, son of Dasaratha, saw the empty cottage devoid of Sita. The mats were displaced. He searched everywhere but unable to see Vaidehi lifted his lovely arms and said:

sanskrit: सीतामपश्यन्धर्मात्मा शोकोपहतचेतनः। विललाप महाबाहू रामः कमललोचनः।।3.62.1।।
transliteration: sītāmapaśyandharmātmā śokopahatacetanḥ| vilalāpa mahābāhū rāmḥ kamalalocanḥ||3.62.1||
meaning: The righteous, the longarmed,lotuseyed Rama, unable to see Sita wept with his senses overwhilmed by grief.

sanskrit: स राजपुत्रः प्रियया विहीनः शोकेन मोहेन च पीड्यमानः। विषादयन्भ्रातरमार्तरूपो भूयो विषादं प्रविवेश तीव्रम्।।3.63.1।।
transliteration: sa rājaputrḥ priyayā vihīnḥ śokena mohena ca pīḍyamānḥ| viṣādayanbhrātaramārtarūpo bhūyo viṣādṃ praviveśa tīvram||3.63.1
meaning: Prince Rama, separated from his beloved, lost his senses out of sorrow. Seeing his brother in a distressed state, he sank again into intense grief.

sanskrit: स दीनो दीनया वाचा लक्ष्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत्। शीघ्रं लक्ष्मण जानीहि गत्वा गोदावरीं नदीम्।।3.64.1।। अपि गोदावरीं सीता पद्मान्
transliteration: sa dīno dīnayā vācā lakṣmaṇṃ vākyamabravīt| śīghrṃ lakṣmaṇa jānīhi gatvā godāvarīṃ nadīm||3.64.1|| api godāvarīṃ sītā pa
meaning: Rama in dejection said these pitiable words to Lakshmana,O Lakashmana, go swiftly to the river Godavari and find out if Sita has gone there to get lotuses.

sanskrit: तप्यमानं तथा रामं सीताहरणकर्शितम्। लोकानामभवे युक्तं सांवर्तकमिवानलम्।।3.65.1।। वीक्षमाणं धनुस्सज्यं निश्श्वसन्तं पुनः प
transliteration: tapyamānṃ tathā rāmṃ sītāharaṇakarśitam| lokānāmabhave yuktṃ sāṃvartakamivānalam||3.65.1|| vīkṣamāṇṃ dhanussajyṃ niśśvas
meaning: Tormented and emaciated due to Sita's abduction, resembling the fire at the time of dissolution of the creation, ready to destroy the world, Rama looked at his bow strung again and again, breathing hot sighs like Lord Si

sanskrit: तं तथा शोकसन्तप्तं विलपन्तमनाथवत्। मोहेन महताविष्टं परिद्यूनमचेतनम्।।3.66.1।। ततस्सौमित्रिराश्वास्य मुहूर्तादिव लक्ष्मणः
transliteration: tṃ tathā śokasantaptṃ vilapantamanāthavat| mohena mahatāviṣṭṃ paridyūnamacetanam||3.66.1|| tatassaumitrirāśvāsya muhūrtā
meaning: Lakshmana, son of Sumitra, consoling the mighty miserable Rama, who was afflicted with sorrow, and was weeping helplessly like an orphan, drowned in great delusion, devoid of consciousness, pressed his feet and addressed

sanskrit: पूर्वजोऽप्युक्तमात्रस्तु लक्ष्मणेन सुभाषितम्। सारग्राही महासारं प्रतिजग्राह राघवः।।3.67.1।।
transliteration: pūrvajo'pyuktamātrastu lakṣmaṇena subhāṣitam| sāragrāhī mahāsārṃ pratijagrāha rāghavḥ||3.67.1||
meaning: Even though Rama was elder, he could grasp the quintessence of the wise counsel only after Lakshmana had said it.

sanskrit: रामस्सम्प्रेक्ष्य तं गृध्रं भुवि रौद्रेण पातितम्। सौमित्रिं मित्रसम्पन्नमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।3.68.1।।
transliteration: rāmassamprekṣya tṃ gṛdhrṃ bhuvi raudreṇa pātitam| saumitriṃ mitrasampannamidṃ vacanamabravīt||3.68.1||
meaning: Seeing the vulture lying on the ground thrown down by the fierce demon, Rama said to friendly Lakshmana:

sanskrit: कृत्वैवमुदकं तस्मै प्रस्थितौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। अवेक्षन्तौ वने सीतां पश्चिमां जग्मतुर्दिशम्।।3.69.1।।
transliteration: kṛtvaivamudakṃ tasmai prasthitau rāmalakṣmaṇau| avekṣantau vane sītāṃ paścimāṃ jagmaturdiśam||3.69.1||
meaning: Rama and Lakshmana offered libations (for Jatayu) and went westward, looking for Sita in the forest.

sanskrit: रामस्तु सहितो भ्रात्रा सीतया च परन्तपः। सुतीक्ष्णस्याश्रमपदं जगाम सह तैर्द्विजैः।।3.7.1।।
transliteration: rāmastu sahito bhrātrā sītayā ca parantapḥ| sutīkṣṇasyāśramapadṃ jagāma saha tairdvijaiḥ||3.7.1||
meaning: Rama, the scorcher of enemies, along with his brother Lakshmana and Sita and the sages went to Sutikshna's hermitage.

sanskrit: तौ तु तत्र स्थितौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। बाहुपाशपरिक्षिप्तौ कबन्धो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।।3.70.1।।
transliteration: tau tu tatra sthitau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau| bāhupāśaparikṣiptau kabandho vākyamabravīt||3.70.1||
meaning: Kabandha saw the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, stand there bound by the shackles of his arms and said:

sanskrit: पुरा राम महाबाहो महाबलपराक्रम। रूपमासीन्ममा चिन्त्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्।।3.71.1।। यथा सोमस्य शक्रस्य सूर्यस्य च यथा
transliteration: purā rāma mahābāho mahābalaparākrama| rūpamāsīnmamā cintyṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam||3.71.1|| yathā somasya śakrasya sūryas
meaning: O longarmed, mighty and powerful Rama in the past I was handsome like the Moon or Indra or the Sun inconceivable to all the three worlds.

sanskrit: एवमुक्तौतु तौ वीरौ कबन्धेन नरेश्वरौ। गिरिप्रदरमासाद्य पावकं विससर्जतुः।।3.72.1।।
transliteration: evamuktautu tau vīrau kabandhena nareśvarau| giripradaramāsādya pāvakṃ visasarjatuḥ||3.72.1||
meaning: Thus said by Kabandha, the two lords of men, the heroes reached a cave in the mountain and lighted the fire.

sanskrit: निदर्शयित्वा रामाय सीतायाः प्रतिपादने। वाक्यमन्वर्थमर्थज्ञः कबन्धः पुनरब्रवीत्।।3.73.1।।
transliteration: nidarśayitvā rāmāya sītāyāḥ pratipādane| vākyamanvarthamarthajñḥ kabandhḥ punarabravīt||3.73.1||
meaning: Having shown Rama the means to find Sita, Kabandha spoke again these significant words:

sanskrit: तौ कबन्धेन तं मार्गं पम्पाया दर्शितं वने। प्रतस्थतुर्दिशं गृह्य प्रतीचीं नृवरात्मजौ।।3.74.1।।
transliteration: tau kabandhena tṃ mārgṃ pampāyā darśitṃ vane| pratasthaturdiśṃ gṛhya pratīcīṃ nṛvarātmajau||3.74.1||
meaning: The two princes set forth in the western direction towards Pampa shown by Kabandha.

sanskrit: दिवं तु तस्यां यातायां शबर्यां स्वेन तेजसा। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा चिन्तयामास राघवः।।3.75.1।।
transliteration: divṃ tu tasyāṃ yātāyāṃ śabaryāṃ svena tejasā| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā cintayāmāsa rāghavḥ||3.75.1||
meaning: When Sabari departed for heaven with her brilliance, Rama contemplated (about the power of sages)with Lakshmana.

sanskrit: रामस्तु सहसौमित्रिस्सुतीक्ष्णेनाभिपूजितः। परिणाम्य निशां तत्र प्रभाते प्रत्यबुध्यत।।3.8.1।।
transliteration: rāmastu sahasaumitrissutīkṣṇenābhipūjitḥ| pariṇāmya niśāṃ tatra prabhāte pratyabudhyata||3.8.1||
meaning: Rama, worshipped by Sutikshna and accompanied by Lakshmana, spent the night at the hermitage, and got up early in the morning.

sanskrit: सुतीक्ष्णेनाभ्यनुज्ञातं प्रस्थितं रघुनन्दनम्। हृद्यया स्निग्धया वाचा भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।3.9.1।।
transliteration: sutīkṣṇenābhyanujñātṃ prasthitṃ raghunandanam| hṛdyayā snigdhayā vācā bhartāramidamabravīt||3.9.1||
meaning: While Rama was leaving with the permission of Sutikshna, Sita spoke these warm, affectionate words to her husband:

sanskrit: जटिलं चीरवसनं प्राञ्जलिं पतितं भुवि। ददर्श रामो दुर्दर्शं युगान्ते भास्करंयथा।।2.100.1।।
transliteration: jaṭilṃ cīravasanṃ prāñjaliṃ patitṃ bhuvi| dadarśa rāmo durdarśṃ yugānte bhāskarṃyathā||2.100.1||
meaning: Rama beheld Bharata with matted locks and robes of bark fallen down on the ground with folded hands like the Sun at the time of dissolution of the world. It was really difficult to look at him.

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतः प्रत्युवाच ह। किं मे धर्माद्विहीनस्य राजधर्मः करिष्यति।।2.101.1।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanṃ śrutvā bharatḥ pratyuvāca ha| kiṃ me dharmādvihīnasya rājadharmḥ kariṣyati||2.101.1||
meaning: On listening to Rama, Bharata replied Of what use shall be these royal duties to me, when I have fallen from righteousness?

sanskrit: तां श्रुत्वा करुणां वाचं पितुर्मरणसंहिताम्। राघवो भरते नोक्तां बभूव गतचेतनः।।2.102.1।।
transliteration: tāṃ śrutvā karuṇāṃ vācṃ piturmaraṇasṃhitām| rāghavo bharate noktāṃ babhūva gatacetanḥ||2.102.1||
meaning: Having heard the words of Bharata regarding the death of his father, Rama became unconscious.

sanskrit: वसिष्ठः पुरतः कृत्वा दारान्दशरथस्य च। अभिचक्राम तं देशं रामदर्शनतर्षितः।।2.103.1।।
transliteration: vasiṣṭhḥ puratḥ kṛtvā dārāndaśarathasya ca| abhicakrāma tṃ deśṃ rāmadarśanatarṣitḥ||2.103.1||
meaning: Longing to see Rama, Vasistha, headed by the wives of Dasaratha, set out on foot (where Rama was offering libations).

sanskrit: तं तु राम स्समाश्वास्य भ्रातरं गुरवत्सलम्। लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे।।2.104.1।।
transliteration: tṃ tu rāma ssamāśvāsya bhrātarṃ guravatsalam| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame||2.104.1||
meaning: Rama with his brother Lakshmana having consoled Bharata who is ever devoted to elders began to question:

sanskrit: ततः पुरुषसिंहानां वृतानां तै स्सुहृद्गणैः। शोचतामेव रजनी दुःखेन व्यत्यवर्तत।।2.105.1।।
transliteration: tatḥ puruṣasiṃhānāṃ vṛtānāṃ tai ssuhṛdgaṇaiḥ| śocatāmeva rajanī duḥkhena vyatyavartata||2.105.1||
meaning: That night passed off painfully for the four lion like brothers as they lamented, surrounded by their hosts of friends.

sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु विरते रामे वचनमर्थवत्। ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरे रामं प्रकृतिवत्सलम्।।2.106.1।। उवाच भरत श्चित्रं धार्मिको धार्मिक
transliteration: evamuktvā tu virate rāme vacanamarthavat| tato mandākinītīre rāmṃ prakṛtivatsalam||2.106.1|| uvāca bharata ścitrṃ dhārmi
meaning: Rama remained silent after saying these meaningful words on the bank of river Mandakini. Then the Bharata, conforming to righteousness, replied in clear words to the virtuous Rama who was affectionate by nature.

sanskrit: पुनरेवं ब्रुवाणं तं भरतं लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। प्रत्युवाच तत श्श्रीमान् ज्ञातिमध्येऽभिसत्कृतः।।2.107.1।।
transliteration: punarevṃ bruvāṇṃ tṃ bharatṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajḥ| pratyuvāca tata śśrīmān jñātimadhye'bhisatkṛtḥ||2.107.1||
meaning: Wellhonoured in the midst of relatives, the celebrated Rama, elder brother of Lakshmana, then said to Bharata who was going to speak again.

sanskrit: आश्वासयन्तं भरतं जाबालिर्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः। उवाच रामं धर्मज्ञं धर्मापेतमिदं वचः।।2.108.1।।
transliteration: āśvāsayantṃ bharatṃ jābālirbrāhmaṇottamḥ| uvāca rāmṃ dharmajñṃ dharmāpetamidṃ vacḥ||2.108.1||
meaning: While Rama, conversant with dharma, was consoling Bharata, Jabali an eminent brahmin addressed him in words contrary to righteousness.

sanskrit: जाबालेस्तु वचश्श्रुत्वा राम स्सत्यात्मनां वरः। उवाच परया भक्त्या स्वबुद्ध्या चाविपन्नया।।2.109.1।।
transliteration: jābālestu vacaśśrutvā rāma ssatyātmanāṃ varḥ| uvāca parayā bhaktyā svabuddhyā cāvipannayā||2.109.1||
meaning: Hearing Jabali's words, Rama, the foremost among the truthful, gave a rejoinder, exercising his own judgment and firm conviction with due respect (to Jabali).

sanskrit: क्रुद्धमाज्ञाय रामं तु वसिष्ठः प्रत्युवाच ह। जाबालिरपि जानीते लोकस्यास्य गतागतिम्।।2.110.1।।
transliteration: kruddhamājñāya rāmṃ tu vasiṣṭhḥ pratyuvāca ha| jābālirapi jānīte lokasyāsya gatāgatim||2.110.1||
meaning: Seeing Rama angry Vasistha intercedes, saying that Jabali is wellaware of the exits and entrances of humans on earth.

sanskrit: वसिष्ठस्तु तदा राममुक्त्वा राजपुरोहितः। अब्रवीद्धर्मसंयुक्तं पुनरेवापरं वचः।।2.111.1।।
transliteration: vasiṣṭhastu tadā rāmamuktvā rājapurohitḥ| abravīddharmasṃyuktṃ punarevāparṃ vacḥ||2.111.1||
meaning: Vasistha, the family priest, continued to speak to Rama on righteousness.

sanskrit: तमप्रतिमतेजोभ्यां भ्रातृभ्यां रोमहर्षणम्। विस्मिता: स‌ङ्गमं प्रेक्ष्य समवेता महर्षयः।।2.112.1।।
transliteration: tamapratimatejobhyāṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ romaharṣaṇam| vismitā: sa‌ṅgamṃ prekṣya samavetā maharṣayḥ||2.112.1||
meaning: The great sages assembled there were amazed at witnessing the meeting of the two brothers (Rama and Bharata) of umparalleled briliance.

sanskrit: तत श्शिरसि कृत्वा तु पादुके भरतस्तदा। आरुरोह रथं हृष्टः शत्रुघ्नेन समन्वितः।।2.113.1।।
transliteration: tata śśirasi kṛtvā tu pāduke bharatastadā| āruroha rathṃ hṛṣṭḥ śatrughnena samanvitḥ||2.113.1||
meaning: Then Bharata accompanied by Satrughna, placing the sandals on his head in delight, boarded the chariot.

sanskrit: स्निग्धगम्भीरघोषेण स्यन्दनेनोपयान्प्रभुः। अयोध्यां भरतः क्षिप्रं प्रविवेश महायशाः।।2.114.1।।
transliteration: snigdhagambhīraghoṣeṇa syandanenopayānprabhuḥ| ayodhyāṃ bharatḥ kṣiprṃ praviveśa mahāyaśāḥ||2.114.1||
meaning: Bharata, the renowned lord (of Ayodhya) travelled on the chariot that produced a deep, soothing, sound. And entered Ayodhya soon.

sanskrit: ततो निक्षिप्य मातृ़ स्स अयोध्यायां दृढ व्रतः। भरत श्शोकसन्तप्तो गुरूनिदमथाब्रवीत्।।2.115.1।।
transliteration: tato nikṣipya mātṛ़ ssa ayodhyāyāṃ dṛḍha vratḥ| bharata śśokasantapto gurūnidamathābravīt||2.115.1||
meaning: After keeping his mothers in Ayodhya, the griefstricken Bharata who was firm in his vows, said to the elders:

sanskrit: प्रतिप्रयाते भरते वसन्रामस्तपोवने। लक्षयामास सोद्वेगमथौत्सुक्यं तपस्विनाम्।।2.116.1।।
transliteration: pratiprayāte bharate vasanrāmastapovane| lakṣayāmāsa sodvegamathautsukyṃ tapasvinām||2.116.1||
meaning: After Bharta, had departed, Rama who was living in the penancegrove of ascetics observed that the ascetics were filled with apprehensions, and were eager (to leave that forest).

sanskrit: राघव स्त्वथ यातेषु तपस्विषु विचिन्तयन्। न तत्रारोचयद्वासं कारणैर्बहुभिस्तदा।।2.117.1।।
transliteration: rāghava stvatha yāteṣu tapasviṣu vicintayan| na tatrārocayadvāsṃ kāraṇairbahubhistadā||2.117.1||
meaning: When the ascetics had departed, Rama thought over the matter well and did not like to reside there for many reasons.

sanskrit: सात्वेवमुक्ता वैदेही अनसूयाऽनसूयया। प्रतिपूज्य वचो मन्दं प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमे।।2.118.1।।
transliteration: sātvevamuktā vaidehī anasūyā'nasūyayā| pratipūjya vaco mandṃ pravaktumupacakrame||2.118.1||
meaning: When Anasuya thus addressed Vaidehi who is free from any malice, she worshipped Anasuya and started speaking in a gentle tone.

sanskrit: अनसूया तु धर्मज्ञा श्रुत्वा तां महतीं कथाम्। पर्यष्वजत बाहुभ्यां शिरस्याघ्राय मैथिलीम्।।2.119.1।।
transliteration: anasūyā tu dharmajñā śrutvā tāṃ mahatīṃ kathām| paryaṣvajata bāhubhyāṃ śirasyāghrāya maithilīm||2.119.1||
meaning: Then righteous Anasuya, having heard the great story of Sita, kissed her on the forehead and embraced her with both the arms.

sanskrit: अतदर्हं महाराजं शयानमतथोचितम्। ययातिमिव पुण्यान्ते देवलोकात्परिच्युतम्।।2.13.1।। अनर्थरूपा सिद्धार्था ह्यभीता भयदर्शिनी।
transliteration: atadarhṃ mahārājṃ śayānamatathocitam| yayātimiva puṇyānte devalokātparicyutam||2.13.1|| anartharūpā siddhārthā hyabhītā
meaning: The maharaja lying on the floor resembled (king) Yayati fallen from heaven after his merits (earned earlier) were exhausted. He neither deserved nor was accustomed to such (humiliating) treatment. Fearless Kaikeyi ,the i

sanskrit: तदन्तःपुरद्वारं समतीत्य जनाकुलम्। प्रविविक्तां ततः कक्ष्यामाससाद पुराणवित्।।2.16.1।। प्रासकार्मुकबिभ्रद्भिर्युवभिर्मृष्ट
transliteration: tadantḥpuradvārṃ samatītya janākulam| praviviktāṃ tatḥ kakṣyāmāsasāda purāṇavit||2.16.1|| prāsakārmukabibhradbhiryuvabhi
meaning: Sumantra, who was conversant with ancient traditions, passed through the entrance of the inner apartment full of people and reached the sparsely crowded courtyard. There alert, loyal young men were attentively guarding t

sanskrit: अथ तं व्यथया दीनं सविशेषममर्षितम्। श्वसन्तमिव नागेन्द्रं रोषविस्फारितेक्षणम्।।2.22.1।। आसाद्य रामस्सौमित्रिं सुहृदं भ्रा
transliteration: atha tṃ vyathayā dīnṃ saviśeṣamamarṣitam| śvasantamiva nāgendrṃ roṣavisphāritekṣaṇam||2.22.1|| āsādya rāmassaumitriṃ suh
meaning: The selfpossessed Rama held his composure and approached his beloved, intimate brother Lakshmana who was (looking) miserable with his mental agony. To him, who was hissing like a king cobra, he said:

sanskrit: अभिवाद्य च कौसल्यां राम स्संप्रस्थितो वनम्। कृतस्वस्त्ययनो मात्रा धर्मिष्ठे वर्त्मनि स्थितः।।2.26.1।। विराजयन्राजसुतो रा
transliteration: abhivādya ca kausalyāṃ rāma ssṃprasthito vanam| kṛtasvastyayano mātrā dharmiṣṭhe vartmani sthitḥ||2.26.1|| virājayanrāja
meaning: After the benedictory rites were performed by his mother Kausalya, Rama paid obeisance to her and staying on the righteous path decided to depart to the forest. He entered the highway thronged with people and illumining

sanskrit: एवं शृत्वा तु संवादं लक्ष्मणः पूर्वमागतः। बाष्पपर्याकुलमुखः शोकं सोढुमशक्नुवन्।।2.31.1।। स भ्रातुश्चरणौ गाढं निपीड्य रघु
transliteration: evṃ śṛtvā tu sṃvādṃ lakṣmaṇḥ pūrvamāgatḥ| bāṣpaparyākulamukhḥ śokṃ soḍhumaśaknuvan||2.31.1|| sa bhrātuścaraṇau gāḍhṃ nip
meaning: Lakshmana who had already reached there heard the conversation (between Sita and Rama). His eyes brimming with tears, he was unable to bear the grief. He held the feet of his brother tightly and said to the illustrious S

sanskrit: ततश्शासन माज्ञाय भ्रातु श्शुभतरं प्रियम्। गत्वा स प्रविवेशाशु सुयज्ञस्य निवेशनम्।।2.32.1।।
transliteration: tataśśāsana mājñāya bhrātu śśubhatarṃ priyam| gatvā sa praviveśāśu suyajñasya niveśanam||2.32.1||
meaning: Lakshmana having understood the very auspicious and welcome order (of Rama) immediately proceeded to the house of Suyajna.

sanskrit: ततो निर्धूय सहसा शिरो निश्श्वस्य चासकृत्। पाणौ पाणिं विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान् कटकटाप्य च ।।2.35.1।। लोचने कोपसंरक्ते वर्णं पू
transliteration: tato nirdhūya sahasā śiro niśśvasya cāsakṛt| pāṇau pāṇiṃ viniṣpiṣya dantān kaṭakaṭāpya ca ||2.35.1|| locane kopasṃrakte
meaning: Overcome with anger, charioteer Sumantra started shaking his head and sighing off and on, crushing his palms and grinding his teeth. His eyes turned red due to anger. Overcome with a sudden, ominous grief, the complexion

sanskrit: तस्यां चीरं वसानायां नाथवत्यामनाथवत्। प्रचुक्रोश जनस्सर्वो धिक्त्वां दशरथं त्विति।।2.38.1।।
transliteration: tasyāṃ cīrṃ vasānāyāṃ nāthavatyāmanāthavat| pracukrośa janassarvo dhiktvāṃ daśarathṃ tviti||2.38.1||
meaning: Beholding Sita who was wearing a bark garment, like one without a support, though having a husband, all the people cried bitterly exclaiming O Dasaratha, fie on you.

sanskrit: रामस्य तु वचः शृत्वा मुनिवेशधरं च तम्। समीक्ष्य सह भार्याभी राजा विगतचेतनः।।2.39.1।। नैनं दुःखेन सन्तप्तः प्रत्यवैक्षत र
transliteration: rāmasya tu vacḥ śṛtvā muniveśadharṃ ca tam| samīkṣya saha bhāryābhī rājā vigatacetanḥ||2.39.1|| nainṃ duḥkhena santaptḥ
meaning: After hearing Rama and beholding him in the robes of an ascetic, Dasaratha and his wives fell unconscious. With his body and mind afflicted with grief, Dasaratha could not look Rama in the face nor could he make a reply.

sanskrit: गतेष्वथ नृपो भूयः पौरेषु सह मन्त्रिभिः। मन्त्रयित्वा ततश्चक्रे निश्चयज्ञस्सनिश्चयम्।।2.4.1।। श्व एव पुष्यो भविताश्वोऽभिष
transliteration: gateṣvatha nṛpo bhūyḥ paureṣu saha mantribhiḥ| mantrayitvā tataścakre niścayajñassaniścayam||2.4.1|| śva eva puṣyo bhavi
meaning: After the citizens departed, the king, an expert in decisionmaking again consulted his counsellors and said, Tomorrow Pushya star is in the ascendence and my son, Rama (handsome) with coppercoloured eyes which resemble r

sanskrit: ततः समीक्ष्य शयने सन्नं शोकेन पार्थिवम्। कौशल्या पुत्रशोकार्ता तमुवाच महीपतिम्।।2.43.1।।
transliteration: tatḥ samīkṣya śayane sannṃ śokena pārthivam| kauśalyā putraśokārtā tamuvāca mahīpatim||2.43.1||
meaning: Struck by the grief of her son's departure, Kausalya looked at the king who lay on the couch completely exhausted and said to him.

sanskrit: तेषामेवं विषण्णानां पीडितानामतीव च। बाष्पविप्लुतनेत्राणां सशोकानां मुमूर्षया।।2.48.1।। अनुगम्य निवृत्तानां रामं नगरवासिन
transliteration: teṣāmevṃ viṣaṇṇānāṃ pīḍitānāmatīva ca| bāṣpaviplutanetrāṇāṃ saśokānāṃ mumūrṣayā||2.48.1|| anugamya nivṛttānāṃ rāmṃ nagar
meaning: The people afflicted with sorrow followed Rama and returned to the city deeply distressed. Eyes overflowing with tears, they longed for death. Smitten with grief, they lost their highmindedness and looked as if their lif

sanskrit: वनं गते धर्मपरे रामे रमयतां वरे। कौसल्या रुदती स्वार्ता भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.61.1।।
transliteration: vanṃ gate dharmapare rāme ramayatāṃ vare| kausalyā rudatī svārtā bhartāramidamabravīt||2.61.1||
meaning: When Rama, the greatest among those who please the people, he who was conscious of his duty left for the forest. Kausalya, sobbing in bitter anguish, said to her husband:

sanskrit: अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां प्रातरेवापरेऽहनि। वन्दिनः पर्युपातिष्ठंस्तत्पार्थिव निवेशनम्।।2.65.1।। सूताः परमसंस्कारा मङ्गलाश
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prātarevāpare'hani| vandinḥ paryupātiṣṭhṃstatpārthiva niveśanam||2.65.1|| sūtāḥ paramasṃskārā ma
meaning: Then on the following day (unaware of Dasaratha's death) panegyrists uttering benedictions, highly accomplished bards and genealogists proficient in reciting auspicious words, singers versed in musical science reached th

sanskrit: भरते ब्रुवति स्वप्नं दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः। प्रविश्यासह्यपरिखं रम्यं राजगृहं पुरम्।।2.70.1।। समागम्य तु राज्ञा च राजपुत
transliteration: bharate bruvati svapnṃ dūtāste klāntavāhanāḥ| praviśyāsahyaparikhṃ ramyṃ rājagṛhṃ puram||2.70.1|| samāgamya tu rājñā ca
meaning: While Bharata was relating his dream, the mounted messengers (from Ayodhya) with their weary horses entered the lovely city of Rajagriha surrounded by an impassable moat. There they met the king of Kekaya country and his

sanskrit: तमेवं शोकसन्तप्तं भरतं कैकयी सुतम्। उवाच वदतां श्रेष्ठो वसिष्ठ श्श्रेष्ठवागृषिः।।2.76.1।।
transliteration: tamevṃ śokasantaptṃ bharatṃ kaikayī sutam| uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vasiṣṭha śśreṣṭhavāgṛṣiḥ||2.76.1||
meaning: Vasistha, the most eloquent and the best of ascetics said to Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi who was tormented with grief:

sanskrit: ततो दशाहेऽतिगते कृतशौचो नृपात्मजः। द्वादशेऽहनि सम्प्राप्ते श्राद्धकर्माण्यकारयत्।।2.77.1।।
transliteration: tato daśāhe'tigate kṛtaśauco nṛpātmajḥ| dvādaśe'hani samprāpte śrāddhakarmāṇyakārayat||2.77.1||
meaning: Having observed the tenday mourning period, Bharata purified himself on the twelfth day and got the shraddha rites (obsequies) performed.

sanskrit: अथ यात्रां समीहन्तं शत्रुघ्नो लक्ष्मणानुजः। भरतं शोकसन्तप्तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।2.78.1।।
transliteration: atha yātrāṃ samīhantṃ śatrughno lakṣmaṇānujḥ| bharatṃ śokasantaptamidṃ vacanamabravīt||2.78.1||
meaning: As the griefstricken Bharata was intending to proceed to Rama, Lakshmana's younger brother Satrughna said to him:

sanskrit: ततः प्रभातसमये दिवसेऽथ चतुर्दशे। समेत्य राजकर्तारो भरतं वाक्यमब्रुवन्।।2.79.1।।
transliteration: tatḥ prabhātasamaye divase'tha caturdaśe| sametya rājakartāro bharatṃ vākyamabruvan||2.79.1||
meaning: Then, at the hour of dawn on the fourteenth day, all those who were empowered to proclaim the king, assembled and addressed Bharata:

sanskrit: अथ भूमिप्रदेशज्ञास्सूत्रकर्मविशारदाः। स्वकर्माभिरताश्शूराः खनका यन्त्रकास्तथा।।2.80.1।। कर्मान्तिकाः स्थपतयः पुरुष यन्त्
transliteration: atha bhūmipradeśajñāssūtrakarmaviśāradāḥ| svakarmābhiratāśśūrāḥ khanakā yantrakāstathā||2.80.1|| karmāntikāḥ sthapatayḥ
meaning: Then surveyors, experts in measurment, energetic and zealous labourers, excavators, engineers, skilled workers, architects, craftsmen, carpenters, roadlevellers, woodcutters, welldiggers, whitewashers, basketmakers, comp

sanskrit: ततो नान्दीमुखीं रात्रिं भरतं सूतमागधाः। तुष्टुवुर्वाग्विशेषज्ञास्स्तवैर्मङ्गलसंहितैः।।2.81.1।।
transliteration: tato nāndīmukhīṃ rātriṃ bharatṃ sūtamāgadhāḥ| tuṣṭuvurvāgviśeṣajñāsstavairmaṅgalasṃhitaiḥ||2.81.1||
meaning: Thereafter bards and panegyrists adept in conversation with an auspicious start pleased Bharata with eulogy in the last part of the night.

sanskrit: तामार्यगणसम्पूर्णां भरतः प्रग्रहां सभाम्। ददर्श बुद्धिसम्पन्नः पूर्णचन्द्रो निशामिव।।2.82.1।।
transliteration: tāmāryagaṇasampūrṇāṃ bharatḥ pragrahāṃ sabhām| dadarśa buddhisampannḥ pūrṇacandro niśāmiva||2.82.1||
meaning: Sagacious Bharata beheld that assembly hall filled with honourable members, like the fullmoon beholds the night stretching forth (with stars).

sanskrit: तत स्समुत्थितः काल्यमास्थाय स्यन्दनोत्तमम्। प्रययौ भरतश्शीघ्रं रामदर्शनकाङ्क्षया।।2.83.1।।
transliteration: tata ssamutthitḥ kālyamāsthāya syandanottamam| prayayau bharataśśīghrṃ rāmadarśanakāṅkṣayā||2.83.1||
meaning: Getting up at dawn, Bharata boarded his excellent chariot and set forth swiftly, longing to see Rama.

sanskrit: ततो निविष्टां ध्वजिनीं गङ्गामन्वाश्रितां नदीम्। निषादराजो दृष्ट्वैव ज्ञातीन्सन्त्वरितोऽऽब्रवीत्।।2.84.1।।
transliteration: tato niviṣṭāṃ dhvajinīṃ gaṅgāmanvāśritāṃ nadīm| niṣādarājo dṛṣṭvaiva jñātīnsantvarito''bravīt||2.84.1||
meaning: Guha, king of the nishadas, observed the bannered army encamped all along the bank of the river Ganga, hurried off and said to his kinsmen:

sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो निषादाधिपतिं गुहम्। प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंहितम्।।2.85.1।।
transliteration: evamuktastu bharato niṣādādhipatiṃ guham| pratyuvāca mahāprājño vākyṃ hetvarthasṃhitam||2.85.1||
meaning: When thus spoken to, Bharata, a great intellectual, replied to Guha with these well thought out and meaningful words.

sanskrit: आचचक्षेऽथ सद्भावं लक्ष्मणस्य महात्मनः। भरतायाप्रमेयाय गुहो गहनगोचरः।।2.86.1।।
transliteration: ācacakṣe'tha sadbhāvṃ lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanḥ| bharatāyāprameyāya guho gahanagocarḥ||2.86.1||
meaning: Then Guha, the forest ranger, described to Bharata the countless qualities of the goodnatured, magnanimous Lakshmana:

sanskrit: गुहस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा भरतो भृशमप्रियम्। ध्यानं जगाम तत्रैव यत्र तच्छ्रुतमप्रियम्।।2.87.1।।
transliteration: guhasya vacanṃ śrutvā bharato bhṛśamapriyam| dhyānṃ jagāma tatraiva yatra tacchrutamapriyam||2.87.1||
meaning: Extremely unhappy over what he heard from Guha, Bharata was immersed in thought then and there.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा निपुणं सर्वं भरत स्सह मन्त्रिभिः। इङ्गुदीमूलमागम्य रामशय्यामवेक्ष्य ताम्।।2.88.1।। अब्रवीज्जननी स्सर्वा इह त
transliteration: tacchrutvā nipuṇṃ sarvṃ bharata ssaha mantribhiḥ| iṅgudīmūlamāgamya rāmaśayyāmavekṣya tām||2.88.1|| abravījjananī ssarvā
meaning: After listening to all that Guha had said, Bharatha reached the foot of the ingudi tree accompanied by his ministers and gazing at Rama's bed, said to all his mothers the magnanimous Rama rested that night here on this g

sanskrit: उष्य रात्रिं तु तत्रैव गङ्गाकूले स राघवः। भरतः काल्यमुत्थाय शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रवीत्।।2.89.1।।
transliteration: uṣya rātriṃ tu tatraiva gaṅgākūle sa rāghavḥ| bharatḥ kālyamutthāya śatrughnamidamabravīt||2.89.1||
meaning: Bharata got up at daybreak after spending the night on the bank of the Ganga at that very place where Rama, the descendent of Raghu, had stayed. And said these words to Satrughna:

sanskrit: भरद्वाजाश्रमं दृष्ट्वा क्रोशादेव नरर्षभः। बलं सर्वमवस्थाप्य जगाम सह मन्त्रिभिः।।2.90.1।। पद्भ्यामेव हि धर्मज्ञो न्यस्तशस
transliteration: bharadvājāśramṃ dṛṣṭvā krośādeva nararṣabhḥ| balṃ sarvamavasthāpya jagāma saha mantribhiḥ||2.90.1|| padbhyāmeva hi dharm
meaning: Bharata, the knower of righteous ways and the best among men, saw the hermitage of Bharadwaja from a distance of one krosa and brought his entire army to a halt. He laid aside all his royal robes and weapons. Clad in sil

sanskrit: कृतबुद्धिं निवासाय तत्रैव स मुनिस्तदा। भरतं कैकयीपुत्रमातिथ्येनन्यमन्त्रयत्।।2.91.1।।
transliteration: kṛtabuddhiṃ nivāsāya tatraiva sa munistadā| bharatṃ kaikayīputramātithyenanyamantrayat||2.91.1||
meaning: With the decision of Bharata, son of Kaikeyi, to stay there for the night, sage Bharadwaja extended to him all hospitality.

sanskrit: ततस्तां रजनीमुष्य भरतस्सपरिच्छदः। कृतातिथ्यो भरद्वाजं कामादभिजगाम ह।।2.92.1।।
transliteration: tatastāṃ rajanīmuṣya bharatassaparicchadḥ| kṛtātithyo bharadvājṃ kāmādabhijagāma ha||2.92.1||
meaning: Bharata with his retinue received the hospitality and spent the night at Bharadwaja's ashram. Then he approached Bharadwaja on his own.

sanskrit: तया महत्या यायिन्या ध्वजिन्या वनवासिनः। अर्दिता यूथपा मत्ताः सयूथास्सम्प्रदुद्रुवुः।।2.93.1।।
transliteration: tayā mahatyā yāyinyā dhvajinyā vanavāsinḥ| arditā yūthapā mattāḥ sayūthāssampradudruvuḥ||2.93.1||
meaning: On seeing the great army marching, the exited leaders of herds of elephants inhabiting the forest were frightened and ran off with their herds.

sanskrit: दीर्घकालोषित स्तस्मिन्गिरौ गिरिवनप्रियः। वैदेह्याः प्रियमाकाङ्क्षन्स्वं च चित्तं विलोभयन्।।2.94.1।। अथ दाशरथिश्चित्रं चि
transliteration: dīrghakāloṣita stasmingirau girivanapriyḥ| vaidehyāḥ priyamākāṅkṣansvṃ ca cittṃ vilobhayan||2.94.1|| atha dāśarathiścitr
meaning: Rama, resembling the gods, who had been living there for long developed a liking for the mountains and forests. With a desire to please Sita and his own mind, he showed her the wonderful Chitrakuta mountain as Indra did

sanskrit: अथ शैलाद्विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेश्वरः। अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम्।।2.95.1।।
transliteration: atha śailādviniṣkramya maithilīṃ kosaleśvarḥ| adarśayacchubhajalāṃ ramyāṃ mandākinīṃ nadīm||2.95.1||
meaning: Then Rama, the lord of Kosala, descended from the mountain and showed Sita the charming river Mandakini of sacred waters.

sanskrit: तां तथा दर्शयित्वा तु मैथिलीं गिरिनिम्नगाम्। निषसाद गिरिप्रस्थे सीतां मांसेन छन्दयन्।।2.96.1।।
transliteration: tāṃ tathā darśayitvā tu maithilīṃ girinimnagām| niṣasāda giriprasthe sītāṃ māṃsena chandayan||2.96.1||
meaning: Rama showed Sita, the princess of Mithila the river Mandakini flowing in the mountain, gratified her by offering meat (to eat) and sat on the mountain slope.

sanskrit: सुसंरब्धं तु सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं क्रोधमूर्छितम्। रामस्तु परिसान्त्व्याथ वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्।।2.97.1।।
transliteration: susṃrabdhṃ tu saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇṃ krodhamūrchitam| rāmastu parisāntvyātha vacanṃ cedamabravīt||2.97.1||
meaning: Thereafter, Rama pacified Lakshmana, son of Sumitra who was violently agitated. He said to him who had swooned with rage:

sanskrit: निवेश्य सेनां तु विभुः पद्भ्यां पादवतां वरः। अभिगन्तुं स काकुत्थ्समियेष गुरुवर्तकम्।।2.98.1।।
transliteration: niveśya senāṃ tu vibhuḥ padbhyāṃ pādavatāṃ varḥ| abhigantuṃ sa kākutthsamiyeṣa guruvartakam||2.98.1||
meaning: On encamping the army, lord Bharata, the best among men, wished to approach on foot Rama who was devoted to his father.

sanskrit: निविष्टायां तु सेनायामुत्सुको भरतस्तदा। जगाम भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं शत्रुघ्नमनुदर्शयन्।।2.99.1।।
transliteration: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastadā| jagāma bhrātarṃ draṣṭuṃ śatrughnamanudarśayan||2.99.1||
meaning: Eager to see his brother, Bharata encamped the army and set out showing the hermitage to Satrughna.

sanskrit: तपस्स्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् । नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् ।।1.1.1।।
transliteration: tapassvādhyāyanirataṁ tapasvī vāgvidāṁ varam। nāradaṁ paripapraccha vālmīkir munipuṅgavam।।
meaning: Ascetic Valmiki enquired of Narada, preeminent among the sages ever engaged in the practice of religious austerities or study of the Vedas and best among the eloquent.

sanskrit: सुमन्त्रश्चोदितो राज्ञा प्रोवाचेदं वचस्तदा। यथर्श्यशृङ्गस्त्वानीत श्श्रुणु मे मन्त्रिभिस्सह।।1.10.1।।
transliteration: sumantraścodito rājñā provācedṃ vacastadā| yatharśyaśṛṅgastvānīta śśruṇu me mantribhissaha||1.10.1||
meaning: Thus prompted by king Dasaratha, Sumantra said, "I shall relate to you the manner in which Rsyasringa was brought to the court. Listen to me along with your ministers".

sanskrit: भूय एव हि राजेन्द्र शृणु मे वचनं हितम्। यथा स देवप्रवर: कथायामेवमब्रवीत्।।1.11.1।।
transliteration: bhūya eva hi rājendra śṛṇu me vacanṃ hitam| yathā sa devapravara: kathāyāmevamabravīt||1.11.1||
meaning: "Great king, I shall tell you the way Sanatkumara, great among the celestials further narrated the story. Listen to my words which may prove useful to you (said Sumantra)".

sanskrit: तत: काले बहुतिथे कस्मिंश्चित्सुमनोहरे। वसन्ते समनुप्राप्ते राज्ञो यष्टुं मनोऽभवत्।।1.12.1।।
transliteration: tata: kāle bahutithe kasmiṃścitsumanohare| vasante samanuprāpte rājño yaṣṭuṃ mano'bhavat||1.12.1||
meaning: After a long time, at the advent of charming spring a desire arose in the mind of the king (Dasaratha) to perform the sacrifice.

sanskrit: पुन: प्राप्ते वसन्ते तु पूर्णस्संवत्सरोऽभवत्। प्रसवार्थं गतो यष्टुं हयमेधेन वीर्यवान्।।1.13.1।।
transliteration: puna: prāpte vasante tu pūrṇassṃvatsaro'bhavat| prasavārthṃ gato yaṣṭuṃ hayamedhena vīryavān||1.13.1||
meaning: After completion of one year when spring returned, the valiant king (Dasaratha) entered the sacrificial pavilion to worship celestial beings for begetting sons.

sanskrit: अथ संवत्सरे पूर्णे तस्मिन्प्राप्ते तुरङ्गमे। सरय्वाश्चोत्तरे तीरे राज्ञो यज्ञोऽभ्यवर्तत।।1.14.1।।
transliteration: atha sṃvatsare pūrṇe tasminprāpte turaṅgame| sarayvāścottare tīre rājño yajño'bhyavartata||1.14.1||
meaning: After completion of one year when the sacrificial horse had returned, the sacrifice by the king (Dasaratha) commenced on the northern bank of river Sarayu.

sanskrit: मेथावी तु ततो ध्यात्वा स किञ्चिदिदमुत्तरम्। लब्धसंज्ञस्ततस्तं तु वेदज्ञो नृपमब्रवीत्।।1.15.1।।
transliteration: methāvī tu tato dhyātvā sa kiñcididamuttaram| labdhasṃjñastatastṃ tu vedajño nṛpamabravīt||1.15.1||
meaning: Rsyasringa, a highly intellectual and knowledgeable one in the Vedas, pondered for a while, revived his memory and said to the king.

sanskrit: ततो नारायणो देवो नियुक्तस्सुरसत्तमै:। जानन्नपि सुरानेवं श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रवीत्।।1.16.1।।
transliteration: tato nārāyaṇo devo niyuktassurasattamai:| jānannapi surānevṃ ślakṣṇṃ vacanamabravīt||1.16.1||
meaning: Although Omniscient lord Narayana knew the means to be employed, when he was requested by the best of devatas he spoke to them softly:

sanskrit: पुत्रत्वं तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञस्तस्य सुमहात्मन:। उवाच देवतास्सर्वास्स्वयम्भूर्भगवानिदम्।।1.17.1।।
transliteration: putratvṃ tu gate viṣṇau rājñastasya sumahātmana:| uvāca devatāssarvāssvayambhūrbhagavānidam||1.17.1||
meaning: When Visnu had decided to be born as the son of that great king (Dasaratha), the selfborn Lord (Brahma), addressed all devatas :

sanskrit: निर्वृत्ते तु क्रतौ तस्मिन्हयमेधे महात्मन:। प्रतिगृह्य सुरा भागान्प्रतिजग्मुर्यथागतम्।।1.18.1।।
transliteration: nirvṛtte tu kratau tasminhayamedhe mahātmana:| pratigṛhya surā bhāgānpratijagmuryathāgatam||1.18.1||
meaning: Completed by the magnanimous king (Dasaratha). The aswamedha and putreshti sacrifices, the devatas received their share of havis and returned to their respective abodes.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा राजसिंहस्य वाक्यमद्भुतविस्तरम्। हृष्टरोमा महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.19.1।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rājasiṃhasya vākyamadbhutavistaram| hṛṣṭaromā mahātejā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata||1.19.1||
meaning: Having heard these wonderful words of Dasaratha, the lion among kings, the brilliant Viswamitra with hair on end replied:

sanskrit: नारदस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वाक्यविशारद:। पूजयामास धर्मात्मा सहशिष्यो महामुनि: ।।1.2.1।।
transliteration: nāradasya tu tadvākyṃ śrutvā vākyaviśārada:| pūjayāmāsa dharmātmā sahaśiṣyo mahāmuni: ||1.2.1||
meaning: On hearing the words of Narada the distinguished and righteous sage Valmiki, proficient in composing slokas worshipped him along with his disciples.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा राजशार्दूलो विश्वामित्रस्य भाषितम्। मुहूर्तमिव निस्संज्ञस्संज्ञावानिदमब्रवीत्।।1.20.1।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā rājaśārdūlo viśvāmitrasya bhāṣitam| muhūrtamiva nissṃjñassṃjñāvānidamabravīt||1.20.1||
meaning: On hearing Viswamitra, words the tiger among kings (Dasaratha) lost his senses for a moment and on regaining his consciousness spoke this way.

sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य स्नेहपर्याकुलाक्षरम्। समन्यु: कौशिको वाक्यं प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम्।।1.21.1।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā vacanṃ tasya snehaparyākulākṣaram| samanyu: kauśiko vākyṃ pratyuvāca mahīpatim||1.21.1||
meaning: Out of affection towards his son, his (king Dasaratha's) plea to Viswamitra was full of contradiction. And on hearing the king, enraged Viswamitra replied:

sanskrit: तथा वसिष्ठे ब्रुवति राजा दशरथस्सुतम प्रहृष्टवदनो राममाजुहाव सलक्ष्मणम्।।1.22.1।।
transliteration: tathā vasiṣṭhe bruvati rājā daśarathassutama prahṛṣṭavadano rāmamājuhāva salakṣmaṇam||1.22.1||
meaning: Vasishta having said thus, king Dasaratha, with cheerful countenance summoned Rama and Lakshmana.

sanskrit: प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:। अभ्यभाषत काकुत्स्थौ शयानौ पर्णसंस्तरे।।1.23.1।।
transliteration: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuni:| abhyabhāṣata kākutsthau śayānau parṇasṃstare||1.23.1||
meaning: When the night turned into daybreak, the eminent ascetic Viswamitra, addressing the descendants of Kakutstha (Rama and Lakshmana) who were lying on a bed of leaves said:

sanskrit: तत: प्रभाते विमले कृताह्निकमरिन्दमौ। विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य नद्यास्तीरमुपागतौ।।1.24.1।।
transliteration: tata: prabhāte vimale kṛtāhnikamarindamau| viśvāmitrṃ puraskṛtya nadyāstīramupāgatau||1.24.1||
meaning: Thereafter the destroyers of foes, Rama and Lakshmana offering their morning oblations on that bright dawn arrived at the bank of the river (Ganga) with Viswamitra ahead of them.

sanskrit: अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य मुनेर्वचनमुत्तमम्। श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूल: प्रत्युवाच शुभां गिरम्।।1.25.1।।
transliteration: atha tasyāprameyasya munervacanamuttamam| śrutvā puruṣaśārdūla: pratyuvāca śubhāṃ giram||1.25.1||
meaning: On hearing the excellent words of Viswamitra, a sage with unimaginable faculty. Rama, the tiger among men (Rama) replied in a, gentle voice:

sanskrit: मुनेर्वचनमक्लीबं श्रुत्वा नरवरात्मज:। राघव: प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच दृढव्रत:।।1.26.1।।
transliteration: munervacanamaklībṃ śrutvā naravarātmaja:| rāghava: prāñjalirbhūtvā pratyuvāca dṛḍhavrata:||1.26.1||
meaning: After listening to the manly command of ascetic Viswamitra, Rama, of the lineage of Raghu, the son of the foremost of men and firm in determination, replied with folded palms:

sanskrit: अथ तां रजनीमुष्य विश्वामित्रो महायशाः। प्रहस्य राघवं वाक्यमुवाच मधुराक्षरम्।।1.27.1।।
transliteration: atha tāṃ rajanīmuṣya viśvāmitro mahāyaśāḥ| prahasya rāghavṃ vākyamuvāca madhurākṣaram||1.27.1||
meaning: The night over, illustrious Viswamitra called Rama with a sweet smile.

sanskrit: प्रतिगृह्य ततोऽस्त्राणि प्रहृष्टवदनश्शुचि:। गच्छन्नेव च काकुत्स्थो विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्।।1.28.1।।
transliteration: pratigṛhya tato'strāṇi prahṛṣṭavadanaśśuci:| gacchanneva ca kākutstho viśvāmitramathābravīt||1.28.1||
meaning: After performing the purificatory rites, Rama received the weapons with a cheerful face. In the way Rama said to Viswamitra.

sanskrit: अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य तद्वनं परिपृच्छत:। विश्वामित्रो महातेजा व्याख्यातुमुपचक्रमे।।1.29.1।।
transliteration: atha tasyāprameyasya tadvanṃ paripṛcchata:| viśvāmitro mahātejā vyākhyātumupacakrame||1.29.1||
meaning: The highly lustrous Viswamitra heard the words of Rama of immeasurable prowess. On his (Rama's) query about the forest, Viswamitra explains.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा वस्तु समग्रं तद्धर्मात्मा धर्मसंहितम् । व्यक्तमन्वेषते भूयो यद्वृत्तं तस्य धीमत: ।।1.3.1।।
transliteration: śrutvā vastu samagrṃ taddharmātmā dharmasṃhitam | vyaktamanveṣate bhūyo yadvṛttṃ tasya dhīmata: ||1.3.1||
meaning: Hearing the entire story of Rama from the intellecual Narada, the righteous (Valmiki) sought to know clearly more about the history of Rama endowed with wisdom.

sanskrit: अथ तौ देशकालज्ञौ राजापुत्रावरिन्दमौ। देशे काले च वाक्यज्ञावब्रूतां कौशिकं वच:।।1.30.1।।
transliteration: atha tau deśakālajñau rājāputrāvarindamau| deśe kāle ca vākyajñāvabrūtāṃ kauśikṃ vaca:||1.30.1||
meaning: Thus spoke the two princes to Viswamitra. They were conscious of place and time to speak and capable of conquering enemies.

sanskrit: अथ तां रजनीं तत्र कृतार्थौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। ऊषतुर्मुदितौ वीरौ प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना।।1.31.1।।
transliteration: atha tāṃ rajanīṃ tatra kṛtārthau rāmalakṣmaṇau| ūṣaturmuditau vīrau prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā||1.31.1||
meaning: There, with their purpose fulfilled the heroes, Rama and Lakshmana, full of joy in their hearts spent the night.

sanskrit: [Description of the four sons of Brahma and the dynasty of Kusanabha-- enraged Windgod turns the daughters of Kusanabha
transliteration: [Description of the four sons of Brahma and the dynasty of Kusanabha-- enraged Windgod turns the daughters of Kusanabha
meaning: There was a great ascetic named Kusa, born to Brahma, as ascetic indefatigable in vows, knowldegeable in dharma and a respector of the virtuous.

sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कुशनाभस्य धीमत:। शिरोभिश्चरणौ स्पृष्ट्वा कन्याशतमभाषत।।1.33.1।।
transliteration: tasya tadvacanṃ śrutvā kuśanābhasya dhīmata:| śirobhiścaraṇau spṛṣṭvā kanyāśatamabhāṣata||1.33.1||
meaning: On hearing the words of sagacious Kusanabha, his hundred daughters touched his feet with their heads and said:

sanskrit: कृतोद्वाहे गते तस्मिन् ब्रह्मदत्ते च राघव। अपुत्र: पुत्रलाभाय पौत्रीमिष्टिमकल्पयत्।।1.34.1।।
transliteration: kṛtodvāhe gate tasmin brahmadatte ca rāghava| aputra: putralābhāya pautrīmiṣṭimakalpayat||1.34.1||
meaning: "O son of Raghu's dynasty (Rama) Brahmadatta got married and left for his kingdom. Now a putreshti was performed by king Kusanabha in order to beget a son.

sanskrit: उपास्य रात्रिशेषं तु शोणाकूले महर्षिभि:। निशायां सुप्रभातायां विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.35.1।।
transliteration: upāsya rātriśeṣṃ tu śoṇākūle maharṣibhi:| niśāyāṃ suprabhātāyāṃ viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata||1.35.1||
meaning: Viswamitra lay on the bank of Sona with the ascetics, for the rest of the night. (Getting up) at daybreak he said:

sanskrit: उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन्नुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ। प्रतिनन्द्य कथां वीरावूचतुर्मुनिपुङ्गवम्।।1.36.1।।
transliteration: uktavākye munau tasminnubhau rāghavalakṣmaṇau| pratinandya kathāṃ vīrāvūcaturmunipuṅgavam||1.36.1||
meaning: While Viswamitra preeminent ascetic among the sages was telling the story (of Ganga) to the heroic Rama and Lakshmana, they extolled it and enquired:

sanskrit: तप्यमाने तपो देवे देवा: सर्षिगणा: पुरा। सेनापतिमभीप्सन्त: पितामहमुपागमन्।।1.37.1।।
transliteration: tapyamāne tapo deve devā: sarṣigaṇā: purā| senāpatimabhīpsanta: pitāmahamupāgaman||1.37.1||
meaning: In olden days when Iswara was engaged in austerities, the devatas together with the ascetics, approached Lord Brahma for an army general.

sanskrit: तां कथां कौशिको रामे निवेद्य कुशिकात्मज:। पुनरेवापरं वाक्यं काकुत्स्थ मिदमब्रवीत्।।1.38.1।।
transliteration: tāṃ kathāṃ kauśiko rāme nivedya kuśikātmaja:| punarevāparṃ vākyṃ kākutstha midamabravīt||1.38.1||
meaning: Viswamitra, an offspring of Kusika having related the story (of Karthikeya) to the son of the Kakusthas (Rama) said again.

sanskrit: विश्वामित्रवचश्श्रुत्वा कथाऽन्ते रघुनन्दन:। उवाच परमप्रीतो मुनिं दीप्तमिवानलम्।।1.39.1।।
transliteration: viśvāmitravacaśśrutvā kathā'nte raghunandana:| uvāca paramaprīto muniṃ dīptamivānalam||1.39.1||
meaning: Immensely pleased with the words of Viswamitra, to the ascetic flaming bright like fire, Rama spoke towards the end of the narration:

sanskrit: प्राप्तराज्यस्य रामस्य वाल्मीकिर्भगवानृषि:। चकार चरितं कृत्स्नं विचित्रपदमात्मवान्।।1.4.1।।
transliteration: prāptarājyasya rāmasya vālmīkirbhagavānṛṣi:| cakāra caritṃ kṛtsnṃ vicitrapadamātmavān||1.4.1||
meaning: The divine sage Valmiki, composed in wonderful lines the entire lifestory of Rama who regained his kingdom.

sanskrit: . देवतानां वचश्श्रुत्वा भगवान्वै पितामह:। प्रत्युवाच सुसन्त्रस्तान्कृतान्तबलमोहितान्।।1.40.1।।
transliteration: . devatānāṃ vacaśśrutvā bhagavānvai pitāmaha:| pratyuvāca susantrastānkṛtāntabalamohitān||1.40.1||
meaning: Having heard the devatas, extremely frightened, and deprived of their sensual perception by the prowess of fate. The adorable grandsire (Brahma) replied:

sanskrit: पुत्रांश्चिरगतान् ज्ञात्वा सगरो रघुनन्दन। नप्तारमब्रवीद्राजा दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा।।1.41.1।।
transliteration: putrāṃściragatān jñātvā sagaro raghunandana| naptāramabravīdrājā dīpyamānṃ svatejasā||1.41.1||
meaning: "O Delight of the Raghus, king Sagara, realising that his sons had left long ago said to his grandson Anshuman resplendent with his own lustre:

sanskrit: कालधर्मं गते राम सगरे प्रकृतीजना:। राजानं रोचयामासुरंशुमन्तं सुधार्मिकम्।।1.42.1।।
transliteration: kāladharmṃ gate rāma sagare prakṛtījanā:| rājānṃ rocayāmāsurṃśumantṃ sudhārmikam||1.42.1||
meaning: "O Rama when Sagara died, the subjects installed the highly virtuous Anshuman as king.

sanskrit: देवदेवे गते तस्मिन् सोऽङ्गुष्ठाग्रनिपीडिताम्। कृत्वा वसुमतीं राम संवत्सरमुपासत।।1.43.1।।
transliteration: devadeve gate tasmin so'ṅguṣṭhāgranipīḍitām| kṛtvā vasumatīṃ rāma sṃvatsaramupāsata||1.43.1||
meaning: "O Rama when that God of the gods (Brahma) departed, Bhagiratha, pressing the earth with the tip of his big toe (standing supported by the big toe) penanced (meditated upon Siva) for one year.

sanskrit: स गत्वा सागरं राजा गङ्गयाऽनुगतस्तदा । प्रविवेश तलं भूमेर्यत्र ते भस्मसात्कृता:।।1.44.1।।
transliteration: sa gatvā sāgarṃ rājā gaṅgayā'nugatastadā | praviveśa talṃ bhūmeryatra te bhasmasātkṛtā:||1.44.1||
meaning: Thereupon that king followed by Ganga reached the ocean and entered the lower regions of the earth where the sons of Sagara were found reduced to ashes.

sanskrit: विश्वामित्रवचश्श्रुत्वा राघव स्सहलक्ष्मण:। विस्मयं परमं गत्वा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्।।1.45.1।।
transliteration: viśvāmitravacaśśrutvā rāghava ssahalakṣmaṇa:| vismayṃ paramṃ gatvā viśvāmitramathābravīt||1.45.1||
meaning: On hearing the words of Viswamitra, Rama along with Lakshmana, filled with astonishment said to him:

sanskrit: हतेषु तेषु पुत्रेषु दिति: परमदु:खिता। मारीचं काश्यपं राम भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्।।1.46.1।।
transliteration: hateṣu teṣu putreṣu diti: paramadu:khitā| mārīcṃ kāśyapṃ rāma bhartāramidamabravīt||1.46.1||
meaning: "O Rama! afflicted with great grief when her sons were killed, Diti said to her husband Kasyapa, son of Maricha:

sanskrit: सप्तधातु कृते गर्भे दिति: परमदु:खिता। सहस्राक्षं दुराधर्षं वाक्यं सानुनयाऽब्रवीत्।।1.47.1।।
transliteration: saptadhātu kṛte garbhe diti: paramadu:khitā| sahasrākṣṃ durādharṣṃ vākyṃ sānunayā'bravīt||1.47.1||
meaning: Deeply distressed Diti, having come to know that the embryo had been severed into seven pieces, humbly spoke to the unassailable Indra.

sanskrit: पृष्ट्वा तु कुशलं तत्र परस्परसमागमे। कथान्ते सुमतिर्वाक्यं व्याजहार महामुनिम्।।1.48.1।।
transliteration: pṛṣṭvā tu kuśalṃ tatra parasparasamāgame| kathānte sumatirvākyṃ vyājahāra mahāmunim||1.48.1||
meaning: Getting together they enquired one another's health. And then Sumati spoke to the great ascetic (Viswamitra).

sanskrit: अफलस्तु ततश्शक्रो देवानग्निपुरोगमान्। अब्रवीत्त्रस्तवदनस्सर्षिस्सङ्घान् सचारणान्।।1.49.1।।
transliteration: aphalastu tataśśakro devānagnipurogamān| abravīttrastavadanassarṣissaṅghān sacāraṇān||1.49.1||
meaning: Deprived of testicles, Indra with a frightened face addressed hordes of rishis and charanas with agni in the forefront.

sanskrit: . सर्वा पूर्वमियं येषामासीत्कृत्स्ना वसुन्धरा । प्रजापतिमुपादाय नृपाणां जयशालिनाम् ।।1.5.1।।
transliteration: . sarvā pūrvamiyṃ yeṣāmāsītkṛtsnā vasundharā | prajāpatimupādāya nṛpāṇāṃ jayaśālinām ||1.5.1||
meaning: Formerly, this entire earth belonged to those victorious kings starting from Prajapati (Manu).

sanskrit: तत: प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा रामस्सौमित्रिणा सह। विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञवाटमुपागमत्।।1.50.1।।
transliteration: tata: prāguttarāṃ gatvā rāmassaumitriṇā saha| viśvāmitrṃ puraskṛtya yajñavāṭamupāgamat||1.50.1||
meaning: Rama accompanied by Lakshmana with Viswamitra ahead proceeded in northeasterly direction and reached the sacrificial ground.

sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रस्य धीमत:। हृष्टरोमा महातेजाश्शतानन्दो महातपा:।।1.51.1।। गौतमस्य सुतो ज्येष्ठस्तपसा द्य
transliteration: tasya tadvacanṃ śrutvā viśvāmitrasya dhīmata:| hṛṣṭaromā mahātejāśśatānando mahātapā:||1.51.1|| gautamasya suto jyeṣṭhas
meaning: Satananda the eldest son of Gautama, a great sage who looked brilliant with the power of austerities was thrilled to hear the words of Viswamitra the intellectual and experienced great astonishment on beholding Rama.

sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रो महाबल:। प्रणतो विनयाद्वीरो वसिष्ठं जपतां वरम्।।1.52.1।।
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā paramaprīto viśvāmitro mahābala:| praṇato vinayādvīro vasiṣṭhṃ japatāṃ varam||1.52.1||
meaning: Overwhelmed with joy the mighty, heroic Viswamitra upon seeing Vasishta, the greatest among ascetics, was and offered respectful salutations.

sanskrit: एवमुक्ता वसिष्ठेन शबला शत्रुसूदन। विदधे कामधुक्कामान्यस्य यस्य यथेप्सितम्।।1.53.1।।
transliteration: evamuktā vasiṣṭhena śabalā śatrusūdana| vidadhe kāmadhukkāmānyasya yasya yathepsitam||1.53.1||
meaning: "O Destroyer of foes (Rama)" addressed thus by Vasishta the wishfulfilling Sabala satisfied each one's desires.

sanskrit: कामधेनुं वसिष्ठोऽपि यदा न त्यज्यते मुनि:। तदास्य शबलां राम विश्वामित्रोऽन्वकर्षत।।1.54.1।।
transliteration: kāmadhenuṃ vasiṣṭho'pi yadā na tyajyate muni:| tadāsya śabalāṃ rāma viśvāmitro'nvakarṣata||1.54.1||
meaning: "O Rama when sage Vasishta did not consent to part with the wishfulfilling cow, Viswamitra dragged Sabala by force.

sanskrit: ततस्तानाकुलान् दृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रास्त्रमोहितान्। वसिष्ठश्चोदयामास कामधुक् सृज योगत:।।1.55.1।।
transliteration: tatastānākulān dṛṣṭvā viśvāmitrāstramohitān| vasiṣṭhaścodayāmāsa kāmadhuk sṛja yogata:||1.55.1||
meaning: Thereafter, Vasishta having seen the forces tortured and overpowered by the weapons of Viswamitra said, "O Kamadhenu create additional forces through your yogic power."

sanskrit: एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन विश्वामित्रो महाबल:। आग्नेयमस्त्रमुत्क्षिप्य तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत्।।1.56.1।।
transliteration: evamukto vasiṣṭhena viśvāmitro mahābala:| āgneyamastramutkṣipya tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt||1.56.1||
meaning: Thus said Vasishta. Mighty Viswamitra lifted up agneya astra (shaft of fire) and discharging it said, 'stay, stay'.

sanskrit: ततस्सन्तप्तहृदय: स्मरन्निग्रहमात्मन:। विनिश्श्वस्य विनिश्श्वस्य कृतवैरो महत्मना।।1.57.1।। स दक्षिणां दिशं गत्वा महिष्या
transliteration: tatassantaptahṛdaya: smarannigrahamātmana:| viniśśvasya viniśśvasya kṛtavairo mahatmanā||1.57.1|| sa dakṣiṇāṃ diśṃ gatvā
meaning: "O Descendant of Raghu (Rama) having created enmity between himself and the magnanimous Vasishta, Viswamitra recollecting the disgrace and repeatedly sighing with a distressed heart went with his eldest wife towards sout

sanskrit: ततस्त्रिशङ्कोर्वचनं श्रुत्वा क्रोधसमन्वितम् । ऋषिपुत्रशतं राम राजानमिदमब्रवीत्।।1.58.1।।
transliteration: tatastriśaṅkorvacanṃ śrutvā krodhasamanvitam | ṛṣiputraśatṃ rāma rājānamidamabravīt||1.58.1||
meaning: "O Rama to these words of king Trisanku, the hundred sons of the sage angrily reacted:

sanskrit: उक्तवाक्यं तु राजानं कृपया कुशिकात्मज:। अब्रवीन्मधुरं वाक्यं साक्षाच्चण्डालरूपिणम्।।1.59.1।।
transliteration: uktavākyṃ tu rājānṃ kṛpayā kuśikātmaja:| abravīnmadhurṃ vākyṃ sākṣāccaṇḍālarūpiṇam||1.59.1||
meaning: What the king said was proved by his chandala form which the son of Kushika (Viswamitra) heard and out of compassion spoke these sweet words:

sanskrit: . तस्यां पुर्यामयोध्यायां वेदवित्सर्वसङ्ग्रह: । दीर्घदर्शी महातेजा: पौरजानपदप्रिय: ।।1.6.1।। इक्ष्वाकूणामतिरथो यज्वा धर्
transliteration: . tasyāṃ puryāmayodhyāyāṃ vedavitsarvasaṅgraha: | dīrghadarśī mahātejā: paurajānapadapriya: ||1.6.1|| ikṣvākūṇāmatiratho
meaning: From that city of Ayodhya, king Dasaratha ruled the entire world, following the tradition of Manu who was a highly powerful protector of the people. Dasaratha was well versed in the Vedas. He commanded all resources. Far

sanskrit: तपोबलहतान् कृत्वा वासिष्ठान् समहोदयान्। ऋषिमध्ये महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत।।1.60.1।।
transliteration: tapobalahatān kṛtvā vāsiṣṭhān samahodayān| ṛṣimadhye mahātejā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata||1.60.1||
meaning: The most brilliant Viswamitra, having destroyed the sons of Vasishta including Mahodaya by his ascetic power, said this in the midst of saints:

sanskrit: विश्वामित्रो महात्माथ प्रस्थितान् प्रेक्ष्य तानृषीन्। अब्रवीन्नरशार्दूलस्सर्वांस्तान्वनवासिन:।।1.61.1।।
transliteration: viśvāmitro mahātmātha prasthitān prekṣya tānṛṣīn| abravīnnaraśārdūlassarvāṃstānvanavāsina:||1.61.1||
meaning: O Tiger among men (Rama) thereafter great Viswamitra seeing the departing sages of the forest said:

sanskrit: शुनश्शेफं नरश्रेष्ठ गृहीत्वा तु महायशा:। व्यश्राम्यत् पुष्करे राजा मध्याह्ने रघुनन्दन।।1.62.1।।
transliteration: śunaśśephṃ naraśreṣṭha gṛhītvā tu mahāyaśā:| vyaśrāmyat puṣkare rājā madhyāhne raghunandana||1.62.1||
meaning: O Foremost of men, O Delight of the Raghus (Rama) the illustrious king (Ambarisha) took Sunassepha with him. (On the way) at Pushkara he took some rest at noon.

sanskrit: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु व्रतस्नातं महामुनिम्। अभ्यागच्छन् सुरास्सर्वे तप: फलचिकीर्षव:।।1.63.1।।
transliteration: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu vratasnātṃ mahāmunim| abhyāgacchan surāssarve tapa: phalacikīrṣava:||1.63.1||
meaning: All the gods wanted to bestow the fruits of austerties on the mighty ascetic (Viswamitra). They approached him after a thousand years of penace and his final ritual bath.

sanskrit: सुरकार्यमिदं रम्भे कर्तव्यं सुमहत्त्वया। लोभनं कौशिकस्येह काममोहसमन्वितम्।।1.64.1।।
transliteration: surakāryamidṃ rambhe kartavyṃ sumahattvayā| lobhanṃ kauśikasyeha kāmamohasamanvitam||1.64.1||
meaning: "O Rambha you must entice Viswamitra by lust and passion. This important work must be done by you in the interest of the gods".

sanskrit: अथ हैमवतीं राम दिशं त्यक्त्वा महामुनि:। पूर्वां दिशमनुप्राप्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्।।1.65.1।।
transliteration: atha haimavatīṃ rāma diśṃ tyaktvā mahāmuni:| pūrvāṃ diśamanuprāpya tapastepe sudāruṇam||1.65.1||
meaning: "O Rama thereafter the great ascetic (Viswamitra), abandoning the north of the Himavat mountain reached the eastern quarter and performed rigorous austerities.

sanskrit: तत: प्रभाते विमले कृतकर्मा नराधिप:। विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं आजुहाव सराघवम्।।1.66.1।।
transliteration: tata: prabhāte vimale kṛtakarmā narādhipa:| viśvāmitrṃ mahātmānṃ ājuhāva sarāghavam||1.66.1||
meaning: The day dawned bright and clear when the king (Janaka) performed his daily routine rites and welcomed the great Viswamitra with the two Raghavas (Rama and Lakshmana).

sanskrit: . जनकस्य वचश्श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनि: । धनुर्दर्शय रामाय इति होवाच पार्थिवम्।।1.67.1।।
transliteration: . janakasya vacaśśrutvā viśvāmitro mahāmuni: | dhanurdarśaya rāmāya iti hovāca pārthivam||1.67.1||
meaning: At the words of Janaka, great ascetic Viswamitra said to the king, "Let the bow be shown to Rama".

sanskrit: जनकेन समादिष्टा दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहना:। त्रिरात्रमुषिता मार्गे तेऽयोध्यां प्राविशन् पुरीम्।।1.68.1।।
transliteration: janakena samādiṣṭā dūtāste klāntavāhanā:| trirātramuṣitā mārge te'yodhyāṃ prāviśan purīm||1.68.1||
meaning: Commanded by Janaka the messengers travelled for three days, rested for three nights on the way and entered the city of Ayodhya along with their horses tired.

sanskrit: ततो रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां सोपाध्याय: सबान्धव:। राजा दशरथो हृष्ट स्सुमन्त्रमिदमब्रवीत्।।1.69.1।।
transliteration: tato rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ sopādhyāya: sabāndhava:| rājā daśaratho hṛṣṭa ssumantramidamabravīt||1.69.1||
meaning: With the passing of the night king Dasaratha, accompanied by spiritual preceptors and relatives said to Sumantra:

sanskrit: . तस्यामात्या गुणैरासन्निक्ष्वाकोस्तु महात्मन: । मन्त्रज्ञाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च नित्यं प्रियहिते रता: ।।1.7.1।।
transliteration: . tasyāmātyā guṇairāsannikṣvākostu mahātmana: | mantrajñāśceṅgitajñāśca nityṃ priyahite ratā: ||1.7.1||
meaning: The ministers of the great descendent of the Ikshvakus were endowed with all virtues. They were competent counsellors, skilled in judging motives from facial features and were always intent on doing good and all that was

sanskrit: तत: प्रभाते जनक: कृतकर्मा महर्षिभि:। उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञ श्शतानन्दं पुरोहितम्।।1.70.1।।
transliteration: tata: prabhāte janaka: kṛtakarmā maharṣibhi:| uvāca vākyṃ vākyajña śśatānandṃ purohitam||1.70.1||
meaning: Thereafter at dawn after the maharshis had performed their daily (sacrificial) rites the eloquent Janaka said to the chief priest Satananda:

sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं जनक: प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलि:। श्रोतुमर्हसि भद्रं ते कुलं न: परिकीर्तितम्।।1.71.1।।
transliteration: evṃ bruvāṇṃ janaka: pratyuvāca kṛtāñjali:| śrotumarhasi bhadrṃ te kulṃ na: parikīrtitam||1.71.1||
meaning: Vasishta having thus described (the genealogy of Dasaratha) Janaka with folded hands rejoined, "Be blessed. Let me relate the genealogy of my race. Listen".

sanskrit: तमुक्तवन्तं वैदेहं विश्वामित्रो महामुनि:। उवाच वचनं वीरं वसिष्ठसहितो नृपम्।।1.72.1।।
transliteration: tamuktavantṃ vaidehṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuni:| uvāca vacanṃ vīrṃ vasiṣṭhasahito nṛpam||1.72.1||
meaning: When Janaka the valiant king of Videha thus spoke (on the genealogy of his family) the mighty ascetic Viswamitra accompanied by Vasishta said to Janaka:

sanskrit: यस्मिंस्तु दिवसे राजा चक्रे गोदानमुत्तमम् । तस्मिं स्तु दिवसे शूरो युधाजित्समुपेयिवान्।।1.73.1।।
transliteration: yasmiṃstu divase rājā cakre godānamuttamam	| tasmiṃ stu divase śūro yudhājitsamupeyivān||1.73.1||
meaning: The day the king (Dasaratha) made a gift of the best (available) cows the heroic Yudhajit arrived.

sanskrit: अथ रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः। आपृष्ट्वा तौ च राजानौ जगामोत्तरपर्वतम् ।।1.74.1।। आशीर्भि: पूरयित्वा च कु
transliteration: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ| āpṛṣṭvā tau ca rājānau jagāmottaraparvatam	||1.74.1|| āśīrbhi: pūrayitvā c
meaning: Night over, the great ascetic Viswamitra, profusely blessed the princes born in the race of Raghu, took leave of the two kings and set out towards the northern (Himalayas) mountains.

sanskrit: राम दाशरथे राम वीर्यं ते श्रूयतेऽद्भुतम्। धनुषो भेदनं चैव निखिलेन मया श्रुतम्।।1.75.1।।
transliteration: rāma dāśarathe rāma vīryṃ te śrūyate'dbhutam| dhanuṣo bhedanṃ caiva nikhilena mayā śrutam||1.75.1||
meaning: "O Rama, Rama, son of Dasaratha I have heard in full of your marvellous prowess and your feat in breaking the bow of Siva.

sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तज्जामदग्न्यस्य वाक्यं दाशरथिस्तदा। गौरवाद्यंन्त्रितकथ: पितू राममथाब्रवीत्।।1.76.1।।
transliteration: śrutvā tajjāmadagnyasya vākyṃ dāśarathistadā| gauravādyṃntritakatha: pitū rāmamathābravīt||1.76.1||
meaning: Hearing the words of the son of Jamadagni (Parasurama), Rama, the son of Dasaratha, avoiding further conversation out of respect for his father intercepted Parasurama saying:

sanskrit: गते रामे प्रशान्तात्मा रामो दाशरथिर्धनु:। वरुणायाप्रमेयाय ददौ हस्ते ससायकम्।।1.77.1।।
transliteration: gate rāme praśāntātmā rāmo dāśarathirdhanu:| varuṇāyāprameyāya dadau haste sasāyakam||1.77.1||
meaning: When Parasurama departed, Rama, son of Dasaratha with a serene mind gave the bow along with the arrow to Varuna of immeasurable strength.

sanskrit: तस्य त्वेवं प्रभावस्य धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मन:। सुतार्थं तप्यमानस्य नासीद्वंशकरस्सुत:।।1.8.1।।
transliteration: tasya tvevṃ prabhāvasya dharmajñasya mahātmana:| sutārthṃ tapyamānasya nāsīdvṃśakarassuta:||1.8.1||
meaning: Such a majestic, righteous, and magnaninous king had no son to perpetuate the race even though he performed austerities for one.

sanskrit: एतच्छ्रुत्वा रहस्सूतो राजानमिदमब्रवीत्। ऋत्विग्भिरुपदिष्टोऽयं पुरावृत्तो मया श्रुत:।।1.9.1।।
transliteration: etacchrutvā rahassūto rājānamidamabravīt| ṛtvigbhirupadiṣṭo'yṃ purāvṛtto mayā śruta:||1.9.1||
meaning: The charioteer tells the king in privacy that he has heard the advice given by the offciating priests.

sanskrit: स तां पुष्करिणीं गत्वा पद्मोत्पलझषाकुलाम्। रामस्सौमित्रि सहितो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः।।4.1.1।।
transliteration: sa tāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ gatvā padmotpalajhaṣākulām| rāmassaumitri sahito vilalāpākulendriyḥ||4.1.1||
meaning: Arriving with Laksmana at the lake filled with lotuses, lilies and fishes, Rama, his senses oppressed, burst into tears.

sanskrit: ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टं सम्रब्धं तमुपागतम्। अहं प्रसादयाञ्चक्रे भ्रातरं प्रियकाम्यया4.10.1
transliteration: tatḥ krodhasamāviṣṭṃ samrabdhṃ tamupāgatam| ahṃ prasādayāñcakre bhrātarṃ priyakāmyayā4.10.1
meaning: 'I sought to appease my brother who arrived in an agitated state overpowered with anger.

sanskrit: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा हर्षपौरुषवर्धनम्। सुग्रीवः पूजयाञ्चक्रे राघवं प्रशशंस च4.11.1।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanṃ śrutvā harṣapauruṣavardhanam| sugrīvḥ pūjayāñcakre rāghavṃ praśaśṃsa ca4.11.1||
meaning: The words of Rama boosted Sugriva's joy and manliness. He offered him prayers and praise:

sanskrit: एतच्च वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवेण सुभाषितम्। प्रत्ययार्थं महातेजा रामो जग्राह कार्मुकम्4.12.1।।
transliteration: etacca vacanṃ śrutvā sugrīveṇa subhāṣitam| pratyayārthṃ mahātejā rāmo jagrāha kārmukam4.12.1||
meaning: Having heard Sugriva's pleasing words, the brilliant Rama took up the bow in order to inspire confidence in Sugriva.

sanskrit: ऋष्यमूकात्स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धां लक्ष्मणाग्रजः। जगाम सहसुग्रीवो वालिविक्रमपालिताम्4.13.1।।
