transliteration: ṛkṣāṃśca dvīpinaścaiva nīlakomalakaprabhān| rurūnapetāpajayān dṛṣṭvā śokṃ jayiṣyasi||3.73.38||
meaning: When you see, shining like sapphires, the bears, tigers, antelopes who know no defeat, you will get over your grief.

sanskrit: राम तस्य तु शैलस्य महती शोभते गुहा। शिलापिधाना काकुत्स्थ दुःखं चास्याः प्रवेशनम्।।3.73.39।।
transliteration: rāma tasya tu śailasya mahatī śobhate guhā| śilāpidhānā kākutstha duḥkhṃ cāsyāḥ praveśanam||3.73.39||
meaning: O son of the Kakutstha family, there is a beautiful cave in that mountain covered with a slab of stone. It is difficult to enter.

sanskrit: तस्या गुहायाः प्राग्द्वारे महान्शीतोदको ह्रदः। फलमूलान्वितो रम्यो नानामृगसमावृतः।।3.73.40।।
transliteration: tasyā guhāyāḥ prāgdvāre mahānśītodako hradḥ| phalamūlānvito ramyo nānāmṛgasamāvṛtḥ||3.73.40||
meaning: At the eastern entrance of the cave there is a cool watertank. On its bank teeming with various animals are delightful fruits and roots.

sanskrit: तस्यां वसति सुग्रीवश्चतुर्भिस्सह वानरैः। कदाचिच्छिखरे तस्य पर्वतस्यावतिष्ठते।।3.73.41।।
transliteration: tasyāṃ vasati sugrīvaścaturbhissaha vānaraiḥ| kadācicchikhare tasya parvatasyāvatiṣṭhate||3.73.41||
meaning: Sugriva dwells in that cave with four other monkeys. At times he sits on the top of the mountain.

sanskrit: कबन्धस्त्वनुशास्यैवं तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ। स्रग्वी भास्करवर्णाभः खे व्यरोचत वीर्यवान्।।3.73.42।।
transliteration: kabandhastvanuśāsyaivṃ tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau| sragvī bhāskaravarṇābhḥ khe vyarocata vīryavān||3.73.42||
meaning: Having instructed both Rama and Lakshmana, courageous Kabandha, wearing a flowergarland, shone brightly like the Sun in the sky.

sanskrit: तं तु खस्थं महाभागं कबन्धं रामलक्ष्मणौ। प्रस्थितौ त्वं व्रजस्वेति वाक्यमूचतुरन्तिके।।3.73.43।।
transliteration: tṃ tu khasthṃ mahābhāgṃ kabandhṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau| prasthitau tvṃ vrajasveti vākyamūcaturantike||3.73.43||
meaning: Both Rama and Lakshmana, ready to depart, went near the glorious Kabandha waiting in the sky and said, You may go now.

sanskrit: गम्यतां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमिति तावब्रवीत्स च। सुप्रीतौ तावनुज्ञाप्य कबन्धः प्रस्थितस्तदा।।3.73.44।।
transliteration: gamyatāṃ kāryasiddhyarthamiti tāvabravītsa ca| suprītau tāvanujñāpya kabandhḥ prasthitastadā||3.73.44||
meaning: Then Kabandha said to the brothers satisfied, You may go now to accomplish your task. Then he took leave.

sanskrit: स तत्कबन्धः प्रतिपद्य रूपं वृतश्श्रिया भास्करतुल्यदेहः। निदर्शयन्राममवेक्ष्य खस्थः सख्यं कुरुष्वेति तदाभ्युवाच।।3.73.45।
transliteration: sa tatkabandhḥ pratipadya rūpṃ vṛtaśśriyā bhāskaratulyadehḥ| nidarśayanrāmamavekṣya khasthḥ sakhyṃ kuruṣveti tadābhyuvāc
meaning: Kabandha assumed his true form, his body shining like the radiance of the Sun. He stood in the sky showing his form and looking at Rama, said, Make friendship with Sugriva. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण

sanskrit: तौ शैलेष्वाचितानेकान् क्षौद्रकल्पफलान्द्रुमान्। वीक्षन्तौ जग्मतुर्ध्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.74.2।।
transliteration: tau śaileṣvācitānekān kṣaudrakalpaphalāndrumān| vīkṣantau jagmaturdhraṣṭuṃ sugrīvṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau||3.74.2||
meaning: Observing the trees loaded with honeysweet fruits on the mountain, Rama and Lakshmana went to see Sugriva.

sanskrit: कृत्वा च शैलपृष्ठे तु तौ वासं रामलक्ष्मणौ। पम्पायाः पश्चिमं तीरं राघवावुपतस्थतुः।।3.74.3।।
transliteration: kṛtvā ca śailapṛṣṭhe tu tau vāsṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau| pampāyāḥ paścimṃ tīrṃ rāghavāvupatasthatuḥ||3.74.3||
meaning: Rama and Lakshmana halted on the slope of the mountain and then departed for the western bank of Pampa.

sanskrit: तौ पुष्करिण्याः पम्पायास्तीरमासाद्य पश्चिमम्। अपश्यतां ततस्तत्र शबर्या रम्यमाश्रमम्।।3.74.4।।
transliteration: tau puṣkariṇyāḥ pampāyāstīramāsādya paścimam| apaśyatāṃ tatastatra śabaryā ramyamāśramam||3.74.4||
meaning: Both reached the west bank of lake Pampa and saw the delightful hermitage of Sabari.

sanskrit: तौ तमाश्रममासाद्य द्रुमैर्बहुभीरावृतम्। सुरम्यमभिवीक्षन्तौ शबरीमभ्युपेयतुः।।3.74.5।।
transliteration: tau tamāśramamāsādya drumairbahubhīrāvṛtam| suramyamabhivīkṣantau śabarīmabhyupeyatuḥ||3.74.5||
meaning: Both reached the beautiful hermitage full of many kinds of trees. There they saw Sabari, and went towards her.

sanskrit: तौ च दृष्ट्वा तदा सिद्धा समुत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः। रामस्य पादौ जग्राह लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः।।3.74.6।।
transliteration: tau ca dṛṣṭvā tadā siddhā samutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ| rāmasya pādau jagrāha lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmatḥ||3.74.6||
meaning: On seeing them both, Sabari, an accomplished ascetic, got up with folded hands and touched the feet of the sagacious Rama and Lakshmana.

sanskrit: पाद्यमाचमनीयं च सर्वं प्रादाद्यथाविधि। तामुवाच ततो रामश्श्रमणीं संशितव्रताम्।।3.74.7।।
transliteration: pādyamācamanīyṃ ca sarvṃ prādādyathāvidhi| tāmuvāca tato rāmaśśramaṇīṃ sṃśitavratām||3.74.7||
meaning: She offered them water to wash their feet and water to sip as per tradition. Then Rama spoke to Sabari who used to perform austere penance:

sanskrit: कच्चित्ते निर्जिता विघ्नाः कच्चित्ते वर्धते तपः। कच्चित्ते नियतः क्रोध आहारश्च तपोधने।।3.74.8।।
transliteration: kaccitte nirjitā vighnāḥ kaccitte vardhate tapḥ| kaccitte niyatḥ krodha āhāraśca tapodhane||3.74.8||
meaning: O ascetic hope you have overcome your obstacles to penance, you have controlled your anger and your desire for food. Is your austerity in progress.

sanskrit: कच्चित्ते नियमाः प्राप्ताः कच्चित्ते मनसः सुखम्। कच्चित्ते गुरुशुश्रूषा सफला चारुभाषिणि।।3.74.9।।
transliteration: kaccitte niyamāḥ prāptāḥ kaccitte manasḥ sukham| kaccitte guruśuśrūṣā saphalā cārubhāṣiṇi||3.74.9||
meaning: O Sweettongued Sabari, have you achieved selfcontrol? Has your mind attained peace ? Have your services to the preceptor yielded results?

sanskrit: रामेण तापसी पृष्टा सा सिद्धा सिद्धसम्मता। शशंस शबरी वृद्धा रामाय प्रत्युपस्थिता।।3.74.10।।
transliteration: rāmeṇa tāpasī pṛṣṭā sā siddhā siddhasammatā| śaśṃsa śabarī vṛddhā rāmāya pratyupasthitā||3.74.10||
meaning: When Rama asked Sabari who was an old, accomplished ascetic adored by siddhas, she stood in front and replied :

sanskrit: अद्य प्राप्ता तपस्सिद्धिस्तव संदर्शनान्मया। अद्य मे सफलं तप्तं गुरवश्च सुपूजिताः।।3.74.11।।
transliteration: adya prāptā tapassiddhistava sṃdarśanānmayā| adya me saphalṃ taptṃ guravaśca supūjitāḥ||3.74.11||
meaning: On seeing you now my penance has attained fulfilment, my services to my preceptors have borne fruit.

sanskrit: अद्य मे सफलं जन्म स्वर्गश्चैव भविष्यति। त्वयि देववरे राम पूजिते पुरुषर्षभ।।3.74.12।।
transliteration: adya me saphalṃ janma svargaścaiva bhaviṣyati| tvayi devavare rāma pūjite puruṣarṣabha||3.74.12||
meaning: O best of men, O highest of the gods my birth has become fruitful today with your worship, (you have made) even attainment of heaven quite certain.

sanskrit: चक्षुषा तव सौम्येन पूतास्मि रघुनन्दन। गमिष्याम्यक्षयान्लोकांस्त्वत्प्रसादादरिन्दम।।3.74.13।।
transliteration: cakṣuṣā tava saumyena pūtāsmi raghunandana| gamiṣyāmyakṣayānlokāṃstvatprasādādarindama||3.74.13||
meaning: O delight of the Raghus, your handsome look has sanctified me, O subduer of enemies, by your grace I will reach the inmperishable worlds.

sanskrit: चित्रकूटं त्वयि प्राप्ते विमानैरतुलप्रभैः। इतस्ते दिवमारूढा यानहं पर्यचारिषम्।।3.74.14।।
transliteration: citrakūṭṃ tvayi prāpte vimānairatulaprabhaiḥ| itaste divamārūḍhā yānahṃ paryacāriṣam||3.74.14||
meaning: The men I served have ascended heaven on aerial chariots of incomparable radiance the moment you touched Chitrakuta.

sanskrit: तैश्चाहमुक्ता धर्मज्ञैर्महाभागैर्महर्षिभिः। आगमिष्यति ते रामस्सुपुण्यमिममाश्रमम्।।3.74.15।। स ते प्रतिग्रहीतव्यस्सौमित्र
transliteration: taiścāhamuktā dharmajñairmahābhāgairmaharṣibhiḥ| āgamiṣyati te rāmassupuṇyamimamāśramam||3.74.15|| sa te pratigrahītavya
meaning: Those great honourable sages who knew the ways of dharma said: 'Rama would visit this sacred hermitage along with Lakshmana. He would be your guest. Receive him with due honour. And you would attain the great, inexhausti

sanskrit: मया तु विविधं वन्यं सञ्चितं पुरुषर्षभ। तवार्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र पम्पायास्तीरसम्भवम्।।3.74.17।।
transliteration: mayā tu vividhṃ vanyṃ sañcitṃ puruṣarṣabha| tavārthe puruṣavyāghra pampāyāstīrasambhavam||3.74.17||
meaning: O best among men I have collected and kept for your sake different kinds of forestfood grown on the bank of Pampa.

sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्स धर्मात्मा शबर्या शबरीमिदम्। राघवः प्राह विज्ञाने तां नित्यमबहिष्कृताम्।।3.74.18।।
transliteration: evamuktassa dharmātmā śabaryā śabarīmidam| rāghavḥ prāha vijñāne tāṃ nityamabahiṣkṛtām||3.74.18||
meaning: Entreated by her in that manner, the righteous Rama spoke to Sabari who was established in true knowledge:

sanskrit: दनोस्सकाशात्तत्त्वेन प्रभावं ते महात्मनः। श्रुतं प्रत्यक्षमिच्छामि सन्द्रष्टुं यदि मन्यसे।।3.74.19।।
transliteration: danossakāśāttattvena prabhāvṃ te mahātmanḥ| śrutṃ pratyakṣamicchāmi sandraṣṭuṃ yadi manyase||3.74.19||
meaning: I have heard from great Danu about your power. If you agree, I would like to see this power in person.

sanskrit: एतत्तु वचनं श्रुत्ता रामवक्त्राद्विनिस्सृतम्। शबरी दर्शयामास तावुभौ तद्वनं महत्।।3.74.20।।
transliteration: etattu vacanṃ śruttā rāmavaktrādvinissṛtam| śabarī darśayāmāsa tāvubhau tadvanṃ mahat||3.74.20||
meaning: At these words from the mouth of Rama, Sabari took them both round the great garden.

sanskrit: पश्य मेघघनप्रख्यं मृगपक्षिसमाकुलम्। मतङ्गवनमित्येव विश्रुतं रघुनन्दन।।।3.74.21।।
transliteration: paśya meghaghanaprakhyṃ mṛgapakṣisamākulam| mataṅgavanamityeva viśrutṃ raghunandana|||3.74.21||
meaning: O delight of the Raghus see this garden looking like the dense cloud. Full of animals and birds, it is popularly known as Matanga garden.

sanskrit: इह ते भावितात्मानो गुरवो मे महावने। जुहवाञ्चक्रिरे तीर्थं मन्त्रवन्मन्त्रपूजितम्।।3.74.22।।
transliteration: iha te bhāvitātmāno guravo me mahāvane| juhavāñcakrire tīrthṃ mantravanmantrapūjitam||3.74.22||
meaning: My precepters, who had perceived the Supreme Spirit made sacrificial offerings in this great garden, invoked gods through the power of mantras. They brought water and offered oblations to the sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: इयं प्रत्यक्थ्सली वेदिर्यत्र ते मे सुसत्कृताः। पुष्पोपहारं कुर्वन्ति श्रमादुद्वेपिभिः करैः।।3.74.23।।
transliteration: iyṃ pratyakthsalī vediryatra te me susatkṛtāḥ| puṣpopahārṃ kurvanti śramādudvepibhiḥ karaiḥ||3.74.23||
meaning: This is the altar named Pratyaksthali where the saints aged and exhausted( by performing chandrayana) whom I worshipped made offerings of flowers with trembling hands.

sanskrit: तेषां तपःप्रभावेण पश्याद्यापि रघूद्वह। द्योतयन्ति दिशस्सर्वाश्श्रिया वेद्योऽतुलप्रभाः।।3.74.24।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tapḥprabhāveṇa paśyādyāpi raghūdvaha| dyotayanti diśassarvāśśriyā vedyo'tulaprabhāḥ||3.74.24||
meaning: O Rama see, even now they illuminate the sacrificial altars with the power of their penance. They shed light in all directions with a matchless brilliance.

sanskrit: अशक्नुवद्भिस्तैर्गन्तुमुपवासश्रमालसैः। चिन्तितेऽभ्यागतान्पश्य सहितान्सप्तसागरान्।।3.74.25।।
transliteration: aśaknuvadbhistairgantumupavāsaśramālasaiḥ| cintite'bhyāgatānpaśya sahitānsaptasāgarān||3.74.25||
meaning: Look at the seven seas, which have reached here at their mere thought as they could not reach them due to fatigue from fasting.

sanskrit: कृताभिषेकैस्तैर्न्यस्ता वल्कलाः पादपेष्विह। अद्यापि नावशुष्यन्ति प्रदेशे रघुनन्दन।।3.74.26।।
transliteration: kṛtābhiṣekaistairnyastā valkalāḥ pādapeṣviha| adyāpi nāvaśuṣyanti pradeśe raghunandana||3.74.26||
meaning: O delight of the Raghus look at the bark robes spread on the trees to dry after their bathing which are still wet.

sanskrit: देवकार्याणि कुर्वद्भिर्यानीमानि कृतानि वै। पुष्पैःकुवलयैस्सार्धं म्लानत्वं नोपयान्तिवै।।3.74.27।।
transliteration: devakāryāṇi kurvadbhiryānīmāni kṛtāni vai| puṣpaiḥkuvalayaissārdhṃ mlānatvṃ nopayāntivai||3.74.27||
meaning: The flowers including lotuses offered by the sages while worshipping gods have not yet wilted.

sanskrit: कृत्स्नं वनमिदं दृष्टं श्रोतव्यं च श्रुतं त्वया। तदिच्छाम्यभ्यनुज्ञाता त्यक्तुमेतत्कलेबरम्।।3.74.28।।
transliteration: kṛtsnṃ vanamidṃ dṛṣṭṃ śrotavyṃ ca śrutṃ tvayā| tadicchāmyabhyanujñātā tyaktumetatkalebaram||3.74.28||
meaning: You have seen the entire garden and have listened what is to be heard. With your permission I would like to give up this body.

sanskrit: तेषामिच्छाम्यहं गन्तुं समीपं भावितात्मनाम्। मुनीनामाश्रमो येषामहं च परिचारिणी।।3.74.29।।
transliteration: teṣāmicchāmyahṃ gantuṃ samīpṃ bhāvitātmanām| munīnāmāśramo yeṣāmahṃ ca paricāriṇī||3.74.29||
meaning: I wish to reach those realisers of the Supreme Spirit whom I served and to whom this hermitage belonged.

sanskrit: धर्मिष्ठं तु वचश्श्रुत्वा राघवस्सहलक्ष्मणः। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे आश्चर्यमिति तत्त्वतः।।3.74.30।।
transliteration: dharmiṣṭhṃ tu vacaśśrutvā rāghavassahalakṣmaṇḥ| praharṣamatulṃ lebhe āścaryamiti tattvatḥ||3.74.30||
meaning: Rama and Lakshmana on hearing the pious words of Savari joyfully exclaimed, This is really wonderful.

sanskrit: तामुवाच ततो रामश्श्रमणीं संशितव्रताम्। अर्चितोऽहं त्वया भक्त्या गच्छकामं यथासुखम्।।3.74.31।।
transliteration: tāmuvāca tato rāmaśśramaṇīṃ sṃśitavratām| arcito'hṃ tvayā bhaktyā gacchakāmṃ yathāsukham||3.74.31||
meaning: Looking at Sabari who was steadfast in her vow, Rama said, O ascetic, you have worshipped me with devotion. You may go wherever you like (to the world you desire)

sanskrit: इत्युक्ता जटिला वृद्धा चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरा। तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते शबरी देहं जीर्णं जिहासती।।3.74.32।। अनुज्ञाता तु रामेण हुत्वा
transliteration: ityuktā jaṭilā vṛddhā cīrakṛṣṇājināmbarā| tasminmuhūrte śabarī dehṃ jīrṇṃ jihāsatī||3.74.32|| anujñātā tu rāmeṇa hutvātm
meaning: With matted locks, tattered bark clothes and deer skin, Sabari consigned her old and emaciated body to the fire at that moment, with the permission of Rama and ascended to heaven, her body glowing like fire.

sanskrit: दिव्याभरणसंयुक्ता दिव्यमाल्यानुलेपना। दिव्याम्बरधरा तत्र बभूव प्रियदर्शना।।3.74.34।। विराजयन्ती तं देशं विद्युत्सौदामिनी
transliteration: divyābharaṇasṃyuktā divyamālyānulepanā| divyāmbaradharā tatra babhūva priyadarśanā||3.74.34|| virājayantī tṃ deśṃ vidyut
meaning: Adorned with wonderful ornaments and beautiful garlands, anointed with fragrant unguents, robed in most beautiful clothes, she appeared like a streak of lightning, her body shining bright and her face contented.

sanskrit: यत्र ते सुकृतात्मानो विहरन्ति महर्षयः।।3.74.35।। तत्पुण्यं शबरी स्थानं जगामात्मसमाधिना।
transliteration: yatra te sukṛtātmāno viharanti maharṣayḥ||3.74.35|| tatpuṇyṃ śabarī sthānṃ jagāmātmasamādhinā|
meaning: By virtue of her selfmeditation, Sabari went to that sacred world where the holy sages lived because of their good deeds. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे चतुस्सप्ततितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seven

sanskrit: स चिन्तयित्वा धर्मात्मा प्रभावं तं महात्मनाम्। हितकारिणमेकाग्रं लक्ष्मणं राघवोऽब्रवीत्।।3.75.2।।
transliteration: sa cintayitvā dharmātmā prabhāvṃ tṃ mahātmanām| hitakāriṇamekāgrṃ lakṣmaṇṃ rāghavo'bravīt||3.75.2||
meaning: Thinking about the power of the great sages, righteous Rama said to Lakshmana, his wellwisher with singleminded devotion:

sanskrit: दृष्टोऽयमाश्रमस्सौम्य बह्वाश्चर्यो महात्मनाम्। विश्वस्तमृगशार्दूलो नानाविहगसेवितः।।3.75.3।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭo'yamāśramassaumya bahvāścaryo mahātmanām| viśvastamṛgaśārdūlo nānāvihagasevitḥ||3.75.3||
meaning: O handsome one, we have seen this highly wonderful hermitage, where deer and tigers dwell together with mutual confidence, where birds of all kinds inhabit.

sanskrit: सप्तानां च समुद्राणामेषु तीर्थेषु लक्ष्मण। उपस्पृष्टं च विधिवत्पितरश्चापि तर्पिताः।।3.75.4।।
transliteration: saptānāṃ ca samudrāṇāmeṣu tīrtheṣu lakṣmaṇa| upaspṛṣṭṃ ca vidhivatpitaraścāpi tarpitāḥ||3.75.4||
meaning: O Lakshmana, having bathed in the waters of the seven seas (by taking ritualistic bath in these waters) the manes are offered oblations in accordance with tradition.

sanskrit: प्रणष्टमशुभं तत्तत्कल्याणं समुपस्थितम्। तेन तत्त्वेन हृष्टं मे मनो लक्ष्मण सम्प्रति।।3.75.5।। हृदये हि नरव्याघ्र शुभमावि
transliteration: praṇaṣṭamaśubhṃ tattatkalyāṇṃ samupasthitam| tena tattvena hṛṣṭṃ me mano lakṣmaṇa samprati||3.75.5|| hṛdaye hi naravyāgh
meaning: We have got rid of inauspicious time and good days have come. Therefore, I feel truly happy. Good fortune will appear (now), O Lakshmana, O tiger among men

sanskrit: तदागच्छ गमिष्यामि पम्पां तां प्रियदर्शनाम्।।3.75.6।। ऋष्यमूको गिरिर्यत्र नातिदूरे प्रकाशते। यस्मिन्वसति धर्मात्मा सुग्री
transliteration: tadāgaccha gamiṣyāmi pampāṃ tāṃ priyadarśanām||3.75.6|| ṛṣyamūko giriryatra nātidūre prakāśate| yasminvasati dharmātmā s
meaning: Come, let us go to Pampa, which is pleasing to look at. Sugriva, the rigteous self, the son of the Sun has been staying for fear of Vali at the shining Rishyamuka, not far from here.

sanskrit: अभित्वरे च तं द्रष्टुं सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्।।3.75.8।। तदधीनं हि मे सौम्य सीतायाः परिमार्गणम्।
transliteration: abhitvare ca tṃ draṣṭuṃ sugrīvṃ vānararṣabham||3.75.8|| tadadhīnṃ hi me saumya sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam|
meaning: I am hastening to see that noble Sugriva the mighty monkey, as the search for Sita depends on him, O handsome one

sanskrit: एवं ब्रुवाणं तं धीरं रामं सौमित्रिरब्रवीत्।।3.75.9।। गच्छावस्त्वरितं तत्र ममापि त्वरते मनः।
transliteration: evṃ bruvāṇṃ tṃ dhīrṃ rāmṃ saumitrirabravīt||3.75.9|| gacchāvastvaritṃ tatra mamāpi tvarate manḥ|
meaning: To the words of Rama who was of stable mind, Lakshmana replied : My mind too is hastening me. Let us get there quickly.

sanskrit: आश्रमात्तु तत स्तस्मान्निष्क्रम्य स विशाम्पतिः।।3.75.10।। आजगाम ततः पम्पां लक्ष्मणेन सह प्रभुः।
transliteration: āśramāttu tata stasmānniṣkramya sa viśāmpatiḥ||3.75.10|| ājagāma tatḥ pampāṃ lakṣmaṇena saha prabhuḥ|
meaning: Then Rama the lord of men along with Lakshmana departed from the hermitage and went to Pampa.

sanskrit: स ददर्श ततः पुण्यामुदारजनसेविताम्।।3.75.11।। नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णां पम्पां पानीयवाहिनीम्। पद्मैस्सौगन्धिकैस्ताम्रां शुक्लां
transliteration: sa dadarśa tatḥ puṇyāmudārajanasevitām||3.75.11|| nānādrumalatākīrṇāṃ pampāṃ pānīyavāhinīm| padmaissaugandhikaistāmrāṃ ś
meaning: He saw the sacred lake Pampa whose sweet flow of water was used by great seers. It abounded in trees and creepers. Its surface was red with lotuses at one place, white with clusters of lilies at another and with blue lot

sanskrit: स तामासाद्य वै रामो दूरादुदकवाहिनीम्।।3.75.13।। मतङ्गसरसं नाम ह्रदं समवगाहत।
transliteration: sa tāmāsādya vai rāmo dūrādudakavāhinīm||3.75.13|| mataṅgasarasṃ nāma hradṃ samavagāhata|
meaning: Rama reached the Matanga lake which he could see from a distance and bathed in it.

sanskrit: अरविन्दोत्पलवतीं पद्मसौगन्धिकायुताम्।।3.75.14।। पुष्पिताम्रवणोपेतां बर्हिणोद्घुष्टनादिताम्। तिलकैर्बीजपूरैश्च धवैश्शुक्ल
transliteration: aravindotpalavatīṃ padmasaugandhikāyutām||3.75.14|| puṣpitāmravaṇopetāṃ barhiṇodghuṣṭanāditām| tilakairbījapūraiśca dhav
meaning: Lake Pampa was filled with red lotuses and their fragrance.The bank was lined with blossoming mango trees and trees of several kinds like tilaka trees with fruits full of seeds like citron, dhava trees, white trees in bl

sanskrit: स ददर्श ततः पम्पां शीतवारिनिधिं शुभाम्।।3.75.20।। तिलकाशोकपुन्नागवकुलोद्दालकाशिनीम्।
transliteration: sa dadarśa tatḥ pampāṃ śītavārinidhiṃ śubhām||3.75.20|| tilakāśokapunnāgavakuloddālakāśinīm|
meaning: Rama saw lake Pampa with cool waters and the groves on the bank filled with tilaka, ashoka, punnaga, bakula and uddala trees.

sanskrit: स रामो विविधान्वृक्षान्सरांसि विविधानि च।।3.75.21।। पश्यन्कामाभिसन्तप्तो जगाम परमं ह्रदम्।
transliteration: sa rāmo vividhānvṛkṣānsarāṃsi vividhāni ca||3.75.21|| paśyankāmābhisantapto jagāma paramṃ hradam|
meaning: On seeing different kinds of trees and tanks, the lovestriken Rama visited that great lake.

sanskrit: पुष्पितोपवनोपेतां सालचम्पकशोभिताम्।।3.75.22।। षट्पदौघसमाविष्टां श्रीमतीमतुलप्रभाम्। स्फटिकोपमतोयाढ्यां श्लक्ष्णवालुकसन्त
transliteration: puṣpitopavanopetāṃ sālacampakaśobhitām||3.75.22|| ṣaṭpadaughasamāviṣṭāṃ śrīmatīmatulaprabhām| sphaṭikopamatoyāḍhyāṃ ślak
meaning: There were lovely pleasuregardens in full bloom filled with sal and champk trees. Honeybees on flowers looked lovely and bright. The waters were crystalclear and fragrant with lotuses.The soft sands on the banks of Pampa

sanskrit: अस्यास्तीरे तु पूर्वोक्तः पर्वतो धातुमण्डितः। ऋष्यमूक इति ख्यातः पुण्यः पुष्पितपादपः।।3.75.25।।
transliteration: asyāstīre tu pūrvoktḥ parvato dhātumaṇḍitḥ| ṛṣyamūka iti khyātḥ puṇyḥ puṣpitapādapḥ||3.75.25||
meaning: The famous mount, sacred Rishyamuka is situated on the bank of Pampa full of blossoming trees.

sanskrit: हरेः ऋक्षरजोनाम्नः पुत्रस्तस्य महात्मनः। अध्यास्ते तं महावीर्यस्सुग्रीव इति विश्रुतः।।3.75.26।।
transliteration: hareḥ ṛkṣarajonāmnḥ putrastasya mahātmanḥ| adhyāste tṃ mahāvīryassugrīva iti viśrutḥ||3.75.26||
meaning: The mighty son of Riksharaja, the great soul, the Sun whose son was the wellknown Sugriva, resides on this mountain.

sanskrit: सुग्रीवमभिगच्छ त्वं वानरेन्द्रं नरर्षभ। इत्युवाच पुनर्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यविक्रमम्।।3.75.27।।
transliteration: sugrīvamabhigaccha tvṃ vānarendrṃ nararṣabha| ityuvāca punarvākyṃ lakṣmaṇṃ satyavikramam||3.75.27||
meaning: Rama said to Lakshmana, the best of men, who had truth as his strength, Go to Sugriva, lord of the monkeys.

sanskrit: राज्यभ्रष्टेन दीनेन तस्यामासक्तचेतसा। कथं मया विना शक्यं सीतां लक्ष्मण जीवितुम्।।3.75.28।।
transliteration: rājyabhraṣṭena dīnena tasyāmāsaktacetasā| kathṃ mayā vinā śakyṃ sītāṃ lakṣmaṇa jīvitum||3.75.28||
meaning: O Lakshmana, deprived of the kingdom I have become a destitute. With my heart attached to Sita how can I live without her ?

sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्त्वा मदनाभिपीडितः स लक्ष्मणं वाक्यमनन्यचेतसम्। विवेश पम्पां नलिनीं मनोरमां रघूत्तमश्शोकविषादयन्त्रितः।।3.75.29
transliteration: ityevamuktvā madanābhipīḍitḥ sa lakṣmaṇṃ vākyamananyacetasam| viveśa pampāṃ nalinīṃ manoramāṃ raghūttamaśśokaviṣādayantr
meaning: Having said these words to Lakshmana who was listening to him with undivided attention, Rama, the best of the Raghus, oppressed by love and afflicted by tears of grief entered Pampa, the delightful lotuslake.

sanskrit: ततो महद्वर्त्म सुदूरसङ्क्रमं क्रमेण गत्वा प्रविलोकयन्वनम्। ददर्श पम्पां शुभदर्शकाननामनेकनानाविधपक्षिजालकाम्।।3.75.30।।
transliteration: tato mahadvartma sudūrasaṅkramṃ krameṇa gatvā pravilokayanvanam| dadarśa pampāṃ śubhadarśakānanāmanekanānāvidhapakṣijāla
meaning: Thereafter, going slowly to a distance, Rama and Lakshmana saw Pampa surrounded by beautiful forests full of many varieties of birds. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततिमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends

sanskrit: उत्थाय तु यथाकालं राघवस्सहसीतया। उपस्पृश्यसुशितेन जलेनोत्पलगन्धिना।।3.8.2।।
transliteration: utthāya tu yathākālṃ rāghavassahasītayā| upaspṛśyasuśitena jalenotpalagandhinā||3.8.2||
meaning: In the morning Rama and Sita got up in time and took bath in cool, lilyfragrant water.

sanskrit: अथ तेऽग्निं सुरांश्चैव वैदेही रामलक्ष्मणौ। काल्यं विधिवदभ्यर्च्य तपस्विशरणे वने।।3.8.3।। उदयन्तं दिनकरं दृष्ट्वा विगतकल्
transliteration: atha te'gniṃ surāṃścaiva vaidehī rāmalakṣmaṇau| kālyṃ vidhivadabhyarcya tapasviśaraṇe vane||3.8.3|| udayantṃ dinakarṃ dṛ
meaning: And as per routine, sinless Sita, Rama and Lakshmana offered prayers to the fire and other gods of the forest which was the refuge of the ascetics. Seeing the rising Sun, they worshipped him, and approaching Sutikshna, s

sanskrit: सुखोषितास्स्मभगवंस्त्वया पूज्येन पूजिताः। आपृच्छामः प्रयास्यामो मुनयस्त्वरयन्ति नः।।3.8.5।।
transliteration: sukhoṣitāssmabhagavṃstvayā pūjyena pūjitāḥ| āpṛcchāmḥ prayāsyāmo munayastvarayanti nḥ||3.8.5||
meaning: O revered Sutikshna received by one so worshipworthy like you, we spent the night well. We (now)take leave of you. The sages are hastening us.

sanskrit: त्वरामहे वयं द्रष्टुं कृत्स्नमाश्रममण्डलम्। ऋषीणां पुण्यशीलानां दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्।।3.8.6।।
transliteration: tvarāmahe vayṃ draṣṭuṃ kṛtsnamāśramamaṇḍalam| ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyaśīlānāṃ daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinām||3.8.6||
meaning: We wish to see the entire circle of hermitages of the sages, residing in Dandaka forest. So we are in a hurry.

sanskrit: अभ्यनुज्ञातुमिच्छामस्सहैभिर्मुनिपुङ्गवैः। धर्मनित्यैस्तपोदान्तैर्विशिखैरिव पावकैः।।3.8.7।।
transliteration: abhyanujñātumicchāmassahaibhirmunipuṅgavaiḥ| dharmanityaistapodāntairviśikhairiva pāvakaiḥ||3.8.7||
meaning: We seek your permission to go with the great sages, who are ever engaged in righteousness, selfcontrolled by virtue of their penance, and are like flameless fire.

sanskrit: अविषह्यातपो यावत्सूर्यो नातिविराजते। अमार्गेणागतां लक्ष्मीं प्राप्येवान्वयवर्जितः।।3.8.8।। तावदिच्छामहे गन्तुमित्युक्त्व
transliteration: aviṣahyātapo yāvatsūryo nātivirājate| amārgeṇāgatāṃ lakṣmīṃ prāpyevānvayavarjitḥ||3.8.8|| tāvadicchāmahe gantumityuktvā
meaning: We wish to depart before the Sun grows unbearably hot like the man devoid of good lineage who acquires wealth through unlawful means (becomes arrogant). Thereafter Rama along with Sita and Lakshmana offered worship at th

sanskrit: तौ संस्पृशन्तौ चरणावुत्थाप्य मुनिपुङ्गवः। गाढमालिङ्ग्य सस्नेहमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्।।3.8.10।।
transliteration: tau sṃspṛśantau caraṇāvutthāpya munipuṅgavḥ| gāḍhamāliṅgya sasnehamidṃ vacanamabravīt||3.8.10||
meaning: When both Rama and Lakshmana touched the feet of Sutikshna, the best of the sages, he lifted them up, hugged them tightly, and said affectionately:

sanskrit: अरिष्टं गच्छ पन्थानं राम सौमित्रिणा सह। सीतया चानया सार्धं छाययेवानुवृत्तया।।3.8.11।।
transliteration: ariṣṭṃ gaccha panthānṃ rāma saumitriṇā saha| sītayā cānayā sārdhṃ chāyayevānuvṛttayā||3.8.11||
meaning: You may safely tread, O Rama, this path along with Lakshmana and Sita who is following you like a shadow.

sanskrit: पश्याश्रमपदं रम्यं दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्। एषां तपस्विनां वीर तपसा भावितात्मनाम्।।3.8.12।।
transliteration: paśyāśramapadṃ ramyṃ daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinām| eṣāṃ tapasvināṃ vīra tapasā bhāvitātmanām||3.8.12||
meaning: O valient Rama the sages, living in the Dandaka forest, are self realised souls. See how delightful is the location of their hermitages.

sanskrit: सप्राज्यफलमूलानि पुष्पितानि वनानि च। प्रशस्तमृगयूथानि शान्तपक्षिगणानि च।। 3.8.13।। फुल्लपङ्कजषण्डानि प्रसन्नसलिलानि च। क
transliteration: saprājyaphalamūlāni puṣpitāni vanāni ca| praśastamṛgayūthāni śāntapakṣigaṇāni ca|| 3.8.13|| phullapaṅkajaṣaṇḍāni prasann
meaning: You will see the beautiful forestareas with abundant fruits and roots, flowers in full bloom, herds of animals, flocks of quiet birds tanks and lakes filled with clean waters and shining with fully blossomed lotuses, res

sanskrit: गम्यतां वत्स सौमित्रे भवानपि च गच्छतु। आगन्तव्यं च ते दृष्ट्वा पुनरेवाश्रमं मम।।3.8.16।।
transliteration: gamyatāṃ vatsa saumitre bhavānapi ca gacchatu| āgantavyṃ ca te dṛṣṭvā punarevāśramṃ mama||3.8.16||
meaning: O dear Rama, O Lakshmana you may leave (now), you may have to come back to this hermitage after seeing those places.

sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा काकुत्स्थस्सहलक्ष्मणः। प्रदक्षिणं मुनिं कृत्वा प्रस्थातुमुपचक्रमे।।3.8.17।।
transliteration: evamuktastathetyuktvā kākutsthassahalakṣmaṇḥ| pradakṣiṇṃ muniṃ kṛtvā prasthātumupacakrame||3.8.17||
meaning: Thus addressed, Rama, scion of the Kakutsthas along with Lakshmana circumambulated the sage (in reverence) and set forth.

sanskrit: ततश्शुभतरे तूणी धनुषी चायतेक्षणा। ददौ सीता तयोर्भ्रात्रोः खङ्गौ च विमलौ ततः।।3.8.18।।
transliteration: tataśśubhatare tūṇī dhanuṣī cāyatekṣaṇā| dadau sītā tayorbhrātroḥ khaṅgau ca vimalau tatḥ||3.8.18||
meaning: Thereafter largeeyed Sita handed the brothers two quivers, two bows as well as two excellent swords.

sanskrit: आबध्य च शुभे तूणी चापे चादाय सुस्वनौ। निष्क्रान्तावाश्रमाद्गन्तुमुभौ तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।।3.8.19।।
transliteration: ābadhya ca śubhe tūṇī cāpe cādāya susvanau| niṣkrāntāvāśramādgantumubhau tau rāmalakṣmaṇau||3.8.19||
meaning: Both Rama and Lakshmana tied their auspicious quivers, took the two twanging bows and departed from the hermitage.

sanskrit: श्रीमन्तौ रूपसम्पन्नौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा। प्रस्थितौ धृतचापौ तौ सीतया सह राघवौ।।3.8.20।।
transliteration: śrīmantau rūpasampannau dīpyamānau svatejasā| prasthitau dhṛtacāpau tau sītayā saha rāghavau||3.8.20||
meaning: Handsome Rama and Lakshmana, glowing in their radiance held the bows and exited with Sita. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे अष्टमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the eighth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ram

sanskrit: अयं धर्मस्सुसूक्ष्मेण विधिना प्राप्यते महान्। निवृत्तेन तु शक्योऽयं व्यसनात्कामजादिह।।3.9.2।।
transliteration: ayṃ dharmassusūkṣmeṇa vidhinā prāpyate mahān| nivṛttena tu śakyo'yṃ vyasanātkāmajādiha||3.9.2||
meaning: This great path of dharma you are following now can be attained only through subtle means by one free from addiction born of passion.

sanskrit: त्रीण्येव व्यसनान्यत्र कामजानि भवन्त्युत। मिथ्यावाक्यं परमकं तस्माद्गुरुतरावुभौ।।3.9.3।। परदाराभिगमनं विना वैरं च रौद्रत
transliteration: trīṇyeva vyasanānyatra kāmajāni bhavantyuta| mithyāvākyṃ paramakṃ tasmādgurutarāvubhau||3.9.3|| paradārābhigamanṃ vinā v
meaning: There are three kinds of vices born out of lust. First, speaking untruth, second, having sexual relation with others' wives and third, resorting to violence with no enmity. The later two vices are of serious nature.

sanskrit: मिथ्यावाक्यं न ते भूतं न भविष्यति राघव।।3.9.4।। कुतोऽभिलाषणं स्त्रीणां परेषां धर्मनाशनम्।
transliteration: mithyāvākyṃ na te bhūtṃ na bhaviṣyati rāghava||3.9.4|| kuto'bhilāṣaṇṃ strīṇāṃ pareṣāṃ dharmanāśanam|
meaning: O Rama you never spoke untruth in the past nor will you speak in future. How can there be any desire in you to destroy the virtue of others' wives ?

sanskrit: तव नास्ति मनुष्येन्द्र न चाभूत्ते कदाचन।।3.9.5।। मनस्यपि तथा राम न चैतद्विद्यते क्वचित्।
transliteration: tava nāsti manuṣyendra na cābhūtte kadācana||3.9.5|| manasyapi tathā rāma na caitadvidyate kvacit|
meaning: O Rama, lord among men, you hadn't it (lust for other women) in the past. You havn't it now. Never does it exist even in your mind.

sanskrit: स्वदारनिरतस्त्वं च नित्यमेव नृपात्मज।।3.9.6।। धर्मिष्ठस्सत्यसन्धश्च पितुर्निर्देशकारकः।
transliteration: svadāraniratastvṃ ca nityameva nṛpātmaja||3.9.6|| dharmiṣṭhassatyasandhaśca piturnirdeśakārakḥ|
meaning: O prince, you are always faithful to your wife. You are righteous, truthful and obedient to your father's orders.

sanskrit: सत्यसन्ध महाभाग श्रीमल्लक्ष्मणपूर्वज।।3.9.7।। त्वयि धर्मश्च सत्यं च त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्।
transliteration: satyasandha mahābhāga śrīmallakṣmaṇapūrvaja||3.9.7|| tvayi dharmaśca satyṃ ca tvayi sarvṃ pratiṣṭhitam|
meaning: O Rama, you are truthful, honourable, powerful. O elder brother of Lakshmana, in you is established truth and righteousness.

sanskrit: तच्च सर्वं महाबाहो शक्यं धर्तुं जितेन्द्रियैः।।3.9.8।। तव वश्येन्द्रियत्वं च जानामि शुभदर्शन।
transliteration: tacca sarvṃ mahābāho śakyṃ dhartuṃ jitendriyaiḥ||3.9.8|| tava vaśyendriyatvṃ ca jānāmi śubhadarśana|
meaning: O longarmed one, to contain all this is only possible for those who have conquered the senses. O handsome one, I know your ability to control the senses.

sanskrit: तृतीयं यदिदं रौद्रं परप्राणाभिहिंसनम्।।3.9.9।। निर्वैरं क्रियते मोहात्तच्च ते समुपस्थितम्।
transliteration: tṛtīyṃ yadidṃ raudrṃ paraprāṇābhihiṃsanam||3.9.9|| nirvairṃ kriyate mohāttacca te samupasthitam|
meaning: (But) you are a victim to the third (vice born of lust) i.e. showing violence without cause for enmity

sanskrit: प्रतिज्ञातस्त्वया वीर दण्डकारण्यवासिनाम्।।3.9.10।। ऋषीणां रक्षणार्थाय वधस्संयति रक्षसाम्।
transliteration: pratijñātastvayā vīra daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinām||3.9.10|| ṛṣīṇāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya vadhassṃyati rakṣasām|
meaning: O valiant one, you have promised to kill the demons in the battle, in order to protect the sages residing in the Dandaka forest.

sanskrit: एतन्निमित्तं च वनं दण्डका इति विश्रुतम्।।3.9.11।। प्रस्थितस्त्वं सह भ्रात्रा धृतबाणशरासनः।
transliteration: etannimittṃ ca vanṃ daṇḍakā iti viśrutam||3.9.11|| prasthitastvṃ saha bhrātrā dhṛtabāṇaśarāsanḥ|
meaning: It is only on account of this that you entered the wellknown Dandaka forest with your brother wielding bow and arrows.

sanskrit: ततस्त्वां प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा मम चिन्ताकुलं मनः।।3.9.12।। त्वद्वृत्तं चिन्तयन्त्या वै भवेन्निश्श्रेयसं हितम्।
transliteration: tatastvāṃ prasthitṃ dṛṣṭvā mama cintākulṃ manḥ||3.9.12|| tvadvṛttṃ cintayantyā vai bhavenniśśreyasṃ hitam|
meaning: I am, therefore, worried in my mind when I see you here and think of your wellbeing. I wish your ultimate good. [The next two lines appear, more or less, a repetition. So omitted : Editor]

sanskrit: त्वां चैव प्रस्थितं दृष्ट्वा राम चिन्ताकुलं मनः।।3.9.13।। सर्वतचशिन्तय्नत्या मे तव निश्श्रेयसं नृप। न हि मे रोचते वीर गम
transliteration: tvāṃ caiva prasthitṃ dṛṣṭvā rāma cintākulṃ manḥ||3.9.13|| sarvatacaśintaynatyā me tava niśśreyasṃ nṛpa| na hi me rocate
meaning: O brave Rama, I do not like your going to Dandaka forest. I shall tell you the reason. Do listen.

sanskrit: त्वं हि बाणधनुष्पाणिर्भ्रात्रा सह वनं गतः।।3.9.15।। दृष्ट्वा वनचरान्सर्वान्कच्चित्कुर्याश्शरव्ययम्।
transliteration: tvṃ hi bāṇadhanuṣpāṇirbhrātrā saha vanṃ gatḥ||3.9.15|| dṛṣṭvā vanacarānsarvānkaccitkuryāśśaravyayam|
meaning: Of course, you will go to the forest with your brother, holding the bow and arrows. Release the arrows when you see the forestrangers.

sanskrit: क्षत्रियाणामपि धनुर्हुताशस्येन्धनानि च।।3.9.16।। समीपतस्स्थितं तेजो बलमुच्छ्रयते भृशम्।
transliteration: kṣatriyāṇāmapi dhanurhutāśasyendhanāni ca||3.9.16|| samīpatassthitṃ tejo balamucchrayate bhṛśam|
meaning: A bow in the hand of a kshatriya is like fuel to fire. It surely swells his strength and his brilliance.

sanskrit: पुरा किल महाबाहो तपस्स्वी सत्यवाक्छुचिः।।3.9.17।। कस्मिंश्चिदभवत्पुण्ये वने रतमृगद्विजे।
transliteration: purā kila mahābāho tapassvī satyavākchuciḥ||3.9.17|| kasmiṃścidabhavatpuṇye vane ratamṛgadvije|
meaning: O mightyarmed one, there dwelt in the past an ascetic, noble and truthful in a sacred forest where animals and birds lived merrily together.

sanskrit: तस्यैव तपसो विघ्नं कर्तुमिन्द्रश्शचीपतिः।।3.9.18।। खङ्गपाणिरथागच्छदाश्रमं भटरूपधृत्।
transliteration: tasyaiva tapaso vighnṃ kartumindraśśacīpatiḥ||3.9.18|| khaṅgapāṇirathāgacchadāśramṃ bhaṭarūpadhṛt|
meaning: Once Indra, husband of Sachi, came to his hermitage in the guise of an attendant, sword in hand, in order to hinder his penance.

sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तदाश्रमपदे निशितः खङ्ग उत्तमः।।3.9.19।। स न्यासविधिना दत्तः पुण्ये तपसि तिष्ठतः।
transliteration: tasmiṃstadāśramapade niśitḥ khaṅga uttamḥ||3.9.19|| sa nyāsavidhinā dattḥ puṇye tapasi tiṣṭhatḥ|
meaning: Then while the sage was practising penance at the hermitage, he gave him that excellent sword to be kept in trust.

sanskrit: स तच्छस्त्रमनुप्राप्य न्यासरक्षणतत्परः।।3.9.20।। वने तु विचरत्येव रक्षन्प्रत्ययमात्मनः।
transliteration: sa tacchastramanuprāpya nyāsarakṣaṇatatparḥ||3.9.20|| vane tu vicaratyeva rakṣanpratyayamātmanḥ|
meaning: Having received the weapon as a trust, the sage went wandering in the forest, always attentive in safeguarding the weapon.

sanskrit: यत्र गच्छत्युपादातुं मूलानि च फलानि च।।3.9.21।। न विना याति तं खङ्गं न्यासरक्षणतत्परः।
transliteration: yatra gacchatyupādātuṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca||3.9.21|| na vinā yāti tṃ khaṅgṃ nyāsarakṣaṇatatparḥ|
meaning: Vigilant about protecting the sword deposited with him, the sage never moved without it even when he went gathering roots and fruits.

sanskrit: नित्यं शस्त्रं परिवहन्क्रमेण स तपोधनः।।3.9.22।। चकार रौद्रीं स्वां बुद्धिं त्यक्त्वा तपसि निश्चयम्।
transliteration: nityṃ śastrṃ parivahankrameṇa sa tapodhanḥ||3.9.22|| cakāra raudrīṃ svāṃ buddhiṃ tyaktvā tapasi niścayam|
meaning: While the sage moved about holding the weapon, he gave up the practice of penance gradually and developed a violent mindset.

sanskrit: ततस्सरौद्रेऽभिरतः प्रमत्तोऽधर्मकर्शितः।।3.9.23।। तस्य शस्त्रस्य संवासाज्जगाम नरकं मुनिः।
transliteration: tatassaraudre'bhiratḥ pramatto'dharmakarśitḥ||3.9.23|| tasya śastrasya sṃvāsājjagāma narakṃ muniḥ|
meaning: By association with the sword, he developed a violent attitude. And in that habitual state of excitement he was dragged into unrighteous ways which (ultimately) took him to hell.

sanskrit: एवमेतत्पुरा वृत्तं शस्त्रसंयोगकारणम्।।3.9.24।। अग्निसंयोगवद्धेतुश्शस्त्रसंयोग उच्यते। स्नेहाच्च बहुमानाच्च स्मारये त्वां
transliteration: evametatpurā vṛttṃ śastrasṃyogakāraṇam||3.9.24|| agnisṃyogavaddhetuśśastrasṃyoga ucyate| snehācca bahumānācca smāraye tv
meaning: Contact with the weapon has led to this in the past. Like contact with fire, it leads man to destruction. I say this out of my love and reverence for you as a reminder and not as an instruction.

sanskrit: न कथञ्चन सा कार्या गृहीतधनुषा त्वया। बुद्धिर्वैरं विना हन्तुं राक्षसान्दण्डकाश्रितान्।।3.9.26।। अपराधं विना हन्तुं लोकान
transliteration: na kathañcana sā kāryā gṛhītadhanuṣā tvayā| buddhirvairṃ  vinā hantuṃ rākṣasāndaṇḍakāśritān||3.9.26|| aparādhṃ vinā hant
meaning: While holding a bow, you should not have the intention to kill demons residing in Dandaka with no animosity against you. O valiant one I do not desire that any one should be killed without incurring any offence.

sanskrit: क्षत्रियाणां तु वीराणां वनेषु निरतात्मनाम्।।3.9.27।। धनुषा कार्यमेतावदार्तानां त्वभिरक्षणम्।
transliteration: kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu vīrāṇāṃ vaneṣu niratātmanām||3.9.27|| dhanuṣā kāryametāvadārtānāṃ tvabhirakṣaṇam|
meaning: It is the duty of a kshatriya, a warrior to protect with his bow those who practise selfcontrol (penance) in the forest in a state of panic.

sanskrit: क्वच शस्त्रं क्व च वनं क्व च क्षात्रं तपः क्वच।।3.9.28।। व्याविद्धमिदमस्माभिर्द्देशधर्मस्तु पूज्यताम्।
transliteration: kvaca śastrṃ kva ca vanṃ kva ca kṣātrṃ tapḥ kvaca||3.9.28|| vyāviddhamidamasmābhirddeśadharmastu pūjyatām|
meaning: Where is the question of wielding a weapon and living in the forest, where is the life of a kshatriya and the life of penance? For us, this is an encroachment. Let the law of the land be honoured.

sanskrit: तदार्य कलुषा बुद्धिर्जायते शस्त्रसेवनात्।।3.9.29।। पुनर्गत्वा त्वयोध्यायां क्षत्रधर्मं चरिष्यसि।
transliteration: tadārya kaluṣā buddhirjāyate śastrasevanāt||3.9.29|| punargatvā tvayodhyāyāṃ kṣatradharmṃ cariṣyasi|
meaning: Lord, when we handle the weapon, the mind gets vitiated. (Only) after returning to Ayodhya can you perform the duty of a kshatriya.

sanskrit: अक्षया तु भवेत्प्रीतिश्श्वश्रूश्वशुरयोर्मम।।3.9.30।। यदि राज्यं परित्यज्य भवेस्त्वं निरतो मुनिः।
transliteration: akṣayā tu bhavetprītiśśvaśrūśvaśurayormama||3.9.30|| yadi rājyṃ parityajya bhavestvṃ nirato muniḥ|
meaning: You would have been on unlimited source of joy to my fatherinlaw and motherinlaw had you permanently renounced the kingdom for the life of an ascetic.

sanskrit: धर्मादर्थः प्रभवति धर्मात्प्रभवते सुखम्।।3.9.31।। धर्मेण लभते सर्वं धर्मसारमिदं जगत्।
transliteration: dharmādarthḥ prabhavati dharmātprabhavate sukham||3.9.31|| dharmeṇa labhate sarvṃ dharmasāramidṃ jagat|
meaning: Righteousness brings wealth. Wealth brings happiness. Righteousness brings everything. In fact, the essence of the world is righteousness.

sanskrit: आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तै कर्शयित्वा प्रयत्नतः।।3.9.32।। प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभ्यते सुखम्।
transliteration: ātmānṃ niyamaistaistai karśayitvā prayatnatḥ||3.9.32|| prāpyate nipuṇairdharmo na sukhāllabhyate sukham|
meaning: The wise earn dharma through getting their bodies emaciated by carefully adopting different means of discipline (selftorture). Happiness does not beget happiness.

sanskrit: नित्यं शुचिमतिस्सौम्य चर धर्मं तपोवने।।3.9.33।। सर्वं हि विदितं तुभ्यं त्रैलोक्यमपि तत्त्वतः।
transliteration: nityṃ śucimatissaumya cara dharmṃ tapovane||3.9.33|| sarvṃ hi viditṃ tubhyṃ trailokyamapi tattvatḥ|
meaning: O gentle one you may move in this forest of ascetics with a pure mind. The true meaning behind everything in these three worlds is known to you, indeed.

sanskrit: राजाऽपि तौ महातेजा स्सस्मार प्रोषितौ सुतौ। उभौ भरतशत्रुघ्नौ महेन्द्रवरुणोपमौ।।2.1.4।।
transliteration: rājā'pi tau mahātejā ssasmāra proṣitau sutau| ubhau bharataśatrughnau mahendravaruṇopamau||2.1.4||
meaning: The glorious king Dasaratha also remembered his sons, Bharata and Satrughna, who were like the great Indra and Varuna, (now) away from home.

sanskrit: सर्व एव तु तस्येष्टा श्चत्वारः पुरुषर्षभाः। स्वशरीराद्विनिर्वृत्ताश्चत्वार इव बाहवः।।2.1.5।।
transliteration: sarva eva tu tasyeṣṭā ścatvārḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ| svaśarīrādvinirvṛttāścatvāra iva bāhavḥ||2.1.5||
meaning: Dasaratha, a bull among men, loved all his four sons equally just as the arms of his own body.

sanskrit: तेषामपि महातेजा रामो रतिकरःपितुः। स्वयम्भूरिव भूतानां बभूव गुणवत्तरः।।2.1.6।।
transliteration: teṣāmapi mahātejā rāmo ratikarḥpituḥ| svayambhūriva bhūtānāṃ babhūva guṇavattarḥ||2.1.6||
meaning: Even among them the brilliant Rama was a source of delight to his father like the Selfborn (Brahma) to all living beings.

sanskrit: स हि देवैरुदीर्णस्य रावणस्य वधार्थिभिः। अर्थितो मानुषे लोके जज्ञे विष्णुस्सनातनः।।2.1.7।।
transliteration: sa hi devairudīrṇasya rāvaṇasya vadhārthibhiḥ| arthito mānuṣe loke jajñe viṣṇussanātanḥ||2.1.7||
meaning: Entreated by the devatas desirous of slaying arrogant Ravana, the eternal Visnu was indeed born in the mortal world as Rama.

sanskrit: कथञ्चिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति। न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया।।2.1.11।।
transliteration: kathañcidupakāreṇa kṛtenaikena tuṣyati| na smaratyapakārāṇāṃ śatamapyātmavattayā||2.1.11||
meaning: Gifted with selfrestraint, Rama was pleased even with a single benefit done somehow to him, yet did not remember even a hundred offences committed by others.

sanskrit: शीलवृद्धैर्ज्ञानवृद्धैर्वयोवृद्धैश्च सज्जनैः। कथयन्नास्त वै नित्यमस्त्रयोग्यान्तरेष्वपि।।2.1.12।।
transliteration: śīlavṛddhairjñānavṛddhairvayovṛddhaiśca sajjanaiḥ| kathayannāsta vai nityamastrayogyāntareṣvapi||2.1.12||
meaning: Even during intervals of his practice of weapons he never failed to interact with saintly persons and with people advanced in age, virtue and wisdom.

sanskrit: निभृत स्संवृताकारो गुप्तमन्त्र स्सहायवान्। अमोघक्रोधहर्षश्च त्यागसंयमकालवित्।।2.1.23।।
transliteration: nibhṛta ssṃvṛtākāro guptamantra ssahāyavān| amoghakrodhaharṣaśca tyāgasṃyamakālavit||2.1.23||
meaning: He (Rama) was modest and did not reveal his inner feelings. He counselled in secrecy and had good friends. Never was his anger or pleasure in vain. He knew the occasion when to sacrifce and when to exercise restraint.

sanskrit: ﻿दृढभक्ति स्स्थिरप्रज्ञो नासद्ग्राही न दुर्वचाः। निस्तन्द्रिरप्रमत्तश्च स्वदोषपरदोषवित्।।2.1.24।।
transliteration: ﻿dṛḍhabhakti ssthiraprajño nāsadgrāhī na durvacāḥ| nistandrirapramattaśca svadoṣaparadoṣavit||2.1.24||
meaning: ﻿ He was firm in his devotion and steady in intellect. He accepted nothing ignoble nor used bad words. He was not swayed by emotions or prone to idleness. He knew his faults as well as of others.

sanskrit: शास्त्रज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च पुरुषान्तरकोविदः। यः प्रग्रहानुग्रहयोर्यथान्यायं विचक्षणः।।2.1.25।।
transliteration: śāstrajñaśca kṛtajñaśca puruṣāntarakovidḥ| yḥ pragrahānugrahayoryathānyāyṃ vicakṣaṇḥ||2.1.25||
meaning: He was versed in scriptures. He was grateful (to those who did him some good) and skilled in differentiating the comparative merits of men. Fair in his judgement he dispensed justice in accordance with law by reprimandin

sanskrit: सत्सङ्ग्रहप्रग्रहणे स्थानविन्निग्रहस्य च। आयकर्मण्युपायज्ञ स्सन्दृष्टव्ययकर्मवित्।।2.1.26।।
transliteration: satsaṅgrahapragrahaṇe sthānavinnigrahasya ca| āyakarmaṇyupāyajña ssandṛṣṭavyayakarmavit||2.1.26||
meaning: He was skilled in receiving and encouraging the righteous and in punishing (the wicked). He knew whom to punish. He knew the right means of raising revenue and also expending money in the prescribed manner.

sanskrit: श्रैष्ठ्यं शास्त्रसमूहेषु प्राप्तो व्यामिश्रकेषु च। अर्थधमौ च सङ्गृह्य सुखतन्त्रो न चालसः।।2.1.27।।
transliteration: śraiṣṭhyṃ śāstrasamūheṣu prāpto vyāmiśrakeṣu ca| arthadhamau ca saṅgṛhya sukhatantro na cālasḥ||2.1.27||
meaning: He obtained proficiency in scriptures and interconnected (mutually contradictory) branches of learning. Only after having grasped the (philosophy of) artha (statecraft) and dharma (righteousness), he sought pleasure. He

sanskrit: वैहारिकाणां शिल्पानां विज्ञाताऽऽर्थविभागवित्। आरोहे विनये चैव युक्तो वारणवाजिनाम्।।2.1.28।।
transliteration: vaihārikāṇāṃ śilpānāṃ vijñātā''rthavibhāgavit| ārohe vinaye caiva yukto vāraṇavājinām||2.1.28||
meaning: He had understanding of art and craft useful for entertainment. He knew proper ways of dispensing wealth. He was experienced in riding elephants and horses and in humbling them.

sanskrit: धनुर्वेदविदां श्रेष्ठो लोकेऽतिरथसम्मतः। अभियाता प्रहर्ता च सेनानयविशारदः।।2.1.29।।
transliteration: dhanurvedavidāṃ śreṣṭho loke'tirathasammatḥ| abhiyātā prahartā ca senānayaviśāradḥ||2.1.29||
meaning: He was the best among those skilled in archery in this world. He was reckoned as a great wielder of warchariots and one who strikes at the enemies by advancing towards them. He was an expert in commanding troops. (Atirat

sanskrit: अप्रधृष्यश्च सङ्ग्रामे क्रुध्दैरपि सुरासुरैः। अनसूयो जितक्रोधो न दृप्तो न च मत्सरी। न चावमन्ता भूतानां न च कालवशानुगः।।।
transliteration: apradhṛṣyaśca saṅgrāme krudhdairapi surāsuraiḥ| anasūyo jitakrodho na dṛpto na ca matsarī| na cāvamantā bhūtānāṃ na ca k
meaning: He was incapable of being repressed even by the enraged devatas or rakshasas in the battle. He was free from envy and had subdued his anger and pride. He was never malicious and he never slighted any living being nor did

sanskrit: एवं श्रेष्ठगुणैर्युक्तः प्रजानां पार्थिवात्मजः। सम्मतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु वसुधायाः क्षमागुणैः।।2.1.31।। बुद्ध्या बृहस्पतेस्तु
transliteration: evṃ śreṣṭhaguṇairyuktḥ prajānāṃ pārthivātmajḥ| sammatastriṣu lokeṣu vasudhāyāḥ kṣamāguṇaiḥ||2.1.31|| buddhyā bṛhaspatest
meaning: Thus endowed with such excellent qualities, the subjects in the three worlds held him in high esteem. In forbearance he was like the earth, in wisdom like Brihaspati and in prowess like the consort of Sachi (Indra).

sanskrit: तथा सर्वप्रजाकान्तैः प्रीतिसंजननैः पितुः।।2.1.32।। गुणैर्विरुरुचे रामो दीप्तस्सूर्य इवांशुभिः।
transliteration: tathā sarvaprajākāntaiḥ prītisṃjananaiḥ pituḥ||2.1.32|| guṇairviruruce rāmo dīptassūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ|
meaning: Rama whose virtues were cherished by all his subjects was a source of delight to his father and he shone like the rays of the resplendent Sun.

sanskrit: तमेवं व्रतसम्पन्नमप्रधृष्यपराक्रमम्।।2.1.33।। लोक पालोपमं नाथमकामयत मेदिनी।
transliteration: tamevṃ vratasampannamapradhṛṣyaparākramam||2.1.33|| loka pālopamṃ nāthamakāmayata medinī|
meaning: The earth desired him as her lord, for he was bestowed with such avowed virtues and with indomitable prowess equal to all the guardians of the quarters.

sanskrit: एतैस्तु बहुभिर्युक्तं गुणैरनुपमैस्सुतम्।।2.1.34।। दृष्ट्वा दशरथो राजा चक्रे चिन्तां परन्तपः।
transliteration: etaistu bahubhiryuktṃ guṇairanupamaissutam||2.1.34|| dṛṣṭvā daśaratho rājā cakre cintāṃ parantapḥ|
meaning: Observing his son endowed with such innumerable and incomparable virtues, king Dasaratha, subduer of enemies started thinking.

sanskrit: अथ राज्ञो बभूवैवं वृद्धस्य चिरजीविनः।।2.1.35।। प्रीतिरेषा कथं रामो राजा स्यान्मयि जीवति।
transliteration: atha rājño babhūvaivṃ vṛddhasya cirajīvinḥ||2.1.35|| prītireṣā kathṃ rāmo rājā syānmayi jīvati|
meaning: Thereafter, flashed in the mind of that aged king who had (already) lived long this pleasant thought as to how Rama will become king while he was alive.

sanskrit: एषा ह्यस्य परा प्रीतिर्हृदि संपरिवर्तते।।2.1.36।। कदा नाम सुतं द्रक्ष्याम्यभिषिक्तमहं प्रियम्।
transliteration: eṣā hyasya parā prītirhṛdi sṃparivartate||2.1.36|| kadā nāma sutṃ drakṣyāmyabhiṣiktamahṃ priyam|
meaning: The thought of seeing his dear son coronated repeatedly surfaced his mind so great was his affection (for Rama).

sanskrit: वृद्धिकामो हि लोकस्य सर्वभूतानुकम्पनः।।2.1.37।। मत्तः प्रियतरो लोके पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्।
transliteration: vṛddhikāmo hi lokasya sarvabhūtānukampanḥ||2.1.37|| mattḥ priyataro loke parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān|
meaning: (He said to himself) 'his (Rama's) only desire is to promote the prosperity of this world. He is one who shows compassion to all beings and is like the raingod dearer than me to the people of the world'.

sanskrit: यमशक्रसमो वीर्ये बृहस्पतिसमो मतौ।।2.1.38।। महीधरसमो धृत्यां मत्तश्च गुणवत्तरः।
transliteration: yamaśakrasamo vīrye bṛhaspatisamo matau||2.1.38|| mahīdharasamo dhṛtyāṃ mattaśca guṇavattarḥ|
meaning: 'In prowess he is equal to Yama and Indra,in wisdom to Brihaspati and in firmness to a mountain and in virtues greater than me'.

sanskrit: महीमहमिमां कृत्स्नामधितिष्ठन्तमात्मजम्।।2.1.39।। अनेन वयसा दृष्ट्वा यथास्वर्गमवाप्नुयाम्।
transliteration: mahīmahamimāṃ kṛtsnāmadhitiṣṭhantamātmajam||2.1.39|| anena vayasā dṛṣṭvā yathāsvargamavāpnuyām|
meaning: 'Seeing my son ruling this entire dominion of the earth, I will experience the bliss of attaining heaven at this age.'

sanskrit: इत्येतैर्विविधैस्तैस्तैरन्यपार्थिवदुर्लभैः।।2.1.40।। शिष्टैरपरिमेयैश्च लोके लोकोत्तरैर्गुणैः। तं समीक्ष्य महाराजो युक्तं
transliteration: ityetairvividhaistaistairanyapārthivadurlabhaiḥ||2.1.40|| śiṣṭairaparimeyaiśca loke lokottarairguṇaiḥ| tṃ samīkṣya mahār
meaning: King Dasaratha in consultation with his ministers observed that Rama is endowed with various virtues not found in other kings, immeasurable virtues which are praiseworthy, and exemplary. He is distinguished in this world

sanskrit: दिव्यन्तरिक्षे भूमौ च घोरमुत्पातजं भयम्।।2.1.42।। स़ञ्चचक्षेऽथ मेधावी शरीरे चात्मनो जराम्।
transliteration: divyantarikṣe bhūmau ca ghoramutpātajṃ bhayam||2.1.42|| sa़ñcacakṣe'tha medhāvī śarīre cātmano jarām|
meaning: The sagacious king, too perceived his body ageing and the portentous omens in the heaven, in the sky and on the earth causing dreadful concern.

sanskrit: पूर्णचन्द्राननस्याथ शोकापनुदमात्मनः।।2.1.43।। लोके रामस्य बुबुधे सम्प्रियत्वं महात्मनः।
transliteration: pūrṇacandrānanasyātha śokāpanudamātmanḥ||2.1.43|| loke rāmasya bubudhe sampriyatvṃ mahātmanḥ|
meaning: The king realised afterwards that his grief would be dispelled if noble Rama whose countenance resembled the full moon and who was a favourite of the people is crowned.

sanskrit: आत्मनश्च प्रजानां च श्रेयसे च प्रियेण च।।2.1.44।। प्राप्तकालेन धर्मात्मा भक्त्या त्वरितवान् नृपः।
transliteration: ātmanaśca prajānāṃ ca śreyase ca priyeṇa ca||2.1.44|| prāptakālena dharmātmā bhaktyā tvaritavān nṛpḥ|
meaning: Longing for it, the noble king realized that the time was ripe for the acceleration of the process of safeguarding his own and his subjects' welfare.

sanskrit: नानानगरवास्तव्यान्पृथग्जानपदानपि।।2.1.45।। समानिनाय मेदिन्याः प्रधानान्पृथिवीपतीन्।
transliteration: nānānagaravāstavyānpṛthagjānapadānapi||2.1.45|| samānināya medinyāḥ pradhānānpṛthivīpatīn|
meaning: He summoned individually kings and all important citizens residing in various cities and villages of this earth.

sanskrit: न तु केकयराजानं जनकं वा नराधिपः।।2.1.46।। त्वरया चानयामास पश्चात्तौ श्रोष्यतः प्रियम्।
transliteration: na tu kekayarājānṃ janakṃ vā narādhipḥ||2.1.46|| tvarayā cānayāmāsa paścāttau śroṣyatḥ priyam|
meaning: The king did not invite both the kings of Kekaya and Janaka in haste with an intention that they would hear the glad news at a later date.

sanskrit: तान्वेश्मनानाभरणैर्यथाऽर्हं प्रतिपूजितान्।।2.1.47।। ददर्शालङ्कृतो राजा प्रजापतिरिव प्रजाः।
transliteration: tānveśmanānābharaṇairyathā'rhṃ pratipūjitān||2.1.47|| dadarśālaṅkṛto rājā prajāpatiriva prajāḥ|
meaning: The king who received them in a befitting manner and provided them with residence and ornaments looked like lord Brahma adorned by the people.

sanskrit: अथोपविष्टे नृपतौ तस्मिन्परबलार्दने।।2.1.48।। ततः प्रविविशु श्शेषा राजानो लोकसम्मताः।
transliteration: athopaviṣṭe nṛpatau tasminparabalārdane||2.1.48|| tatḥ praviviśu śśeṣā rājāno lokasammatāḥ|
meaning: After the king (Dasaratha) who was a tormenter of enemy forces was seated, the rest of the kings beloved of their subjects entered (the assembly hall).

sanskrit: अथ राजवितीर्णेषु विविधेष्वासनेषु च।।2.1.49।। राजानमेवाभिमुखाः निषेदुर्नियता नृपाः।
transliteration: atha rājavitīrṇeṣu vividheṣvāsaneṣu ca||2.1.49|| rājānamevābhimukhāḥ niṣedurniyatā nṛpāḥ|
meaning: Then the kings (who entered the assembly) took the seats assigned to them facing the king (Dasaratha), following the royal tradition.

sanskrit: सलब्धमानैर्विनयान्वितैर्नृपैः पुरालयैर्जानपदैश्च मानदैः। उपोपविष्टैर्नृपतिर्वृतो बभौ सहस्रचक्षुर्भगवानिवामरैः।।2.1.50।।
transliteration: salabdhamānairvinayānvitairnṛpaiḥ purālayairjānapadaiśca mānadaiḥ| upopaviṣṭairnṛpatirvṛto babhau sahasracakṣurbhagavāni
meaning: Surrounded by those feudatory kings endowed with modesty, and received with due honour and by the respectful residents of cities and villages, the king (Dasaratha), resembled lord Indra, the thousand eyed encircled by th

sanskrit: शुकबर्हिणसङ्घुष्टं क्रौञ्चहंसरुतायुतम्।।2.10.12।। वादित्ररवसङ्घुष्टं कुब्जा वामनिकायुतम्। लतागृहैश्चित्रगृहैश्चम्पकाशोकश
transliteration: śukabarhiṇasaṅghuṣṭṃ krauñcahṃsarutāyutam||2.10.12|| vāditraravasaṅghuṣṭṃ kubjā vāmanikāyutam| latāgṛhaiścitragṛhaiścamp
meaning: The maharaja entered the inner apartment of Kaikeyi's prosperous abode filled with parrots and peacocks, reverberating with cries of kraunchas and swans and sounds of musical instruments attended with hunchbacks and dwar

sanskrit: स वृद्धस्तरुणीं भार्यां प्राणेभ्योपि गरीयसीम्।।2.10.23।। अपापः पापसङ्कल्पां ददर्श धरणीतले। लतामिव विनिष्कृत्तां पतितां द
transliteration: sa vṛddhastaruṇīṃ bhāryāṃ prāṇebhyopi garīyasīm||2.10.23|| apāpḥ pāpasaṅkalpāṃ dadarśa dharaṇītale| latāmiva viniṣkṛttāṃ
meaning: The guileless, old king beheld his youthful wife who was dearer to him than his own life, filled with deceitful intentions. She looked like a severed creeper, like a goddess fallen down, like a 'Kinnari' thrown down on e

sanskrit: करेणुमिव दिग्धेन विद्धां मृगयुना वने। महागज इवारण्ये स्नेहात्परिममर्श ताम्।।2.10.26।।
transliteration: kareṇumiva digdhena viddhāṃ mṛgayunā vane| mahāgaja ivāraṇye snehātparimamarśa tām||2.10.26||
meaning: Like a mighty sheelephant caressing her cow wounded with a poisoned arrow in the forest, he caressed her lovingly.

sanskrit: परिमृश्य च पाणिभ्यामभिसन्त्रस्तचेतनः। कामी कमलपत्राक्षीमुवाच वनितामिदम्।।2.10.27।।
transliteration: parimṛśya ca pāṇibhyāmabhisantrastacetanḥ| kāmī kamalapatrākṣīmuvāca vanitāmidam||2.10.27||
meaning: With a mind extremely terrified yet passionate, he caressed his lotuseyed wife with his hands, and said:

sanskrit: न तेऽहमभिजानामि क्रोधमात्मनि संश्रितम्। देवि केनाभिशप्ताऽसि केन वाऽसि विमानिता।।2.10.28।। यदिदं मम दुःखाय शेषे कल्याणि प
transliteration: na te'hamabhijānāmi krodhamātmani sṃśritam| devi kenābhiśaptā'si kena vā'si vimānitā||2.10.28|| yadidṃ mama duḥkhāya śeṣ
meaning: O auspicious queen, I do not know whether your anger is directed at me. I do not know the cause of your anger. By whom have you been offended or disrespected? Why are you lying in the dust? This is causing me great sorro

sanskrit: भूमौ शेषे किमर्थं त्वं मयि कल्याणचेतसि।।2.10.29।। भूतोपहतचित्तेव मम चित्तप्रमाथिनी।
transliteration: bhūmau śeṣe kimarthṃ tvṃ mayi kalyāṇacetasi||2.10.29|| bhūtopahatacitteva mama cittapramāthinī|
meaning: While I am here favourably disposed towards you, why are you lying down on the floor like one possessed by an evil spirit? Why are you afflicting my mind?

sanskrit: सन्ति मे कुशला वैद्यास्त्वभितुष्टाश्च सर्वशः।।2.10.30।। सुखितां त्वां करिष्यन्ति व्याधिमाचक्ष्व भामिनी।
transliteration: santi me kuśalā vaidyāstvabhituṣṭāśca sarvaśḥ||2.10.30|| sukhitāṃ tvāṃ kariṣyanti vyādhimācakṣva bhāminī|
meaning: O lovely one there are, to my best satisfaction, expert physicians in all branches (of medical science). They will restore your health. Tell me your ailment.

sanskrit: कस्य वा ते प्रियं कार्यं केन वा विप्रियं कृतम्।।2.10.31।। कः प्रियं लभतामद्य को वा सुमहदप्रियम्।
transliteration: kasya vā te priyṃ kāryṃ kena vā vipriyṃ kṛtam||2.10.31|| kḥ priyṃ labhatāmadya ko vā sumahadapriyam|
meaning: On whom do you wish to bestow favour? Who has caused you displeasure? To whom should I grant favour now? To whom should I cause great displeasure?

sanskrit: मा रोदीर्मा च कार्षीस्त्वं देवि संपरिशोषणम्।।2.10.32।। अवध्यो वध्यतां को वा को वा वध्यो विमुच्यताम्। दरिद्रः को भवत्वाढ्
transliteration: mā rodīrmā ca kārṣīstvṃ devi sṃpariśoṣaṇam||2.10.32|| avadhyo vadhyatāṃ ko vā ko vā vadhyo vimucyatām| daridrḥ ko bhavat
meaning: O queen shed no tears. Drain not your health. Ask me, and I shall slay one who should not be slain or release one who should be slain. I shall make a poor man rich and a wealthy man poor. (Tell me who are such people).

sanskrit: अहं चैव मदीयाश्च सर्वे तव वशानुगाः। न ते किञ्चिदभिप्रायं व्याहन्तुमहमुत्सहे।।2.10.34।।
transliteration: ahṃ caiva madīyāśca sarve tava vaśānugāḥ| na te kiñcidabhiprāyṃ vyāhantumahamutsahe||2.10.34||
meaning: My kins and I are under your control. I will make no effort to go even a little against your wishes.

sanskrit: आत्मनो जीवितेनापि ब्रूहि यन्मनसेच्छसि। बलमात्मनि जानन्ती न मां शङ्कितुमर्हसि।।2.10.35।। करिष्यामि तव प्रीतिं सुकृतेनापि
transliteration: ātmano jīvitenāpi brūhi yanmanasecchasi| balamātmani jānantī na māṃ śaṅkitumarhasi||2.10.35|| kariṣyāmi tava prītiṃ sukṛ
meaning: If you want to do anything even if it means sacrificing my life, I shall do it. Since you know my strength, it does not behove you to doubt me. I swear on my merits. I will do whatever pleases you.

sanskrit: यावदावर्तते चक्रं तावती मे वसुन्धरा।।2.10.36।। प्राचीनास्सिन्धुसौवीरा स्सौराष्ट्रा दक्षिणापथाः। वङ्गाङ्गमगधाः मत्स्याः स
transliteration: yāvadāvartate cakrṃ tāvatī me vasundharā||2.10.36|| prācīnāssindhusauvīrā ssaurāṣṭrā dakṣiṇāpathāḥ| vaṅgāṅgamagadhāḥ mat
meaning: My authority on the land is extended till such places the wheel of any chariot rotates such as the regions in the east, SindhuSauvira areas, Saurashtra, Southern regions, Banga, Anga, Magadha states, Matsya kingdom and K

sanskrit: तत्र जातं बहु द्रव्यं धनधान्यमजाविकम्। ततो वृणीष्व कैकेयि यद्यत्त्वं मनसेच्छसि।।2.10.38।।
transliteration: tatra jātṃ bahu dravyṃ dhanadhānyamajāvikam| tato vṛṇīṣva kaikeyi yadyattvṃ manasecchasi||2.10.38||
meaning: There wealth and foodgrains, sheep and goats and many things are produced. O Kaikeyi, ask whichever of these you wish.

sanskrit: किमायासेन ते भीरु उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ शोभने। तत्त्वं मे ब्रूहि कैकेयि यतस्ते भयमागतम्।।2.10.39।। तत्ते व्यपनयिष्यामि नीहारम
transliteration: kimāyāsena te bhīru uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha śobhane| tattvṃ me brūhi kaikeyi yataste bhayamāgatam||2.10.39|| tatte vyapanayiṣyām
meaning: O lady why do you exert yourself? Arise, arise. O charming Kaikeyi, tell me the cause of your fear. I will dispel it just as the Sun dispels morning mists.

sanskrit: तथोक्ता सा समाश्वस्ता वक्तुकामा तदप्रियम्।।2.10.40।। परिपीडयितुं भूयो भर्तारमुपचक्रमे।
transliteration: tathoktā sā samāśvastā vaktukāmā tadapriyam||2.10.40|| paripīḍayituṃ bhūyo bhartāramupacakrame|
meaning: Thus spoken to, she (Kaikeyi) breathed a sigh of relief. Intending to tell him the unpleasant thing (which was in her mind), she began tormenting her husband all the more. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयो

sanskrit: कथंचिदभिविज्ञाय विवर्णवदनं कृशम्। भ्रातरं भरतं रामः परिजग्राह बाहुना।।2.100.2।।
transliteration: kathṃcidabhivijñāya vivarṇavadanṃ kṛśam| bhrātarṃ bharatṃ rāmḥ parijagrāha bāhunā||2.100.2||
meaning: Rama found it extremely difficult to recognise Bharata with his emaciated body and pallid face. He held him in his arms and lifted him.

sanskrit: आघ्राय रामस्तं मूर्ध्नि परिष्वज्य च राघवः। अङ्के भरतमारोप्य पर्यपृच्छत्समाहितः।।2.100.3।।
transliteration: āghrāya rāmastṃ mūrdhni pariṣvajya ca rāghavḥ| aṅke bharatamāropya paryapṛcchatsamāhitḥ||2.100.3||
meaning: Born in the race of Raghu, Rama embraced Bharata and kissed him on his forehead. Placing him on his lap, he enquired thus with a composed mind:

sanskrit: क्व नु तेऽभूत्पिता तात यदरण्यं त्वमागतः। न हि त्वं जीवतस्तस्य वनमागन्तुमर्हसि।।2.100.4।।
transliteration: kva nu te'bhūtpitā tāta yadaraṇyṃ tvamāgatḥ| na hi tvṃ jīvatastasya vanamāgantumarhasi||2.100.4||
meaning: O dear, now that you have come to the forest, where is our father king Dasaratha? You ought not come to the forest while he is living.

sanskrit: चिरस्य बत पश्यामि दूराद्भरतमागतम्। दुष्प्रतीकमरण्येऽस्मिन् किं तात वनमागतः।।2.100.5।।
transliteration: cirasya bata paśyāmi dūrādbharatamāgatam| duṣpratīkamaraṇye'smin kiṃ tāta vanamāgatḥ||2.100.5||
meaning: You have come a long distance (from Ayodhya) to this forest, O Bharata It is a pity, dear brother, to see you after a long time, so emaciated. What brings you to the forest?

sanskrit: कच्चिद्धारयते तात राजा यत्त्वमिहाऽगतः। कच्चिन्न दीन स्सहसा राजा लोकान्तरं गतः।।2.100.6।।
transliteration: kacciddhārayate tāta rājā yattvamihā'gatḥ| kaccinna dīna ssahasā rājā lokāntarṃ gatḥ||2.100.6||
meaning: My dear (brother), now that you have come here, I trust, king Dasaratha is keeping good health and hope, he has not departed prematurely in despondency for the other world.

sanskrit: कच्चित्सौम्य न ते राज्यं भ्रष्टं बालस्य शाश्वतम्। कच्चिच्छुश्रूषसे तात पितरं सत्यविक्रमम्।।2.100.7।।
transliteration: kaccitsaumya na te rājyṃ bhraṣṭṃ bālasya śāśvatam| kaccicchuśrūṣase tāta pitarṃ satyavikramam||2.100.7||
meaning: O gentle one, being young and inexperienced, I trust, you have not forfeited the kingdom for ever. Dear child, I trust, you are looking after father whose prowess is his truthfulness.

sanskrit: कच्चिद्धशरथो राजा कुशली सत्यसंङ्गरः। राजसूयाश्वमेधानामाहर्ता धर्मनिश्चयः।।2.100.8।।
transliteration: kacciddhaśaratho rājā kuśalī satyasṃṅgarḥ| rājasūyāśvamedhānāmāhartā dharmaniścayḥ||2.100.8||
meaning: I trust king Dasaratha, who is true to his promise, a performer of Rajasuya and Ashwamedha sacrifices and a firm adherent of righteousness is in good health.

sanskrit: स कच्चिद्ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् धर्मनित्यो महाद्युतिः। इक्ष्वाकूणामुपाध्यायो यथावत्तात पूज्यते।।2.100.9।।
transliteration: sa kaccidbrāhmaṇo vidvān dharmanityo mahādyutiḥ| ikṣvākūṇāmupādhyāyo yathāvattāta pūjyate||2.100.9||
meaning: O dear child I trust, the family preceptor of the Ikshvakus, Vasistha, the brahmin (versed in the Vedas), who is learned, ever fixed in virtues and effulgent is being honoured as usual.

sanskrit: सा तात कच्चित्कौसल्या सुमित्रा च प्रजावती। सुखिनी कच्चिदार्या च देवी नन्दति कैकयी।।2.100.10।।
transliteration: sā tāta kaccitkausalyā sumitrā ca prajāvatī| sukhinī kaccidāryā ca devī nandati kaikayī||2.100.10||
meaning: Dear child I trust, Kausalya and Sumitra, mothers of an excellent progeny are happy. I trust, the noble queen Kaikeyi is happy too.

sanskrit: कच्चिद्विनयसम्पन्नः कुलपुत्रो बहुश्रुतः। अनसूयुरनुद्रष्टा सत्कृतस्ते पुरोहितः।।2.100.11।।
transliteration: kaccidvinayasampannḥ kulaputro bahuśrutḥ| anasūyuranudraṣṭā satkṛtaste purohitḥ||2.100.11||
meaning: I trust, you continue to honour the family priest (Suyajna, son of Vasistha) who is endowed with modesty, born of high family, conversant in scriptures, free from envy and who can give you directions with regard to your

sanskrit: कच्चिदग्निषु ते युक्तो विधिज्ञो मतिमानृजुः। हुतं च होष्यमाणं च काले वेदयते सदा।।2.100.12।।
transliteration: kaccidagniṣu te yukto vidhijño matimānṛjuḥ| hutṃ ca hoṣyamāṇṃ ca kāle vedayate sadā||2.100.12||
meaning: I trust, the sagacious priest who knows ritual precepts, who is upright and is employed to take care of your sacred fires, informs you always regarding what was offered and what is to be offered as oblation at appropriat

sanskrit: कच्चिद्देवान्पित्रून् मातृ़र्गुरून्पितृसमानपि। वृद्धांश्च तात वैद्यांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चाभिमन्यसे।।2.100.13।।
transliteration: kacciddevānpitrūn mātṛ़rgurūnpitṛsamānapi| vṛddhāṃśca tāta vaidyāṃśca brāhmaṇāṃścābhimanyase||2.100.13||
meaning: Dear brother, I trust you continue to pay homage to gods, father, mothers, teachers, relations equal to your father, aged people, physicians and brahmins.

sanskrit: इष्वस्त्रवरसम्पन्नमर्थशास्त्र विशारदम्। सुधन्वानमुपाध्यायं कच्चित्त्वं तात मन्यसे।।2.100.14।।
transliteration: iṣvastravarasampannamarthaśāstra viśāradam| sudhanvānamupādhyāyṃ kaccittvṃ tāta manyase||2.100.14||
meaning: I hope you treat with respect Sudhanva who is equipped with the most formidable arrows and other weapons propelled by mantras and a master in the science of statecraft.

sanskrit: कच्चिदात्मसमा श्शूरा श्श्रुतवन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः। कुलीनाश्चेङ्गितज्ञाश्च कृतास्ते तात मन्त्रिणः।।2.100.15।।
transliteration: kaccidātmasamā śśūrā śśrutavanto jitendriyāḥ| kulīnāśceṅgitajñāśca kṛtāste tāta mantriṇḥ||2.100.15||
meaning: I hope, dear brother, you have appointed men who are brave, learned, selfcontrolled, of noble birth and skilled in guessing from hints.

sanskrit: मन्त्रो विजयमूलं हि राज्ञां भवति राघव। सुसंवृतो मन्त्रधरैरमात्यै श्शास्त्रकोविदैः।।2.100.16।।
transliteration: mantro vijayamūlṃ hi rājñāṃ bhavati rāghava| susṃvṛto mantradharairamātyai śśāstrakovidaiḥ||2.100.16||
meaning: O Bharata the wellguarded advice of ministers, learned in scriptures and capable of proper counselling, is the root of victory for kings, specially when the advice is kept in confidence.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषीः कच्चित् कालेऽवबुध्यसे। कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तियस्यर्थनैपुणम्।।2.100.17।।
transliteration: kaccinnidrāvaśṃ naiṣīḥ kaccit kāle'vabudhyase| kacciccāpararātreṣu cintiyasyarthanaipuṇam||2.100.17||
meaning: I trust you are not under the grip of sleep but wake up at appropriate times, I hope you always think of the means of judicious statecraft during the last part of the night.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिस्सह। कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति।।2.100.18।।
transliteration: kaccinmantrayase naikḥ kaccinna bahubhissaha| kaccitte mantrito mantro rāṣṭrṃ na paridhāvati||2.100.18||
meaning: I hope you neither decide alone nor discuss with many. I trust a decision once made by you is not leaked in the kingdom.

sanskrit: कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम्। क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव।।2.100.19।।
transliteration: kaccidarthṃ viniścitya laghumūlṃ mahodayam| kṣipramārabhase kartuṃ na dīrghayasi rāghava||2.100.19||
meaning: O Bharata, having determined on an endeavour involving a little effort and yielding great results, I trust you commence to execute it quickly without procrastination?

sanskrit: कच्चित्तु सुकृतान्येव कृतरूपाणि वा पुनः। विदुस्ते सर्वकार्याणि न कर्तव्यानि पार्थिवाः।।2.100.20।।
transliteration: kaccittu sukṛtānyeva kṛtarūpāṇi vā punḥ| viduste sarvakāryāṇi na kartavyāni pārthivāḥ||2.100.20||
meaning: I trust, other kings come to know of your endeavours only when your endeavours suceed or about to succeed. I hope, efforts intended to be made in future are not revealed to them beforehand.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्नतर्कैर्युक्त्या वा ये चाप्यपरिकीर्तिताः। त्वया वा तवामात्यैर्बुध्यते तात मन्त्रितम्।।2.100.21।।
transliteration: kaccinnatarkairyuktyā vā ye cāpyaparikīrtitāḥ| tvayā vā tavāmātyairbudhyate tāta mantritam||2.100.21||
meaning: Dear brother, I hope others are not able to understand your determination or those of your ministers, either by conjecture or by inference or through other means without being revealed either by you or by your ministers.

sanskrit: कच्चित्सहस्रान्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्। पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्यान्निश्रेयसं महत्।।2.100.22।।
transliteration: kaccitsahasrānmūrkhāṇāmekamicchasi paṇḍitam| paṇḍito hyarthakṛcchreṣu kuryānniśreyasṃ mahat||2.100.22||
meaning: I hope by setting aside a thousand fools, you prefer a single wise man. A wise man will be of immense help in difficult situations.

sanskrit: सहस्राण्यपि मूर्खाणां युद्युपास्ते महीपतिः। अथवाप्ययुतान्येव नास्ति तेषु सहायता।।2.100.23।।
transliteration: sahasrāṇyapi mūrkhāṇāṃ yudyupāste mahīpatiḥ| athavāpyayutānyeva nāsti teṣu sahāyatā||2.100.23||
meaning: Even if the king seeks the assistance from thousands or tens of thousands of fools, they cannot render any help to him.

sanskrit: एकोऽप्यमात्यो मेधावी शूरो दक्षो विचक्षणः। राजानं राजपुत्रं वा प्रापयेन्महतीं श्रियम्।।2.100.24।।
transliteration: eko'pyamātyo medhāvī śūro dakṣo vicakṣaṇḥ| rājānṃ rājaputrṃ vā prāpayenmahatīṃ śriyam||2.100.24||
meaning: A single clearsighted minister who is prudent, brave and skilful can bring about great prosperity to a king or a prince.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्मुख्या महात्स्वेव मध्यमेषु च मध्यमाः। जघन्याश्च जघन्येषु भृत्याः कर्मसु योजिताः।।2.100.25।।
transliteration: kaccinmukhyā mahātsveva madhyameṣu ca madhyamāḥ| jaghanyāśca jaghanyeṣu bhṛtyāḥ karmasu yojitāḥ||2.100.25||
meaning: I hope you have employed highly competent servants for important tasks, mediocre servants in mediocre tasks and low people in inferior tasks.

sanskrit: अमात्यानुपधातीतान्पितृपैतामहाञ्छुचीन्। श्रेष्ठांछ्रेष्ठेषुकच्चित्वं नियोजयसि कर्मसु।।2.100.26।।
transliteration: amātyānupadhātītānpitṛpaitāmahāñchucīn| śreṣṭhāṃchreṣṭheṣukaccitvṃ niyojayasi karmasu||2.100.26||
meaning: I hope you are assigning ministers, who are unyielding to bribery and other temptations, holding positions hereditarily and who are full of integrity and eminence, with superior tasks.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोग्रेण दण्डेन भृशमुद्वेजितप्रजम्। राष्ट्रं तवानुजानन्ति मन्त्रिणः कैकयीसुत।।2.100.27।।
transliteration: kaccinnogreṇa daṇḍena bhṛśamudvejitaprajam| rāṣṭrṃ tavānujānanti mantriṇḥ kaikayīsuta||2.100.27||
meaning: Are not the citizens of your kingdom agitated at severe punishment meted out to them reproaching your ministers?

sanskrit: कच्चित्त्वां नावजानन्ति याजकाः पतितं यथा। उग्रप्रतिग्रहीतारं कामयानमिव स्त्रियः।।2.100.28।।
transliteration: kaccittvāṃ nāvajānanti yājakāḥ patitṃ yathā| ugrapratigrahītārṃ kāmayānamiva striyḥ||2.100.28||
meaning: Just like a performer of sacrifice scorns at an outcaste or a woman scorns at a lustful lover, do the subjects not scorn you for collecting taxes more than what is due?

sanskrit: उपायकुशलं वैद्यं भृत्यसंदूषणे रतम्। शूरमैश्वर्यकामं च यो न हन्ति स हन्यते।।2.100.29।।
transliteration: upāyakuśalṃ vaidyṃ bhṛtyasṃdūṣaṇe ratam| śūramaiśvaryakāmṃ ca yo na hanti sa hanyate||2.100.29||
meaning: A learned person but skilled in contrivances, a warrior with passion for wealth and a man ever engaged in corrupting the minds of servants must be slain. A king who does not kill them is himself killed in due course.

sanskrit: कच्चिद्धृष्टश्च शूरश्च मतिमान् धृतिमान् शुचिः। कुलीनश्चानुरक्तश्च दक्षस्सेनापतिः कृतः।।2.100.30।।
transliteration: kacciddhṛṣṭaśca śūraśca matimān dhṛtimān śuciḥ| kulīnaścānuraktaśca dakṣassenāpatiḥ kṛtḥ||2.100.30||
meaning: I trust you have appointed a man who is cheerful, brave, sagacious, steadfast, honest, of a good family, loyal and efficient as the army chief.

sanskrit: बलवन्तश्च कच्चित्ते मुख्या युध्दविशारदाः। दृष्टापदाना विक्रान्तास्त्वया सत्कृत्यमानिताः।।2.100.31।।
transliteration: balavantaśca kaccitte mukhyā yudhdaviśāradāḥ| dṛṣṭāpadānā vikrāntāstvayā satkṛtyamānitāḥ||2.100.31||
meaning: I trust you honour and respect those prominent soldiers who are courageous, powerful, skilled in war and who have proven heroic exploits.

sanskrit: कच्चिद्बलस्य भक्तं च वेतनं च यथोचितम्। सम्प्राप्तकालं दातव्यं ददासि न विलम्बसे।।2.100.32।।
transliteration: kaccidbalasya bhaktṃ ca vetanṃ ca yathocitam| samprāptakālṃ dātavyṃ dadāsi na vilambase||2.100.32||
meaning: I trust you distribute rations and wages to your army in due time without making delay.

sanskrit: कालातिक्रमणाच्चैव भक्तवेतनयोर्भृताः। भर्तुः कुप्यन्ति दुष्यन्ति सोऽनर्थ स्सुमहान् स्मृतः।।2.100.33।।
transliteration: kālātikramaṇāccaiva bhaktavetanayorbhṛtāḥ| bhartuḥ kupyanti duṣyanti so'nartha ssumahān smṛtḥ||2.100.33||
meaning: It has been mentioned in the scriptures that if provisions and wages are not paid in stipulated time, the dependent attendants will be incensed with their masters and will turn hostile and become corrupt, leading to grea

sanskrit: कच्चित्सर्वेऽनुरक्तास्त्वां कुलपुत्राः प्रधानतः। कच्चित्प्राणां स्तवार्थेषु सन्त्यजन्ति समाहिताः।।2.100.34।।
transliteration: kaccitsarve'nuraktāstvāṃ kulaputrāḥ pradhānatḥ| kaccitprāṇāṃ stavārtheṣu santyajanti samāhitāḥ||2.100.34||
meaning: I hope all men of a good family, especially those who belong to our race, are loyal to you and are ready to sacrifice their lives for your cause.

sanskrit: कच्चिज्जानपदो विद्वान्दक्षिणः प्रतिभानवान्। यथोक्तवादी दूतस्ते कृतो भरत पण्डितः।।2.100.35।।
transliteration: kaccijjānapado vidvāndakṣiṇḥ pratibhānavān| yathoktavādī dūtaste kṛto bharata paṇḍitḥ||2.100.35||
meaning: O Bharata, I hope you have chosen as your envoy an expert born in your own country, wellinformed, skilful and quick to understand one who repeats and reports (exactly) what has been told.

sanskrit: कच्चिदष्टादशान्येषु स्वपक्षे दश पञ्च च। त्रिभिस्त्रिभिरविज्ञातैर्वेत्सि तीर्थानि चारकैः।।2.100.36।।
transliteration: kaccidaṣṭādaśānyeṣu svapakṣe daśa pañca ca| tribhistribhiravijñātairvetsi tīrthāni cārakaiḥ||2.100.36||
meaning: I hope you collect information (of their secret efforts) intelligently through unrecognisable spies with three of them closely watching each of the eighteen officials (there are eighteen categories of officials in a king

sanskrit: कच्चिद्व्यपास्तानहितान्प्रतियातांश्च सर्वदा। दुर्बलाननवज्ञाय वर्तसे रिपुसूदन।।2.100.37।।
transliteration: kaccidvyapāstānahitānpratiyātāṃśca sarvadā| durbalānanavajñāya vartase ripusūdana||2.100.37||
meaning: O slayer of foes, I hope you are always alert about your foes who were defeated by you and have come back. You should not ignore your enemies thinking they are weak.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्न लौकायतिकान्ब्राह्मणांस्तात सेवसे।। अनर्थकुशला ह्येते बालाः पण्डितमानिनः।।2.100.38।।
transliteration: kaccinna laukāyatikānbrāhmaṇāṃstāta sevase|| anarthakuśalā hyete bālāḥ paṇḍitamāninḥ||2.100.38||
meaning: Dear brother, I hope you do not serve those brahmins who are atheists, who foolishly think of this world alone and fancy themselves as learned. They only bring disasters.

sanskrit: धर्मशास्त्रेषु मुख्येषु विद्यमानेषु दुर्बुधाः। बुद्धिमान्वीक्षिकीं प्राप्य निरर्थं प्रवदन्ति ते।।2.100.39।।
transliteration: dharmaśāstreṣu mukhyeṣu vidyamāneṣu durbudhāḥ| buddhimānvīkṣikīṃ prāpya nirarthṃ pravadanti te||2.100.39||
meaning: While principal scriptures do exist, these superficial fellows take resort to the science of logic based on abstract reasoning, and indulge in futile talks.

sanskrit: वीरैरध्युषितां पूर्वमस्माकं तात पूर्वकैः। सत्यनामां दृढ द्वारां हस्त्यश्वरथसङ्कुलाम्।।2.100.40।। ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्व
transliteration: vīrairadhyuṣitāṃ pūrvamasmākṃ tāta pūrvakaiḥ| satyanāmāṃ dṛḍha dvārāṃ hastyaśvarathasaṅkulām||2.100.40|| brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣat
meaning: My dear brother I trust you are protecting the (impregnable) city of Ayodhya worthy of its name, formerly defended by our heroic ancestors, with its sturdy gates, its elephants, horses and chariots, its thousands of vene

sanskrit: कच्चिच्चैत्यशतैर्जुष्ट स्सुनिविष्टजनाकुलः। देवस्थानैः प्रपाभिश्च तटाकैश्चोपशोभितः।।2.100.43।। प्रहृष्टनरनारीकस्समाजोत्सव
transliteration: kacciccaityaśatairjuṣṭa ssuniviṣṭajanākulḥ| devasthānaiḥ prapābhiśca taṭākaiścopaśobhitḥ||2.100.43|| prahṛṣṭanaranārīkas
meaning: O Bharata, my country which is marked with hundreds of sanctuaries near villages where life of the people is made comfortable, where there are shrines, water distribution facilities and tanks, which is wellploughed and r

sanskrit: कच्चित्ते दयितास्सर्वे कृषिगोरक्षजीविनः। वार्तायां संश्रितस्तात लोको हि सुखमेधते।।2.100.47।।
transliteration: kaccitte dayitāssarve kṛṣigorakṣajīvinḥ| vārtāyāṃ sṃśritastāta loko hi sukhamedhate||2.100.47||
meaning: I trust all those men who live on agriculture and cattlerearing are favourable to you. The world's prosperity, dear brother, grows on the profession of cattle rearing.

sanskrit: तेषां गुप्तिपरीहारैः कच्चित्ते भरणं कृतम्। रक्ष्या हि राज्ञा धर्मेण सर्वे विषयवासिनः।।2.100.48।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ guptiparīhāraiḥ kaccitte bharaṇṃ kṛtam| rakṣyā hi rājñā dharmeṇa sarve viṣayavāsinḥ||2.100.48||
meaning: I trust you nourish them and also afford portection and prevent adversities. A king must protect all those people living in his country in accordanc with righteousness.

sanskrit: कच्चिस्त्रिय स्सान्त्वयसि कच्चित्ताश्च सुरक्षिताः। कच्चिन्न श्रद्धास्यासां कच्चिद्गुह्यं न भाषसे।।2.100.49।।
transliteration: kaccistriya ssāntvayasi kaccittāśca surakṣitāḥ| kaccinna śraddhāsyāsāṃ kaccidguhyṃ na bhāṣase||2.100.49||
meaning: I trust, you keep the women pacified and wellprotected, you do not believe their words and do not divulge any secrets to them.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्नागवनं गुप्तं कच्चित्ते सन्ति धेनुकाः। कच्चिन्न गणिकाश्वानां कुञ्जराणां च तृप्यसि।।2.100.50।।
transliteration: kaccinnāgavanṃ guptṃ kaccitte santi dhenukāḥ| kaccinna gaṇikāśvānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ ca tṛpyasi||2.100.50||
meaning: I trust, you protect the habitat of elephants and you have a large number of milch cows. I trust you are not contented with the existing number of female and male elephants and horses.

sanskrit: कच्चिद्दर्शयसे नित्यं मनुष्याणां विभूषितम्। उत्थायोत्थाय पूर्वाह्णे राजपुत्र महापथे।।2.100.51।।
transliteration: kacciddarśayase nityṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vibhūṣitam| utthāyotthāya pūrvāhṇe rājaputra mahāpathe||2.100.51||
meaning: O prince, I trust, you rise early daily and present yourself welladomed to the people on the thoroughfare.

sanskrit: कच्चिन्न सर्वे कर्मान्ताः प्रत्यक्षास्तेऽविशङ्कया। सर्वे वा पुनरुत्सृष्टा मध्यमेवात्र कारणम्।।2.100.52।।
transliteration: kaccinna sarve karmāntāḥ pratyakṣāste'viśaṅkayā| sarve vā punarutsṛṣṭā madhyamevātra kāraṇam||2.100.52||
meaning: All the servants, I trust, do not present themselves to you directly. At the same time they do not remain out of sight with fear at a distance. The middle course is the best way for the welfare of every one.

sanskrit: कच्चित्सर्वाणि दुर्गाणि धनधान्यायुधोदकैः। यन्त्रैश्च परिपूर्णानि तथा शिल्पिधनुर्धरैः।।2.100.53।।
transliteration: kaccitsarvāṇi durgāṇi dhanadhānyāyudhodakaiḥ| yantraiśca paripūrṇāni tathā śilpidhanurdharaiḥ||2.100.53||
meaning: Hope all the forts are adequately provided with wealth, foodgrains, weapons and water, with machines of war and craftsmen and archers.

sanskrit: आयस्ते विपुलः कच्चित्कच्चिदल्पतरो व्ययः। अपात्रेषु न ते कच्चित्कोशो गच्छति राघव।।2.100.54।।
transliteration: āyaste vipulḥ kaccitkaccidalpataro vyayḥ| apātreṣu na te kaccitkośo gacchati rāghava||2.100.54||
meaning: O Bharata, I trust, your revenues are abundant and expenditure much less. I trust you do not give away your treasure to undeserving persons.

sanskrit: देवतार्थे च पित्रर्थेब्राह्मणाभ्यागतेषु च। योधेषु मित्रवर्गेषु कच्चिद्गच्छति ते व्ययः।।2.100.55।।
transliteration: devatārthe ca pitrarthebrāhmaṇābhyāgateṣu ca| yodheṣu mitravargeṣu kaccidgacchati te vyayḥ||2.100.55||
meaning: I trust, you are spending only on gods, ancestors, brahmins, guests, warriors and hosts of friends.

sanskrit: कच्चिदार्यो विशुद्धात्मा क्षारित श्चापरकर्मणा। अपृष्ट श्शास्त्रकुशलैर्न लोभाद्वध्यते शुचिः।।2.100.56।।
transliteration: kaccidāryo viśuddhātmā kṣārita ścāparakarmaṇā| apṛṣṭa śśāstrakuśalairna lobhādvadhyate śuciḥ||2.100.56||
meaning: I trust a man who is honest, purehearted and venerable, falsely accused of adultery is not slain out of avarice without consulting experts in scriptures.

sanskrit: गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्टस्सकारणः। कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ।।2.100.57।।
transliteration: gṛhītaścaiva pṛṣṭaśca kāle dṛṣṭassakāraṇḥ| kaccinna mucyate coro dhanalobhānnararṣabha||2.100.57||
meaning: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

sanskrit: व्यसने कच्चिदाढ्यस्य दुर्गतस्य च राघव। अर्थं विरागाः पश्यन्ति तवामात्या बहुश्रुताः।।2.100.58।।
transliteration: vyasane kaccidāḍhyasya durgatasya ca rāghava| arthṃ virāgāḥ paśyanti tavāmātyā bahuśrutāḥ||2.100.58||
meaning: O Bharata, I trust that your ministers are wellinformed and look into all matters in times of hardship pertaining to whether a man is rich or poor without any bias to either.

sanskrit: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव। तानि पुत्रान्पशून्घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः।।2.100.59।।
transliteration: yāni mithyābhiśastānāṃ patantyaśrūṇi rāghava| tāni putrānpaśūnghnanti prītyarthamanuśāsatḥ||2.100.59||
